title.rendered: 25 Cute Christmas Apple Watch Faces for The Holidays

content.rendered:
Looking to add some festive cheer to your Apple Watch this holiday season? Christmas-themed wallpapers are an easy way to bring that spirit right to your wrist. In this guide, you’ll find the best Christmas Apple Watch faces in full resolution and learn how to apply them in just a few steps. So, let’s get started!

Table of Contents
  • Aesthetic Christmas Apple Watch Faces in High-Res Downloads
    • 1. Cute Penguin
    • 2. Grinchy Christmas Decoration
    • 3. Peekaboo Santa
    • 4. Santa's Gift Run
    • 5. Adorable Christmas Elf
    • 6. Merry Christmas
    • 7. Decorated Christmas Tree
    • 8. Christmas-Themed
    • 9. Snowflake Tiled Xmas
    • 10. Santa Claus
    • 11. Christmas Snowman
    • 12. Christmas in The Air
    • 13. Most Popular Christmas Watch Face
    • 14. Abstract Holiday Watch Face
    • 15. Rudolph Merry Christmas
    • 16. Christmas Wreath
    • 17. Christmas Presents
    • 18. Glowing Christmas Tree
    • 19. Red Christmas Bells
    • 20. Christmas Stickers
    • 21. Winter Theme Merry Christmas
    • 22. Christmas Themed Apple Logo
    • 23. Charming Christmas Tree
    • 24. Hello Santa Merry Christmas
    • 25. Christmas Decoration
  • How to Apply a Watch Face to Your Apple Watch

Aesthetic Christmas Apple Watch Faces in High-Res Downloads

You can download a watch face by clicking the download button below each wallpaper.

1. Cute Penguin

Bring holiday happiness to your wrist with this adorable penguin watch face. Wrapped in a cozy red scarf and Santa hat, it adds a warm, festive touch.

 

Download

2. Grinchy Christmas Decoration 

This Grinch-themed watch face features festive ornaments, wreaths, and stockings. Overall, it brings a fun mix of Christmas cheer and a cheeky attitude to your wrist.

Download

3. Peekaboo Santa 

A cute Santa peeking over a bold red backdrop gives a fun surprise every time you check the time on your watch. Perfect for anyone who loves the joyful, whimsical side of Christmas.

Download

4. Santa’s Gift Run 

Keep up festive energy with this lively watch face featuring Santa carrying a giant sack of presents. The falling snow will definitely remind you of winter nights.

Download

5. Adorable Christmas Elf 

With big, warm eyes, a festive red outfit, and a soft, snowy glow, this tiny helper brightens your wrist. Download this if you love cute, cozy Christmas vibes.

Download

6. Merry Christmas

Start your holiday season with a beautiful Merry Christmas watch face. Every time you raise your wrist, you will be dazzled by the vibrant colors and festive vibes.

Download

7. Decorated Christmas Tree

Here’s a Christmas star for the star within you. Decorated with sparkling ornaments and glistening lights, it is the perfect companion for your wearable. Tap the download button to save this for free.

Download

8. Christmas-Themed

Christmas is incomplete without the classic “Ho-Ho-Ho!”. Deck your Apple Watch with this dark Christmas wallpaper and charm your way into parties.

Download

9. Snowflake Tiled Xmas

If you are a minimalist like me, you will love this snowflake watch face. It’s a perfect way to indulge in winter vibes and set the festive mood. You might also love our collection of cozy winter iPhone wallpapers.

Download

10. Santa Claus

Let the joy of Christmas spread throughout your heart as you welcome our jolly old Santa with his iconic beard. Press the download button to keep Santa’s joyful spirit with you wherever you go.

Download

11. Christmas Snowman

Frosty the Snowman comes to life on your Apple Watch with this delightful Christmas Snowman Watch face. With an adorable charm, this watch face brings the magic of this festival.

Download

12. Christmas in The Air

Feel the magic of Christmas in the air with this enchanting watch face. Tap on the download button to capture a glimpse of Santa and his reindeer spreading joy on your Apple Watch.

Download

13. Most Popular Christmas Watch Face

This watch face is not only a timekeeper but also a statement piece for the holiday season. It reminds us of the family gatherings and joy we celebrate throughout Christmas.

Download

14. Abstract Holiday Watch Face

Get into the holiday spirit and kick off the New Year in style with this abstract Christmas Apple Watch face. The sparkling golden snowflakes that create a Christmas tree symbolize the excitement of festivals.

Download

15. Rudolph Merry Christmas

Add a touch of whimsy to your day with the HD wallpaper of Rudolph on your Apple Watch. Tap the download button and let him accompany you this Christmas.

Download

16. Christmas Wreath

Uplift the elegance of your wrist with this beautifully designed Christmas wreath on a dark background. Get this timeless symbol of warmth and welcome to make your screen pop.

Download

17. Christmas Presents

Unwrap the joy of this beautiful season with this well-curated Apple Watch face. The beautifully wrapped gift will keep reminding you of the grand celebration.

Download

18. Glowing Christmas Tree

Lit from within, this watch face captures the radiance of a festive tree in full glow. Keep the magic of Christmas alive every time you check the time.

Download

19. Red Christmas Bells

Add a touch of musical celebration to your wrist by tapping the download button below. It is a symphony of holiday cheer, bringing the festive spirit to life.

Download

20. Christmas Stickers

From Santa hats to reindeer, these animated stickers will add a playful touch to your wrist companion. Customize your Apple Watch with something different and eye-catching.

Download

21. Winter Theme Merry Christmas

Snow-covered landscapes, delicate icicles, and a palette of cool blues would look fabulous on your wrist. Don’t let this moment slip away, and save this winter wonder.

Download

22. Christmas Themed Apple Logo

Show your Apple love with a festive twist. Download this unique combination of the iconic Apple logo with holiday cheer, creating a stylish statement for tech enthusiasts.

Download

23. Charming Christmas Tree

The charm of the Christmas tree is just a tap away. Let this beautifully decorated tree take center stage on your wrist, reminding you of the timeless tradition.

Download

24. Hello Santa Merry Christmas

Check the time for Santa’s cheerful smile with this HD Apple Watch face. With a simple tap on the download button, you can add an extra dose of joy to your day.

Download

25. Christmas Decoration

This stunning display of holiday elegance captures every detail in high definition, from glittering trifles to festive ribbons. Not just a watch face but a masterpiece of Christmas decor.

Download

How to Apply a Watch Face to Your Apple Watch

Once you have downloaded your favorite watch face to your iPhone, follow the steps below to deck it:

  1. Launch the Apple Watch app on your iPhone. 
  2. At the bottom of the app, tap on Face Gallery. 
  3. Scroll down and select the Photos watch face style. 
  4. Tap Choose Photos, select the saved image, and tap the checkmark to confirm. 
  5. Now, customize the watch face by changing the time size and color, the numerals, and adding watch complications. 
  6. Finally, tap Add, and it will instantly sync to your Apple Watch.

You can set up to 25 photos together so that every time you lift your wrist, you will see a fresh, festive watch face in action! 

Also read: How to Share Your Apple Watch Faces 

Cheers to the Season of Wonders!

As the holiday lights twinkle and the air fills with carols, uplift your festive spirit with some of the best Christmas watch faces for Apple Watch. Whether you’re counting down to Christmas, tracking holiday parties, or simply enjoying the season, these watch faces are your merry companions.

Thank you for reading. Please take a moment to share your favorite faces with the rest of the class in the comments below.

acceptedAnswer.text: System Data storage on Mac consists of different files, such as cached data, DMG files, application support files, old downloads, and more. If you haven't deleted them, System Data storage on Mac will be high. You can delete those files to free up storage on your Mac.

acceptedAnswer.text: The files and folders in the System Data storage consist of junk or temporary files on your Mac. Though it will not cause any issues with the Mac, it's best to exercise caution so you don't delete important files you may need later.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

mainEntity.name: Why is “Request Desktop Site” greyed out?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually means the browser is still loading the page, or the site blocks desktop rendering. Try refreshing the page or switching to another browser.

mainEntity.name: Does desktop mode use more data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Desktop sites load larger images, scripts, and more content overall. It may also take longer to load on slower networks. However, this may not be the case with every website.

mainEntity.name: Does desktop mode work with all websites?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some websites detect your device type and may still force the mobile version, even in desktop mode.

mainEntity.name: Will desktop mode affect site functionality?

acceptedAnswer.text: It might. Some interactive elements may not behave correctly on a touchscreen, especially if the site wasn’t designed with mobile compatibility in mind.

title.rendered: 2025 Apple Holiday Gift Guide: Buying Advice for Every Product

content.rendered:
The festive season brings amazing deals and discounts on Amazon and the official Apple Store website, making it the perfect time to grab some tech goodies. Whether you’re looking to impress loved ones with high-quality gifts or spoil yourself with cutting-edge tech, this comprehensive Apple holiday gift guide is for everyone.

Holiday return policies: Remember to factor in return windows when buying gifts this holiday season. Apple, Amazon, and other major retailers offer extended holiday return periods so that you can buy stuff risk-free. As a guide, we found the following information:

  • Apple: Products received between November 12, 2025, and December 25, 2025, may be returned through January 8, 2026.
  • Amazon: Apple products purchased between November 1 and December 31, 2025, can be returned through January 15, 2026. Most other items purchased between this time frame can usually be returned by January 31, 2026.

Exceptions may apply, so please check the return window when making your purchases! 

Table of Contents
  • Apple’s Black Friday Shopping Event
  • iPhone: The Gift That Never Misses
  • Apple iPad: Versatile Tablets for Every Kind of Gift Recipient
    • iPad 11th Gen
    • iPad Pro (M5)

    • iPad mini (A17 Pro chip)
  • MacBook: The Perfect Gift for Work, Creativity & Everyday Life
    • MacBook Air
    • MacBook Pro
  • AirPods: The Perfect Apple Gift for Anyone
    • AirPods 4
    • AirPods Pro 3
    • AirPods Max
  • Apple Watch: Your 2025 Smartwatch Gift Picks
    • Apple Watch Ultra 3
    • Apple Watch SE 3
    • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Final Thoughts: The Perfect Apple Gift Awaits

Apple’s Black Friday Shopping Event

Apple has officially announced its annual Black Friday shopping event, running from November 28, 2025. There aren’t any actual discounts available, but you can grab some gift card incentives with your shopping as described below:

  • iPhone: Receive up to a $75 Apple Gift Card with purchases of iPhone 15, iPhone 14, or iPhone SE.
  • Mac: Get up to a $200 Apple Gift Card when you buy a 15-inch MacBook Air (M3), a 13-inch MacBook Air (M3), or a 13-inch MacBook Air (M2).
  • iPad: Enjoy up to a $100 Apple Gift Card with the purchase of an iPad Pro, iPad Air, or 10th-generation iPad.
  • Apple Watch: Earn a $50 Apple Gift Card when you buy an Apple Watch SE.
  • AirPods: Score up to a $75 Apple Gift Card with AirPods Max, AirPods Pro 2, or AirPods (4th generation).
  • TV & Home: Get a $50 Apple Gift Card with Apple TV 4K or HomePod purchases.
  • Beats: Receive up to a $50 Apple Gift Card with select Beats products, including Beats Studio Pro, Beats Solo 4 Wireless, Beats Fit Pro, Beats Studio Buds +, Beats Pill, or Beats Flex.
  • Accessories: Collect a $25 Apple Gift Card when you buy select accessories, like the Magic Keyboard, Apple Pencil (2nd generation), or Smart Folio cases for iPads.

If you want direct discounts, there are some awesome deals available on third-party retailers like Amazon. Check out our complete guide on Apple Black Friday deals to find the products you don’t want to miss.

With that said, below we’ve listed some of the best Apple gifts for him and her to buy this Christmas.

iPhone: The Gift That Never Misses

If there’s one Apple product that consistently delivers “wow,” it’s the iPhone. Apple polished performance, photography, and battery life across the board this year, making the iPhone a perfect, no-brainer holiday gift. 

In 2025, the iPhone 17 and iPhone Air lineup will have something for everyone. However, you won’t find discounts on the latest models on Amazon. Only carriers like AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile, etc. have some trade-in and plan-bundle offers.  

Explore these must-have iPhone accessories:

  • Best iPhone 17 Accessories You Must Have
  • Make the Most of Your iPhone Air with These Accessories

On the other hand, the Amazon Renewed store has the iPhone 16 series at a good price.

  • iPhone 16:  $597.68 
  • iPhone 16 Plus: $634.00 
  • iPhone 16 Pro: $794.97 
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max: $864.97

You can also buy a refurbished iPhone 15 series even at a lower price. If you’re still confused, check out the iPhone buying guide to decide which iPhone is right for you.

Apple iPad: Versatile Tablets for Every Kind of Gift Recipient

An iPad is a versatile gift that can serve as a productivity tool, a creativity studio, a reader, or a video-watching device, depending on the user’s needs.

iPad 11th Gen

Powered by the A16 chip, this base-model iPad offers smooth performance for everyday tasks. It’s a solid choice for kids, students, or anyone upgrading from an older tablet, particularly if heavy editing or pro-apps aren’t needed.

  • iPad A16 Wi-Fi: $349 $279 (20% off) 
  • iPad A16 Wi-Fi + Cellular: $499 $429 (14% off)

iPad Pro (M5)

The M5 chip delivers next-level performance for demanding workflows, including AI generation, video editing, digital art, music production, and heavy multitasking. So, the new iPad Pro is ideal for power users looking for a laptop replacement or creative canvas.

  • 13-inch iPad Pro M5: $1,299 $1,199 (8% off) 
  • 11-inch iPad Pro M5: $999 $899 (10% off)

iPad Air M3

If you want to experience the “pro” features without the premium price tag, get the iPad Air. It has a great display, a powerful M3 chip, and is lightweight.

  • 13-inch iPad Air M3: $799 $649 (19% off) 
  • 11-inch iPad Air M3: $599 $449 (25% off)

Also check out: Best accessories for your new M3 iPad Air

iPad mini (A17 Pro chip)

The iPad mini hits the sweet spot for portability and daily life performance with Apple Intelligence. Great for someone who wants a tablet but doesn’t need a large screen.

  • iPad mini (Wi-Fi): $499 $399 (20% off)
  • iPad mini (Wi-Fi + Cellular): $649 $549 (15% off)

With so many options available, if you can’t decide on one, get our expert advice on which iPad to buy in 2025.

MacBook: The Perfect Gift for Work, Creativity & Everyday Life

If you’re putting together a 2025 holiday gift guide for Apple gear, the MacBook remains one of the most compelling gifts.

MacBook Air

The MacBook Air remains Apple’s most universally loved laptop. With the latest M4 chip, 18 hours of battery life, and a super-thin design, it’s ideal for everyday work, students, travel, writing, light editing, and general productivity.

  • 13-inch MacBook Air M4: $999 $749 (25% off) 
  • 15-Inch MacBook Air M4: $1,199 $949 (21% off)

Also read: Which MacBook Air to Get: 15-inch vs 13-inch?

MacBook Pro

Built for pros who need serious performance. With an advanced M5 chip, better thermals, up to 24 hours of battery life, and new Continuity features, the new MacBook Pro handles heavy workloads like video editing, coding, design, data, and AI apps with ease.

  • 14-inch M5 MacBook Pro: $1,599 $1,442 (10% off) 
  • 14-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro: $1,999 $1,748 (13% off) 
  • 16-inch M4 Pro MacBook Pro: $2,499 $2,189 (12% off)

Check out MacBook Pro accessories:

  • Best 14-Inch MacBook Pro Cases You Should Have 
  • Best Sleeves for the 14-inch MacBook Pro

AirPods: The Perfect Apple Gift for Anyone

When it comes to Apple gifts, AirPods remain the no-brainer crowd-pleaser. Whether you’re shopping for a casual listener, a productivity-focused professional, or an audiophile, Apple’s 2025 AirPods lineup has a perfect match.  

AirPods 4

Apple’s entry-level AirPods with a lightweight ergonomic design, Live Translation, and improved sound quality thanks to the H2 chip.

  • AirPods 4: $129 $69 (47%) 
  • AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation: $179 $99 (44%)

AirPods Pro 3

If you want a gift guaranteed to impress, AirPods Pro 3 is the star. It’s Apple’s smartest and most immersive earbuds yet, with Spatial Audio, heart rate sensing, Hearing Aid mode, and much more.

  • AirPods Pro 3: $249 $219.99 (12% off)

Read more:

  • Best AirPods Pro 3 Cases Available Right Now 
  • Apple AirPods Pro 3 vs Pro 2: Big Upgrade or Hype?

AirPods Max

AirPods Max remain the most indulgent headphones in Apple’s lineup. Even in 2025, they stand out for both high-fidelity sound quality and comfortable design.

  • AirPods Max: $549 $399.99 (27% off)

Apple Watch: Your 2025 Smartwatch Gift Picks 

The Apple Watch lineup includes three models: Apple Watch Ultra 3 for adventurers, athletes & outdoor lovers; Apple Watch SE 3 with great value; and Apple Watch Series 11 as the balanced all-rounder. 

Apple Watch Ultra 3

The Apple Watch Ultra 3 has a titanium build, a 49mm large sapphire display, 42 hours of battery life, 5G support, and Satellite communication. Thus, it’s a great gift for hikers, travelers, athletes, and outdoor adventurers.

  • Apple Watch Ultra 3: $779.99 
  • Apple Watch Ultra 2: $799 $599 (25% off)

Make the most out of it with:

  • Best Accessories for Apple Watch Ultra 3, Ultra 2, and Ultra 
  • Best Cases for Apple Watch Ultra 3, Ultra 2, and Ultra 
  • Best Screen Protectors for Apple Watch Ultra 3, Ultra 2, and Ultra

Apple Watch SE 3

If you want to give someone their first Apple smartwatch, this one is ideal. Powered by the same S10 chip as the flagship models, you get smooth performance and solid fitness and wellness features on a budget.

  • SE 3 [GPS 40 mm]: $249 $199 (20% off) 
  • SE 3 [GPS + Cellular 40mm]: $299 $249 (17% off) 
  • SE 3 [GPS 44 mm]: $279 $229 (18% off) 
  • SE 3 [GPS + Cellular 44 mm]: $329 $279 (15% off)

Apple Watch Series 11

Hits a sweet spot between features and price; it has better build and more features than SE, but not as rugged or premium as Ultra. With the hypertension alert and sleep score, Apple Watch Series 11 is a perfect gift for fitness enthusiasts and everyday smartwatch users.

  • Series 11 [Aluminum GPS 42mm]: $399 $339 (15% off) 
  • Series 11 [Aluminum GPS + Cellular 42mm]: $499 $439 (12% off) 
  • Series 11 [Titanium GPS + Cellular 42mm]: $749 $689 (8% off)

You can also get the 46mm variant in every configuration at a good discount.

Final Thoughts: The Perfect Apple Gift Awaits 

Whether you’re shopping for a tech-savvy friend, a family member who loves staying connected, or someone who simply appreciates beautifully designed gadgets, Apple’s 2025 lineup has something for everyone.  

Holiday gifting doesn’t have to be complicated, especially when you’re choosing from a lineup that’s already universally loved. Pick based on the person, not the price tag, and you’ll end up with a gift that feels personal, useful, and guaranteed to spark a smile. 

From the everyday convenience of AirPods and Apple Watch to more premium options like iPhone 17 Pro Max or MacBook, each product brings thoughtful design, powerful features, and that unmistakable Apple ease of use.

acceptedAnswer.text: System Data storage on Mac consists of different files, such as cached data, DMG files, application support files, old downloads, and more. If you haven't deleted them, System Data storage on Mac will be high. You can delete those files to free up storage on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to delete System Data files on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: The files and folders in the System Data storage consist of junk or temporary files on your Mac. Though it will not cause any issues with the Mac, it's best to exercise caution so you don't delete important files you may need later.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

mainEntity.name: Why is “Request Desktop Site” greyed out?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually means the browser is still loading the page, or the site blocks desktop rendering. Try refreshing the page or switching to another browser.

mainEntity.name: Does desktop mode use more data?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Desktop sites load larger images, scripts, and more content overall. It may also take longer to load on slower networks. However, this may not be the case with every website.

mainEntity.name: Does desktop mode work with all websites?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Some websites detect your device type and may still force the mobile version, even in desktop mode.

mainEntity.name: Will desktop mode affect site functionality?

acceptedAnswer.text: It might. Some interactive elements may not behave correctly on a touchscreen, especially if the site wasn’t designed with mobile compatibility in mind.

title.rendered: View Weather Maps on iPhone: Quick Tips to See Radar and Forecasts

content.rendered:
Apple has designed the iPhone Weather app to give you a clear view of weather conditions around you, not just a basic forecast. The app offers weather maps that show live radar, temperature patterns, air quality levels, and wind speed and patterns across nearby regions. With these visuals, you can track storms, monitor changing conditions, and plan your day with more confidence.

Read on to learn everything you need to know about Weather Maps on iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What You Can Do With Weather Maps on iPhone
  • How to View Weather Maps in the Apple Weather App
  • Understand Weather Map Layers
    • 1. Precipitation Layer
    • 2. Temperature Layer
    • 3. Air Quality Layer
    • 4. Wind Layer
  • Best Third-Party Weather Apps for Detailed Weather Maps
  • Tips for Getting the Most Accurate Weather Map Data

What You Can Do With Weather Maps on iPhone

Simply put, weather maps offer an interactive, easy-to-understand view of weather conditions across your region. You can view the following map types:

  • Precipitation radar for rain and snow
  • Temperature maps showing warm and cool zones
  • Air Quality maps displaying AQI levels
  • Wind patterns shown as overlays in select regions

These maps update in real time, so you can stay up to date on the storm movement, rainfall intensity, and temperature changes in your region. This makes the weather maps handy for travel planning, preparing for bad weather, or checking pollution before outdoor activities.

How to View Weather Maps in the Apple Weather App

If you’re already accustomed to using the Weather app on your iPhone, viewing and understanding weather maps is quick and straightforward. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Weather app and tap the Map icon in the bottom left corner.
  2. Depending on your region, the Weather app shows one of the available maps. In our region, the default one is the Air Quality map.
  3. To view a different weather map, tap the Overlay icon at the top left and select from the available options:
    • Precipitation
    • Temperature
    • Wind
  4. Pinch to zoom or swipe on the map to explore the weather conditions across your region.
  5. If you are seeing the Precipitation map, a slider at the bottom shows past and predicted rainfall or snowfall for the next 1 or 12 hours.

Understand Weather Map Layers

Weather maps in the Apple Weather app are built using different layers. Each layer highlights a specific type of weather information, allowing you to switch views based on what you want to track. Therefore, a proper understanding of each layer is essential to make better decisions when planning your day.

1. Precipitation Layer

This layer shows real-time rainfall and snowfall using animated radar. Once you switch to the Precipitation layer, you’ll see different colors that indicate intensity, from light blue for light rain to darker shades for heavy rain or snow. The animation moves across the map so you can see how quickly a storm is approaching or passing. The timeline slider lets you switch between 1-hour and 12-hour timelines.

  • The 1-hour timeline lets you check the past hour and the next hour of expected movement.
  • The 12-hour timeline shows the expected movement over the next 12 hours.

2. Temperature Layer

Switching to the Temperature layer displays a gradient heat map. Warm areas appear in shades of red or orange, while cooler regions show in blue or purple.

3. Air Quality Layer

This layer displays AQI levels across your region. Colors range from green for good air quality to yellow for moderate air quality, and maroon for hazardous air quality.

4. Wind Layer

The layer shows you wind movement and wind speed with animated flow lines or arrows across your region. Wind speed units are typically in kilometers per hour or miles per hour, depending on your device settings. Denser flow lines or longer arrows represent stronger winds, and thinner flow lines or shorter arrows represent light winds.

Best Third-Party Weather Apps for Detailed Weather Maps

While the weather map feature in the Apple Weather app does its job pretty well, you can also explore some powerful third-party alternatives if you want advanced radar layers, hyperlocal tracking, storm prediction, or detailed wind maps. Here are some of the best third-party weather apps for iPhone:

  • Carrot Weather
  • AccuWeather
  • Yahoo Weather
  • RadarScope
  • Windy
  • Weather Underground
  • Clime NOAA Weather Radar

Tips for Getting the Most Accurate Weather Map Data

A few small settings and habits can help you make the most of the weather maps and the entire Weather app in general:

  • Enable Precise Location for accurate local conditions
  • Use a stable Wi-Fi or mobile network for live radar
  • Add multiple cities to compare the weather easily
  • Keep your iPhone updated to access all available map layers
  • Turn on severe weather alerts for early warnings
  • Refresh the Weather app if maps look outdated

Weather Made Clear

Weather maps on iPhone bring weather information to life in a simple, visual way. Whether you are checking how fast rain is moving, comparing temperatures across cities, or keeping an eye on air quality, the map layers give you a clearer picture than a standard forecast. They make the Weather app more practical for everyday decisions and give you a quick, reliable way to stay ahead of changing conditions.

Have you tried using weather maps on your iPhone? Share your experience or questions in the comments below.

FAQs

Does the iPhone Weather app show live radar?

Yes. The precipitation map uses real-time radar to display rain and snow movement.

How accurate are the weather maps on iPhone?

They use trusted weather data sources and update frequently. Accuracy depends on location and a strong internet connection.

Why is the temperature map missing in the Weather app?

This may happen due to outdated iOS software or temporary data issues. Update your iPhone and reopen the Weather app to fix it.

Read more:

  • How to Fix Weather App Not Working on iPhone or iPad
  • Got a New iPhone? Try These 22 Tips to Use It Like a Pro
  • iPhone Battery Draining After iOS 26? Try These Easy Fixes

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

title.rendered: Apple Challenges India’s Antitrust Penalty Law Over $38 Billion Fine

content.rendered:
Apple is taking legal action against a new Indian antitrust law, filing a petition with the Delhi High Court. This disputed legislation could embroil Apple in fines reaching a staggering $38 billion. The legal maneuver comes amid ongoing antitrust tensions with Match Group, the parent company of Tinder, reports Reuters.

India Uses Global Revenue to Calculate Fines

Under a law enacted in 2023, the Competition Commission of India (CCI) can now calculate antitrust penalties based on a company’s worldwide turnover instead of just its local revenue. This means Apple could face fines as high as 10 percent of its entire global revenue, approximately $38 billion. Apple has criticized this method, labeling it as “manifestly arbitrary” and arguing it is both unconstitutional and unjust. The tech giant contends that fines should reflect only the revenue of the implicated entity within India.

Apple vs. Match Group: Background of the Case

The scrutiny on Apple began in 2022 when complaints from Match Group and several Indian startups accused Apple of mandating the use of its in-app purchase system. The CCI previously termed this requirement as abusive conduct in draft findings. However, the investigation has been in limbo following the withdrawal of these draft reports due to leaked confidential information, leaving the case unresolved for now. Apple maintains its innocence, pointing to its relatively modest 9 percent market share in India, contrasted by Android’s dominance, as a mitigating factor.

Apple Preemptively Challenges Law to Avoid Retrospective Use

Apple has highlighted a concern that this new penalty law has already been applied in a separate case dated November 10 involving historical violations. Worried that this precedent might be retroactively applied to their situation, Apple says it had no choice but to bring this constitutional challenge now. Meanwhile, Match Group supports using global revenue figures in fine calculations, arguing it is essential to deter repeat violations. The court is set to hear Apple’s petition on December 3.

Do you believe this could affect future cases? Share your thoughts below.

mainEntity.name: Why is my System Data storage so high on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: System Data storage on Mac consists of different files, such as cached data, DMG files, application support files, old downloads, and more. If you haven't deleted them, System Data storage on Mac will be high. You can delete those files to free up storage on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to delete System Data files on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: The files and folders in the System Data storage consist of junk or temporary files on your Mac. Though it will not cause any issues with the Mac, it's best to exercise caution so you don't delete important files you may need later.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

title.rendered: Master Apple Calendar on Mac: 15 Simple Tips and Tricks

content.rendered:
The Calendar app on your Mac is one of those tools you use every day without realizing how helpful it can actually be. While most people rely on it to check dates or add a quick reminder, it’s capable of much more. With the right tips, you can effortlessly organize your work, birthdays, meetings, holidays, and day-to-day routines.

In this post, we’ve curated 15 essential tips that make using Apple Calendar on your Mac simpler, faster, and more helpful in your daily life.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Share a Calendar
  • 2. Merge Calendars
  • 3. Add an International Holiday Calendar
  • 4. Subscribe to a Calendar
  • 5. Enable Siri Suggestions
  • 6. Use Travel Time Notifications
  • 7. Automatically Open a File or Receive an Email Before an Event
  • 8. Turn ON Time Zone Support
  • 9. Change Week Start Day
  • 10. Adjust Scroll in Week View
  • 11. Show Events in Year View
  • 12. Create Quick Event
  • 13. Propose a New Time for an Event
  • 14. Search for an Event
  • 15. Schedule a Video Call

1. Share a Calendar

If you want to collaborate on events or let your family know what’s on your schedule, you can share an iCloud calendar. When you choose those you want to share with, you can set their permissions as well. So, they can either edit the calendar or simply view it.

  1. Launch the Calendar app on your Mac → Click the calendar icon in the top left.
  2. Select a desired title (Calendar) in the sidebar → Then click the Contact icon that appears or pick Edit → Share Calendar in the menu bar.
  3. Enter your contact in the Share With field of the pop-out window.

  4. Click the person’s name in the same spot to open the drop-down menu and choose the permissions from View Only or View & Edit.

  5. The person you share with will receive a notification that you want to share the calendar. When they accept, you’ll see a green check mark next to their name in the sharing pop-up window.

To stop sharing a calendar, open the calendar and select Edit → Stop Sharing in the menu bar. Then, confirm in the pop-up window. Alternatively, delete the contact in the sharing menu where you added them.

If you prefer to share with a large group, like on your website or blog, check the Public Calendar box in the sharing pop-up menu, then click Done. You’ll then see the URL for the calendar with a share option.

2. Merge Calendars

Because it’s so easy to create a new calendar, you may end up with more than one that is similar to each other. You can merge calendars to turn two iCloud calendars into one. 

  1. Select the calendar and choose Edit → Merge Calendar in the menu bar.
    Alternatively, you can right-click the calendar and pick Merge.

  2. Pick the calendar you want to merge with in the pop-out menu.
  3. You’ll see a message letting you know that all events from the second calendar will merge into the first. To continue, select Merge.
    • Alternatively, select Cancel to quit or Export to save a copy of the calendar to your Mac instead.

3. Add an International Holiday Calendar

To keep up with national holidays, you can add a holiday calendar to the Calendar app on Mac.

But, did you know you can add a holiday calendar from other parts of the world, too? This is handy if you work with others from around the globe.

  1. Select File → New Holiday Calendar in the menu bar.

  2. Choose the region for the calendar → Click Add.

  3. In the subsequent pop-up window, you can adjust a few settings for the new calendar. You can pick a name, color, and location as well as adjust alerts and auto-refresh. Click OK to save the settings.

You should then see your new calendar in the app’s sidebar.

4. Subscribe to a Calendar

Along with adding a holiday calendar, you can subscribe to a calendar like one for your child’s school or favorite sports team.

To begin, you’ll need the URL for the calendar, so grab that first and then follow these steps.

  1. From the menu bar, select File → New Calendar Subscription.

  2. Enter or paste the URL for the calendar that you obtained and click Subscribe.

  3. In the subsequent pop-up window, add the calendar name, pick a color, and optionally adjust the other calendar settings. Click OK when you finish.

You’ll then see your calendar in the sidebar. To make changes or unsubscribe, use Edit in the menu bar or right-click the calendar in the sidebar.

5. Enable Siri Suggestions

When dates appear in places like emails or messages, you can have Siri suggest these events in your calendar. This is a convenient way to add events without extra effort.

  1. To enable Siri Suggestions, open System Settings.
  2. Select Siri & Spotlight on the left → Click Siri Suggestions & Privacy on the right.

  3. In the next window, select Calendar → then toggle on Show Siri Suggestions in application.
  4. Click Done and then close the System Settings.

When you return to the Calendar app, you’ll see the Siri Suggestions option in the Other section of the sidebar. By checking the box, you’ll see the suggested events appear in your calendar.

6. Use Travel Time Notifications

You probably already know you can use Calendar notifications to receive alerts before events begin. But if you have to travel to your event, you can receive a notification based on the time it’ll take you to get there. 

  1. Create your event as you normally would and include the Location.

  2. In the event detail section, click Travel Time and pick an option in the drop-down box. You can choose the driving or walking time or pick a time ahead of when you should leave.

You’ll then receive your calendar alert based on your travel time, which is especially handy for lengthy trips to events.

7. Automatically Open a File or Receive an Email Before an Event 

If you want to refer to a file in your meeting or receive an email with the meeting’s date and time before an event begins, you can use these as Calendar alerts. You can choose a file and have it open, or an email account and get a message at the time you pick.

  1. Create your event like normal and open the detail section.
  2. Select Alert and pick Custom at the bottom.

  3. Use the drop-down box to choose Open File or Email.

  4. Select the file or email account, set the timing, and click OK to save it.

When the alert time arrives before your event, you’ll see the file open or receive the email.

8. Turn ON Time Zone Support

When planning events with others in different time zones, you may need to account for time differences. With Time Zone Support turned on in Calendar, you can set and view events in the time zone of your choice.

  1. Open Calendar. In the menu bar, select Calendar → Settings.

  2. Go to the Advanced tab and check the box for Time Zone Support.

You’ll then see a time zone drop-down box on the top right of your Calendar window. Use it to see all Calendar events in that time zone. 

You also have a time zone drop-down in the event window that you can use when scheduling an event.

9. Change Week Start Day

We all know that a week officially begins on Sunday. But if you want your calendar to show weeks starting on a different day, like Monday, for the workweek, you can change this in a few clicks.

  1. Open Calendar. In the menu bar, select Calendar → Settings.
  2. Go to the General tab and choose the day in the Start week on drop-down box.

You’ll then see your calendar update to begin weeks on that day.

10. Adjust Scroll in Week View

When you use the Week view in Calendar, you can use the arrows on the top right to move to the next or previous week. If you find that you are moving by day instead of by week and it’s tedious, you can change it.

  1. Open Calendar. In the menu bar, select Calendar → Settings.
  2. Go to the General tab and open the Scroll in week view by the drop-down box. You can pick Day, Week, or Week, Stop on Today.

Once you make the change, return to your calendar and use the buttons to move forward or back to test your new setting.

11. Show Events in Year View

Another simple but useful setting you may want to adjust in Calendar is the Year view. While this gives you an overview of the year’s dates, you may want to highlight those with events planned.

  1. Open Calendar. Select Calendar → Settings in the menu bar.
  2. Go to the Advanced tab and check the box for Show events in year view.

  3. Return to your calendar and select Year at the top.

You should see dates with events highlighted.

12. Create Quick Event

To schedule an event in the Calendar app, you simply select the date or the date and time. But you can also create what’s called a Quick Event using natural language. For example, you can type “Dinner at 8pm Saturday” or “Dentist appointment tomorrow morning at 9.”

  1. With Calendar open, click the plus sign on the top left.
  2. In the Create Quick Event pop-up box, enter your event and hit Return.

You’ll then see the event display on your calendar as instructed.

You can schedule all-day events the same way by inserting “all day” into your phrase. For instance, you can type “Our anniversary is all day Friday.”

13. Propose a New Time for an Event

If you’ve been invited to an event and need to reschedule, you can propose a new time to the event organizer in two ways in Calendar on Mac.

  1. Drag event to a new date and/or time
    • First, you can select the event and drag it to the new date and/or time you want to propose. 

    • You’ll receive a pop-up message asking if you’d like to suggest the new time. Select Propose to continue.

    • Second, you can open the event and select Propose a New Time. You’ll then see dates and times when all invitees can attend or just some attendees. 

  2. Select the Propose a New Time option
    • Select the option you want to use, which places the new date and/or time in the event window. Click Propose to request the update from the event organizer.

14. Search for an Event

Have you ever needed to find an event in the past? Maybe you couldn’t recall when it was, but you wanted to see who attended, open its attachment, or read the notes. You can search for an event in the Calendar app just like you can search for an image in Photos on Mac.

  1. Enter a keyword in the Search field on the top right of the Calendar app.
  2. You’ll then see some filters you can use, such as the word in the event title, location, or notes. You can pick one of these to narrow down your results, or click away to see all results, which display along the right.
  3. Choose the event you want, and you’ll head to it on the calendar.
    You can also open it to get the information from it that you need.

15. Schedule a Video Call

Video calls are super popular these days, with so many people working remotely. Luckily, you don’t need Google Meet or Zoom if your participants use FaceTime. 

  1. Create your event as you normally would and select the Camera icon to make it a FaceTime call. You can then send the invite as well as copy or share the link with others.

  2. When the time comes, simply click Join next to FaceTime on the Calendar invitation.

For more details on this feature or to use it on iPhone or iPad too, check out our how-to for scheduling FaceTime calls.

Stay Organized Every Day

And that’s it. Using these tips can make the Calendar app feel more helpful and easier to use in your day-to-day routine. Small changes like adding an international holiday calendar or enabling Siri Suggestions can save time and keep your schedule steady. Once you get used to these tricks, planning on your Mac becomes smoother and more organized.

If you have your own Apple Calendar tips or questions, feel free to share them in the comments.

FAQs

How do I customize my Apple Calendar on my Mac?

To change the view of your calendars, open the Calendar app and pick Calendar → Settings in the menu bar. Then, use the various tabs to adjust your calendar options. If you’re not sure how to customize a setting or what it means, click the Help icon (question mark) in the lower right corner.

How do I color code events in my Apple Calendar Mac?

If you want to change a calendar’s color, right-click it in the sidebar and choose the color or add a Custom Color. For more information or to learn how to do this on your mobile device, look at our guide for changing your calendar color.

acceptedAnswer.text: System Data storage on Mac consists of different files, such as cached data, DMG files, application support files, old downloads, and more. If you haven't deleted them, System Data storage on Mac will be high. You can delete those files to free up storage on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to delete System Data files on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: The files and folders in the System Data storage consist of junk or temporary files on your Mac. Though it will not cause any issues with the Mac, it's best to exercise caution so you don't delete important files you may need later.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

title.rendered: iMessage Not Activating on iPhone? Here’s How to Fix It Fast

content.rendered:
iMessage is one of the most convenient ways to stay connected on your iPhone, so running into an activation error can be frustrating. The good thing is that this problem is usually caused by minor issues such as network settings, time configuration, or temporary glitches. With the right steps, you can get iMessage working again in just a few minutes.

This guide walks you through quick and effective fixes to resolve the iMessage activation error so you can start sending messages without interruption. These solutions also help if FaceTime refuses to activate on your device.

Table of Contents
  • Different iMessage Activation Errors You Might See on iPhone
  • Why Does My iMessage Say Waiting for Activation?
  • Quick Ways to Fix the iMessage Waiting for Activation Error on iPhone
    • 1. Check if You Can Send Text Messages
    • 2. Make Sure Your iPhone Has an Active Internet Connection
    • 3. Set the Correct Date and Time
    • 4. Turn Airplane Mode On and Off
    • 5. Restart Your iPhone
    • 6. Check Apple’s Server Status
    • 7. Turn iMessage Off and On Again
    • 8. Sign Out of Apple ID and Sign In Again
    • 9. Update Carrier Settings and Check Carrier Issues
    • 10. Update iOS
    • 11. Reset Network Settings

Different iMessage Activation Errors You Might See on iPhone

According to Apple, you may see one of the following errors when iMessage fails to activate:

  • Waiting for activation.
  • Activation unsuccessful.
  • An error occurred during activation.
  • Could not sign in, please check your network connection.
  • Unable to contact the iMessage server. Try again.

Before getting into the fixes, it helps to understand why these issues show up.

Why Does My iMessage Say Waiting for Activation?

Most of the time, this happens because of something very small that is easy to correct. These are the most common reasons:

  • You may not be connected to working cellular data or Wi-Fi.
  • Your iPhone settings fail to send an SMS.
  • Something is broken on your carrier’s end, preventing text message delivery.
  • You do not have enough balance to send the iMessage activation text.
  • Your date and time settings are incorrect.
  • There is a temporary problem with Apple’s server.

Since many of these issues share similar roots, the same fixes work for several activation errors at once.

Note Apple mentions that iMessage activation can take up to 24 hours. You may wait before trying these fixes, but if the error persists, move ahead with the steps below.

Quick Ways to Fix the iMessage Waiting for Activation Error on iPhone

You can usually solve iMessage activation problems quickly by trying these effective solutions.

1. Check if You Can Send Text Messages

iMessage activation requires your iPhone to send a standard SMS.

To check;

  1. Open the Messages app and choose a friend or family member (preferably those who use an Android phone).
  2. Send an SMS and see if it is successfully delivered.
  3. If yes, move on to the next fixes. If not, please see how to fix the iPhone not sending text messages issue.

2. Make Sure Your iPhone Has an Active Internet Connection

A working internet connection is essential for iMessage activation. Try loading a webpage in Safari or streaming a video on YouTube. If nothing loads, your Wi-Fi or mobile data may be failing. You can follow guides for fixing Wi-Fi or cellular data issues if needed.

  • Wi-Fi Not Working on iPhone or iPad? 10 Ways to Fix It!
  • iPhone cellular data not working? 11 Ways to fix it!

If you are using cellular data, go to Settings, open Cellular, scroll down, and make sure the toggles for Settings and FaceTime are green. Also, if a VPN is enabled, turn it off because it can interfere with the activation process.

3. Set the Correct Date and Time

Incorrect date and time settings can interrupt iMessage activation. The simplest fix is setting these automatically.

  1. Open the Settings app and tap General.
  2. Tap Date & Time.
  3. Toggle on for Set Automatically.

4. Turn Airplane Mode On and Off

This simple trick often fixes activation glitches. You can toggle Airplane Mode from Control Center or in the Settings app. Wait a few seconds before turning it off again.

5. Restart Your iPhone

Restarting solves more issues than most people realize. Whether it is a router, computer, or phone, rebooting can clear temporary conflicts. Restart your iPhone and see if iMessage activates afterward.

6. Check Apple’s Server Status

Sometimes the problem is not on your end at all. Visit Apple’s System Status page and check if iMessage or Apple ID services are experiencing downtime. If they are, you simply need to wait until Apple resolves the issue.

7. Turn iMessage Off and On Again

  1. Open the Settings → Apps → Messages.
  2. Toggle off iMessage.
  3. After a minute, toggle it on.

8. Sign Out of Apple ID and Sign In Again

Sometimes your Apple ID session encounters a glitch.

To fix it:

  1. Open the Settings app and tap your name at the top.
  2. Scroll to the bottom and tap Sign Out.
  3. Enter your Apple ID password and proceed to sign out successfully.
  4. Next, restart your iPhone.
  5. Open the Settings app and tap Sign in from the top.
  6. After signing in, see if the iMessage problem is fixed. If not, try to turn iMessage off and on again.

9. Update Carrier Settings and Check Carrier Issues

Carriers push updates that improve texting, calling, and internet functionality. It helps to install any pending carrier updates. You should also contact your carrier and ask whether your account has any restrictions that prevent sending text messages or activating iMessage.

10. Update iOS

A software bug may be interfering with iMessage activation. Updating to the latest version of iOS often resolves these issues. Go to Settings, tap General, and open Software Update to install any available updates.

11. Reset Network Settings

If nothing works, resetting network settings is one of the most effective solutions for iMessage activation problems

  1. Open the Settings app and tap General.
  2. Tap Reset.
  3. Tap Reset Network Settings.
  4. Enter your iPhone passcode and confirm.
  5. Once done, restart your iPhone and try to activate iMessage again.

If this still doesn’t fix it, you may consider Reset All Settings. This removes modified system settings but does not erase your data. It’s still a good idea to back up your iPhone before doing this.

Back to Smooth Messaging

Once you try these simple fixes, iMessage usually activates without much trouble. Most issues come from temporary network or system glitches, and a quick reset or setting adjustment often does the job. With iMessage up and running, you can enjoy a smooth and reliable messaging experience again.

If you continue getting the same activation error, reach out to your carrier and Apple Support. They can assist you through call, chat, or even through social channels. Apple also offers the Support app, and most carriers have their dedicated support apps to make things easier.

Here are the support numbers for the most popular US carriers:

  • AT&T: 1-(800)-331-0500
  • Verizon: 1-(800)-922-0204
  • T-Mobile: 1-(877)-746-0909
  • Sprint: 1-(888)-211-4727

If you have questions or found another fix that worked for you, feel free to share it in the comments.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

title.rendered: How to Get Severe Weather Alerts on iPhone and iPad: Complete Guide

content.rendered:
The Weather app on your iPhone can do way more than just show you the forecast for your city and other locations. It can warn you of thunderstorms, heavy rain, heat waves, cyclones, and other dangerous conditions beforehand, so you can stay safe and prepared. However, you must keep severe weather alerts enabled to receive timely warnings.
.
This post details how to set up and use severe weather alerts on your iPhone, so you’re always prepared.

Table of Contents
  • What Types of Severe Weather Alerts Can Your iPhone Receive?
    • Weather App Alerts
    • Emergency and Public Safety Alerts
  • How to Turn On Severe Weather Alerts in the Weather App on iPhone
  • How to Turn On Government & Emergency Weather Alerts
  • Allow Location Access for Accurate Weather Alerts on iPhone
  • Troubleshooting: Not Receiving Severe Weather Alerts?
  • Extra Tips to Stay Prepared for Extreme Weather
  • Stay Alert, Stay Safe

What Types of Severe Weather Alerts Can Your iPhone Receive?

As the name suggests, Severe Weather Alerts notify you about dangerous or disruptive conditions happening near you or in locations you’ve added to the Weather app. However, in addition to the weather alerts handled by the Weather app, your iPhone can also receive government emergency alerts.

Weather App Alerts

These alerts are generated by Apple Weather based on trusted meteorological data. You may receive notifications for:

  • Heavy rain
  • Thunderstorms
  • Flooding risk
  • Heat waves
  • Snow or hail
  • Poor air quality (in supported regions)
  • Next-hour precipitation (in select countries)

Emergency and Public Safety Alerts

These alerts come directly from government agencies and may include:

  • Extreme weather warnings
  • Cyclone or hurricane alerts
  • Flash flood warnings
  • Public safety threats
  • National emergency notifications

Depending on your region, these alerts arrive automatically, without you needing to enable them on your iPhone.

How to Turn On Severe Weather Alerts in the Weather App on iPhone

Unlike Government Alerts, Severe Weather Alerts are not enabled by default, and you must enable them manually for every location you keep track of in the Weather app. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Weather app and tap the List icon in the bottom right corner.
  2. Tap the three-dot button in the top-right corner.
  3. Select Notifications from the dropdown menu.
  4. Under Current Location, toggle on:
    • Severe Weather
    • Next-Hour Precipitation (if available)

To enable Severe Weather alerts for the city you’ve added manually:

  1. Tap the city name under Your Locations.
  2. Toggle on Severe Weather.
  3. Tap Allow on the confirmation prompt.

Repeat this for every city you’ve added.

How to Turn On Government & Emergency Weather Alerts

Government alerts are the official alerts issued by national and regional authorities and come pre-enabled on your iPhone. When a government or emergency alert is received on your iPhone, you’ll hear a distinctive sound that resembles an alarm.

  1. Open the Settings app, then go to Notifications.
  2. Here, scroll to the Government Alert section and toggle on:
    • AMBER Alerts
    • Public Safety Alerts
    • Test Alerts
  3. Next, tap Emergency.
  4. Toggle on Emergency Alerts.

If you do not see the Government Alerts section, it means your carrier handles emergency broadcasts automatically. Your iPhone will still receive them when sent.

Allow Location Access for Accurate Weather Alerts on iPhone

Accurate severe weather alerts depend heavily on proper location permissions. If the Weather app doesn’t have continuous access to your precise location, you won’t receive them when the app is closed. Here’s how to enable it:

  1. Open Settings, scroll to the bottom, then tap Apps.
  2. Here, locate and tap Weather.
  3. Tap Location.
  4. Select Always under the Allow Location Access section.
  5. Toggle on Precise Location to ensure you receive alerts based on your exact location.

Troubleshooting: Not Receiving Severe Weather Alerts?

Extra Tips to Stay Prepared for Extreme Weather

Staying prepared goes beyond turning on alerts. A few extra settings and tools can make your iPhone even more reliable during sudden weather changes:

  • Set up Medical ID and emergency contacts: Helps first responders access your vital information quickly.
  • Use trusted third-party weather apps: Apps like AccuWeather, The Weather Channel, Windy, MAUSAM, or SACHET can offer faster or more detailed alerts.
  • Add Weather widgets: Ensures weather information is visible right on your Home or Lock Screen at a glance.
  • Allow Critical Alerts (if available): Let urgent notifications from third-party weather apps break through Silent mode and Focus modes.
  • Enable system Location-Based Alerts: Improves accuracy for government and app-based warnings.
  • Keep Background App Refresh on: Ensures the Weather app and alert apps stay up-to-date.
  • Review and update saved locations: Add places you care about and remove outdated ones for relevant alerts.

Stay Alert, Stay Safe

That’s pretty much it. Now you know the right settings you need to enable to make your iPhone a reliable early-warning system for dangerous weather conditions. So stop waiting and take out a few minutes to set everything up now, so your device can help keep you safe at all times.

Have you ever received a severe weather alert on your iPhone just in time? Share your experience. We would love to hear how these alerts have helped you stay safe.

FAQs

Are severe weather alerts free?

Yes. All severe weather alerts, government alerts, and Weather app notifications are free to receive.

Do severe weather alerts work when Do Not Disturb is on?

Yes. Time-sensitive and government alerts can break through Do Not Disturb and Focus modes.

What’s the difference between Government Alerts and Weather app alerts?

Weather app alerts come from Apple’s forecasting data, while Government Alerts are official emergency broadcasts sent by national or regional authorities.

  • Location Services Not Working on iPhone? 10 Fixes That Work

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

title.rendered: Apple Set to Surpass Samsung as Global Smartphone Leader Thanks to iPhone 17

content.rendered:
Apple is set to reclaim its position as the top smartphone maker in the world, driven by the strong demand for the iPhone 17 lineup. A new Counterpoint Research report cited by Bloomberg estimates Apple will see a 10% rise in iPhone shipments in 2025, beating Samsung’s projected 4.6% growth.

Apple’s early numbers for the iPhone 17 launch already show the shift. In the first month, sales jumped 22% while the overall smartphone market fell 2.7%. October continued the momentum with a 37% year-over-year rise in iPhone sales compared to the market’s 8% growth.

Market Share Shift and Key Drivers

Apple is now expected to close 2025 with a 19.4% global smartphone market share, enough to edge past Samsung. Counterpoint credits this shift not just to the strength of the iPhone 17 but also to the peak of a major upgrade cycle. Many users who bought phones during the COVID-19 boom are now due for an upgrade. On top of that, 358 million secondhand iPhones were sold between 2023 and Q2 2025, and a portion of those buyers are expected to move to new models next.

Also Read: Did iPhone Air Do Justice to the Death of the Plus Model?

Apple Could Stay on Top Until 2029

The report suggests Apple may retain the number one spot until at least 2029. Key contributors will be future products like the foldable iPhone and the budget-focused iPhone 17e, both expected to expand the brand’s reach.

This projection aligns with Apple’s internal expectations. In its recent earnings call, Tim Cook said the holiday quarter could be the biggest in company history. He highlighted strong demand for the iPhone 17 lineup, although the response to the iPhone Air variant has been mixed.

Would Apple becoming the world’s top smartphone maker again make any difference to you as a buyer?

mainEntity.name: Why is my System Data storage so high on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: System Data storage on Mac consists of different files, such as cached data, DMG files, application support files, old downloads, and more. If you haven't deleted them, System Data storage on Mac will be high. You can delete those files to free up storage on your Mac.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to delete System Data files on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: The files and folders in the System Data storage consist of junk or temporary files on your Mac. Though it will not cause any issues with the Mac, it's best to exercise caution so you don't delete important files you may need later.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.

mainEntity.name: Does desktop mode work with all websites?

acceptedAnswer.text: It might. Some interactive elements may not behave correctly on a touchscreen, especially if the site wasn’t designed with mobile compatibility in mind.

title.rendered: How to Use Emergency SOS on iPhone (Step-by-Step Guide)

content.rendered:
When something goes wrong, your iPhone can literally become a lifesaver. With Emergency SOS, you can quickly contact emergency services, share your location, and alert your emergency contacts with just a few taps or button presses. 

In the latest iOS versions, Apple has also added Satellite support, so you can get help even in a remote place. In this guide, you will learn everything you need to know about how Emergency SOS works, how you can set it up on your iPhone, and how to use it in real-life situations.

Table of Contents
  • What is Emergency SOS on iPhone?
    • Key Features of Emergency SOS in iOS 26
  • How to Set Up Emergency SOS on iPhone
  • How to Use Emergency SOS on Your iPhone
    • Method 1: Hold and Release
    • Method 2: Press the Side Button 3 Times
    • Method 3: Use the On-Screen SOS Slider
  • How Emergency SOS Works After You Call
    • Share Live Photo or Video to Emergency Services
  • How Satellite Emergency SOS Works (iOS 26)
  • Tips for Using Emergency SOS Safely

What is Emergency SOS on iPhone?

Emergency SOS is a built-in safety feature that lets you instantly call emergency services from anywhere, even when you’re not connected to your usual cellular network. It can also send alerts and your real-time location to the people you trust the most. 

In iOS 26, this feature got even smarter, with improved satellite connectivity and faster location sharing. It’s available on iPhone 8 and later, but satellite perks shine on iPhone 14 and up.

Key Features of Emergency SOS in iOS 26

Here’s what you can do with Emergency SOS:

  • Make a quick call to your local emergency number, such as 911 in the US or 112 in Europe, using button presses or on-screen options. 
  • Automatically send your location and your Medical ID to first responders (in supported regions). 
  • Notify emergency contacts with your location updates. 
  • Use satellite SOS when you’re off the grid. 
  • Trigger Crash Detection to call for help after severe car accidents.

These features work quietly in the background but activate instantly when needed. You can also set up and use Emergency SOS on your Apple Watch. It’s quite useful when you’re experiencing an emergency, and your iPhone is out of reach.

How to Set Up Emergency SOS on iPhone

Before you rely on Emergency SOS, take two minutes to set it up.

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone. 
  2. Scroll down and tap Emergency SOS.
  3. Here toggle on: 
    • Call with Hold and Release 
    • Call with 3 Button Presses 
    • Call After Severe Crash (if available)
  4. Next, tap Set up Emergency Contacts in Health.
  5. It will take you to the Health app. Tap Create Medical ID if you have not set it up yet. 
  6. Enter your basic details and tap the checkmark in the top-right corner. 
  7. Tap Add Emergency Contact, then select the people you trust.

Setting up Emergency Contacts is essential as they’ll receive your location when SOS is triggered. On the other hand, Medical ID helps first responders see important info right from your Lock Screen. So, add details such as your blood type, allergies, and medications. 

To learn more, check out our guide on How to set up Medical ID on iPhone and Apple Watch.

How to Use Emergency SOS on Your iPhone

When seconds count, you need speed. Here are all the ways to activate SOS in an emergency, even if your iPhone is locked.

Method 1: Hold and Release

  1. Press and hold the Side and Volume button together. 
  2. Keep holding until the countdown finishes.
  3. Release to automatically call emergency services.

This is the fastest method because it works even when your screen is off.

Method 2: Press the Side Button 3 Times

This is ideal if you want to be discreet. 

Just press the Side button three times quickly, and the SOS screen will appear with the countdown. Once it finishes, your iPhone will connect to the emergency services

Method 3: Use the On-Screen SOS Slider

  1. Hold the Side + Volume button. 
  2. When the screen appears, drag the Emergency SOS slider.

This gives you control if you want time to make a decision.

Note In some situations, you may want to contact emergency services without your iPhone flashing or announcing. For that, go to Settings > Emergency SOS and toggle on Call Quietly.

Also read: Fix iPhone Stuck in Emergency SOS Mode

How Emergency SOS Works After You Call

Once a call is made, the iPhone automatically does the following: 

  • Sends your location: Your emergency contacts receive your initial location plus updates for a period, usually 10–20 minutes if you move.  
  • Shares your Medical ID: If turned on, emergency responders can access critical health information.

It also notifies you with follow-up options. You can even stop location sharing at any time.

Share Live Photo or Video to Emergency Services

Emergency services can send a prompt to share live videos or upload previously recorded photos and videos to understand your surroundings. This live video won’t be saved on your device.

  1. When asked to start sending live videos to emergency personnel, tap Share.  
  2. To pause or resume sharing at any moment, select the Camera button.  
  3. Tap the End Call button and then select Stop Sharing Camera to end live streaming.  

If you only want to share an existing photo or video, select Choose on the prompt, then select the image or video. Finally, if you don’t want to share images or videos with emergency personnel, tap Not Now when asked. 

How Satellite Emergency SOS Works (iOS 26)

If you’re somewhere without cellular or Wi-Fi, like hiking or camping in a remote area, your iPhone can use satellite connection to contact emergency services. Here’s how to use Emergency SOS via satellite on iPhone: 

  1. If your call to emergency services doesn’t connect, you get an alert. Tap Emergency Text via Satellite > Report Emergency.
  2. Now, you need to answer quick questions, like what’s the emergency, are you injured, your current surroundings, etc.
  3. Apple sends your info to emergency responders through a relay center. Your iPhone guides you to point your device toward a satellite. 
  4. Once you’re connected, start a conversation with emergency responders. 

Note that you need a clear view of the sky for the satellite connection. Also, messages may take several seconds to send, and it’s available only in supported countries on iPhone 14 and later. 

Tips for Using Emergency SOS Safely 

  • Be careful with accidental triggers, especially if “Call with 3 Presses” is on. 
  • Keep your Medical ID updated for accurate help. 
  • Tell your emergency contacts that they may receive alerts from you. 
  • Practice the SOS Demo so you don’t panic during a real emergency.

Emergency SOS is a Must for Every iPhone User!

Emergency SOS is one of the most important features on your iPhone. You might never need it, but if you do, it can save your life or someone else’s. With iOS 26 improvements, it’s faster, smarter, and easier to activate than ever before. 

Take a few minutes today to set it up. You’ll thank yourself later.

mainEntity.name: Does Your iPhone Actually Have an EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every iPhone supports eSIM technology. Apple introduced eSIM with the iPhone XS, XS Max, and XR in 2018. Most recent iPhones have EID because they are eSIM-compatible. So if you have a device without eSIM functionality, it may not have an EID number at all.

mainEntity.name: When Will You Actually Need Your EID?

acceptedAnswer.text: You'll need your EID when setting up a new eSIM plan, whether you're switching carriers, adding a second line, or buying a travel eSIM. You'll also need it when transferring your eSIM during an upgrade, troubleshooting activation failures, or unlocking your device for international use.

mainEntity.name: How to Keep Your EID Secure?

acceptedAnswer.text: Treat your EID like your IMEI or serial number. Don't post it publicly on social media or forums. Only share it with legitimate carriers or support teams when you've initiated the contact. If someone calls claiming to be from your carrier and asks for your EID, hang up and call the carrier back using their official number. When you're genuinely activating an eSIM, sharing your EID is completely normal and necessary.
