title.rendered: Apple Introduces New Mini Apps Partner Program With 15% Commission Option

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • 15% commission now applies to mini apps if developers join Apple’s new Mini Apps Partner Program and follow specific tech requirements.
  • Apps must use two Apple APIs—Declared Age Range and Advanced Commerce—to qualify for reduced fees and maintain a secure user experience.
  • Mini app purchases must stay self-contained; items or subscriptions can’t be shared between different mini apps.
  • Tencent isn’t getting exclusive access—despite early reports, Apple confirms all developers must apply under the same terms.
  • You need to apply manually on Apple’s site, and apps must use web tech like HTML5 or JavaScript to qualify for the new program.

Apple has rolled out a new Mini Apps Partner Program that reduces the commission on eligible mini-app purchases to 15%. The announcement follows reports of Apple reaching an agreement with Tencent for WeChat mini apps, though Apple confirms the new program is open to all developers. The information was first reported by 9to5Mac’s Ryan Christoffel.

Apple Expands Support for Mini Apps on the App Store

Apple has supported mini apps built with HTML5 and JavaScript since 2017, but developers never had a dedicated program or financial advantage. The new Partner Program fills that gap by offering a lower commission rate to developers who meet Apple’s requirements.

According to Apple’s Developer website, mini apps must be created using web technologies, and the goal is to help developers grow revenue while offering users a safer, smoother experience inside these lightweight app experiences.

Reduced 15% Commission Comes With New Requirements

Developers won’t be automatically added to the program. They need to apply using a request form on Apple’s website.
To receive the reduced 15% commission on mini-app In-App Purchases, apps must support two key App Store technologies:

  • Declared Age Range API for age-appropriate content
  • Advanced Commerce API for secure and consistent purchase flows

These requirements show Apple’s intention to build a more controlled and user-friendly mini-app ecosystem.

What Counts as a Qualifying Mini App Purchase?

Apple’s Q&A page explains that qualifying transactions must be completed and consumed within a single mini app. Purchases can’t be shared or carried across different mini apps.

Apple lists two qualifying examples:

  1. Consumables like currency, boosts, or items used instantly in one mini app
  2. Auto-renewing subscriptions purchased and accessed only within that same mini app

A simple example would be a word game selling extra attempts for a puzzle or a language learning mini app offering a monthly plan limited to that single mini app.

Tencent Isn’t Getting Special Treatment

Early reports suggested Tencent had negotiated a unique deal, but Apple clarified that Tencent must apply like any other developer. The program is open to all developers hosting mini apps, as long as they follow Apple’s rules.

Conclusion

Apple’s Mini Apps Partner Program marks a bigger push toward expanding mini-app experiences on the App Store. With a reduced commission and clear API requirements, developers now have more incentive to build lightweight, web-based app experiences that stay within Apple’s ecosystem.

title.rendered: 5 Best AirTag Cases That Look Great and Keep Your Tracker Safe

content.rendered:
Apple’s AirTag helps you keep track of your essentials like keys, wallets, and bags. But the tracker’s small size means it needs a reliable case to stay secure. Moreover, you can’t attach it to your keys without a case. A well-designed AirTag case keeps the tracker firmly in place, protects it from scuffs from daily use, and offers practical attachment options like key rings, loops, clips, or adhesive mounts.

In this post, you’ll learn how to choose the right AirTag case and see a comprehensive list of the best options that perfectly suit your needs.

Table of Contents
  • How to Choose the Right AirTag Case
  • 5 Best Apple AirTag Cases: Slim, Rugged, and Stylish
    • Apple AirTag FineWoven Key Ring
    • Spigen AirTag Case
    • Belkin Airtag Secure Holder With Strap
    • Caseology by Spigen Vault Case
    • ElevationLab TagVault AirTag Wallet Holder
  • Which AirTag Case Should You Buy?

How to Choose the Right AirTag Case

When choosing a new AirTag case, always select one that strikes a perfect balance between protection, style, and usability for your everyday routine. Here are some of the most important factors to consider:

  • Material: Check if the case is made of leather, silicone, hard plastic, or metal, as that affects how well it withstands drops, scratches, and rough use.
  • Attachment style: For keys or backpacks, a key ring or clip works best. For wallets or thin items, you might prefer an adhesive mount or ultra-slim case.
  • Fit and protection: Ensure a snug fit that doesn’t block the AirTag’s speaker or signal.
  • Size and form factor: Consider how bulky the case is. A slim wallet holder may add almost no bulk, while a rugged case with a clip may be larger.
  • Design: Go for something that suits your personality or matches your accessories.
  • Price and availability: Many options are available across U.S. retailers, including the Apple Store, Amazon, and Target.

5 Best Apple AirTag Cases: Slim, Rugged, and Stylish

Now that you know how to choose the right AirTag case, here’s a comprehensive list of the best Apple AirTag cases that offer the right balance of protection, convenience, and design:

1. Apple AirTag FineWoven Key Ring

If you have the budget and are looking for a key ring-style AirTag case, you don’t need to look further than Apple’s very own FineWoven Key Ring. The case offers a soft, premium texture with a snug fit tailored for the AirTag. Most importantly, the case doesn’t add bulk to your AirTag and is lightweight, elegant, and designed to complement daily carry items like keys and bags.

2. Spigen AirTag Case

Users looking for something other than key ring cases, the Spigen case is the best option. It’s made from premium silicone, which protects the tracker from scratches and drops while remaining lightweight for daily use. The case features an adhesive strip at the back that lets you stick it to flat surfaces, such as dashboards, bike frames, and other objects.

3. Belkin Airtag Secure Holder With Strap

The Belkin AirTag Secure Holder With Strap uses a twist-and-lock mechanism that keeps the AirTag firmly enclosed, which means it will not pop out even when you attach it to items that move around a lot. The included strap adds flexibility and makes it easy to secure the AirTag to backpacks, luggage, kids’ school bags, gym gear, or even travel pouches. Additionally, it features raised edges that help protect the AirTag from everyday scratches while leaving the speaker area unobstructed for better tracking alerts.

4. Caseology by Spigen Vault Case

Another option from Spigen’s vast range, Caseology’s Vault Case features a rugged, matte-textured design that offers a firm grip and shields the AirTag from scratches and everyday wear and tear. Unlike regular straps, this case includes a carabiner clip that makes it easy to attach to backpacks, pet collars, travel bags, or outdoor gear, providing a secure way to track items that are subject to rougher handling.

5. ElevationLab TagVault AirTag Wallet Holder

The ElevationLab TagVault Wallet Holder is designed for users who prefer carrying their AirTag in a wallet rather than attaching it to keys or bags. It features a super-slim, curved design that fits smoothly inside most bi-fold and tri-fold wallets without adding bulk. The case fully encloses the AirTag in a durable polymer shell, keeping it protected from pressure, bending, and wear that often occur in pockets.

All this makes it a great option for people who want a hidden tracking solution for items like wallets, passport holders, and travel pouches.

Which AirTag Case Should You Buy?

If you want style and durability, Apple’s FineWoven key ring is a top choice. For budget protection, go with the Belkin Secure Holder. Travelers or adventurers should pick the ElevationLab TagVault for waterproof durability.

A good AirTag case keeps the tracker protected, secure, and easy to attach to everyday items. The options in this list offer different levels of protection, style, and convenience, so you can pick one that fits your routine.

Which AirTag case are you using right now? Share your favorite in the comments below.

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. @graph.name: Apple AirTag FineWoven Key Ring
@graph.description: If you have the budget and are looking for a key ring-style AirTag case, you don’t need to look further than Apple’s very own FineWoven Key Ring. The case offers a soft, premium texture with a snug fit tailored for the AirTag.

@graph.name: Spigen AirTag Case
@graph.description: It’s made from premium silicone, which protects the tracker from scratches and drops while remaining lightweight for daily use. The case features an adhesive strip at the back that lets you stick it to flat surfaces, such as dashboards, bike frames, and other objects.

@graph.name: Belkin Apple Airtag Secure Holder With Strap
@graph.description: The Belkin AirTag Secure Holder With Strap uses a twist-and-lock mechanism that keeps the AirTag firmly enclosed, which means it will not pop out even when you attach it to items that move around a lot.

@graph.name: Caseology by Spigen Vault Case
@graph.description: Another option from Spigen’s vast range, Caseology’s Vault Case features a rugged, matte-textured design that offers a firm grip and shields the AirTag from scratches and everyday wear and tear.

@graph.name: ElevationLab TagVault AirTag Wallet Holder
@graph.description: The ElevationLab TagVault Wallet Holder is designed for users who prefer carrying their AirTag in a wallet rather than attaching it to keys or bags. It features a super-slim, curved design that fits smoothly inside most bi-fold and tri-fold wallets without adding bulk.

title.rendered: 6 Best Compact Apple Watch Power Banks Worth Buying

content.rendered:
Running out of battery on your Apple Watch can be frustrating, especially when you’re tracking workouts or navigating on the go. Thankfully, modern power banks designed specifically for the Apple Watch keep your device charged all day long. 

In this guide, we’ll explore the best power banks for Apple Watch, from ultra-portable keychain chargers to travel-friendly multi-device hubs. I’ll outline their main features and charging performance so that you can easily choose the right one. 

Table of Contents
  • What to Consider in a Good Apple Watch Power Bank
    • 1. Compatibility & Charging Performance
    • 2. Battery Capacity vs. Portability
    • 3. Charging Options
    • 4. Build Quality & Safety
    • 5. Design & Usability
  • Top 6 Apple Watch Power Banks: Our Best Picks
    • 1. Anker MagGo 10,000 mAh Power Bank
    • 2. LISEN 10,000 mAh MagSafe Apple Watch Power Bank
    • 3. HUOTO 1200 mAh Mini Power Bank
    • 4. JOYROOM 2000 mAh Apple Watch Power Bank
    • 5. i.VALUX 1000 mAh Portable Power Bank
    • 6. INIU 5000 mAh Apple Watch Power Bank
  • Final Verdict: Which Apple Watch Power Bank Should You Buy?

What to Consider in a Good Apple Watch Power Bank 

The right Apple Watch power bank should fit your routine and reliably charge your Apple Watch. Here’s what to look for before you buy: 

1. Compatibility & Charging Performance

Make sure it’s Apple Watch-certified or uses a built-in magnetic charger designed specifically for the watch. That ensures stable charging and safe alignment. For newer models like Series 11, Ultra 3, and SE 3, look for fast charging (5W or higher). 

2. Battery Capacity vs. Portability 

You don’t need massive power; even a 1,000 mAh to 2,000 mAh battery can fully recharge your Apple Watch once or twice. If you also want to top up your iPhone, go for something around 10,000 mAh. Just make sure it’s still compact and travel-friendly enough to carry easily. 

3. Charging Options 

Choose between a watch-only charger and a multiport power bank that charges your watch, phone, and AirPods at once. It’s all about USB-C ports, wireless charging pads, or integrated cables that will make all the difference when on the go. 

4. Build Quality & Safety 

Stick to the recognized brands that have overcurrent, overheating, and short-circuit protection. The best power banks are airline-safe, durable, and built with premium materials for long-term reliability. 

5. Design & Usability 

Look for a magnetic, cable-free design that snaps easily to your watch. Bonus points if it’s keychain-sized or fits neatly in your pocket or travel pouch.

Top 6 Apple Watch Power Banks: Our Best Picks

Here, I have listed some travel-friendly and safe magnetic power banks designed for the Apple Watch. 

1. Anker MagGo 10,000 mAh Power Bank

If your Apple Watch always seems to run out of battery, the Anker MagGo Power Bank is the kind of backup you’ll actually want to carry. With a built-in Apple-certified magnetic charger, you can snap your watch in place instantly for fast charging; no extra cables or docks are needed. 

This compact 10,000 mAh battery also comes with a 35W USB-C port and built-in cable, so you can fast-charge your iPhone, iPad, or AirPods alongside your watch. What really stands out is convenience. Anker MagGo features an adjustable magnetic watch stand and a smart display to display battery status.  

Therefore, if you’re looking for a reliable, travel-ready charger that handles both your Apple Watch and iPhone, this Anker power bank is an easy win. 

2. LISEN 10,000 mAh MagSafe Apple Watch Power Bank

LISEN Ultra Slim MagSafe Power Bank is a portable charger that won’t weigh down your pocket but still gives serious backup. With a 10,000 mAh battery packed into a sleek, just-0.5-inch-thick body, it’s designed for those who carry light but expect big performance.  

The magnetic MagSafe surface locks your Apple Watch with satisfying precision. On the wired side, there’s a built-in, durable USB-C cable supporting up to 20W fast charging and wireless charging up to ~7.5 W for the latest watch models. So, you can juice your devices multiple times. 

In real-world use, it’s safer thanks to overcharge protection and NTC temperature control. Also, LISEN has ensured you can board flights without worry. The digital display on the side shows charging status and remaining power. Overall, the LISEN battery pack strikes a solid balance between size and power. 

Check out: Best MagSafe accessories for iPhone 

3. HUOTO 1200 mAh Mini Power Bank

If you’re always on the move and tend to misplace things, the HUOTO portable wireless charger brings a smart, travel-ready solution. With a built-in 1200 mAh battery, it’s compact enough (about the size of the watch itself) and ready to give your watch roughly 1-1.5 full charges.  

The magnetic wireless charging pad automatically aligns with your watch. Additionally, the power bank has a metal buckle for attaching it to your keychain. I really liked its new indicator light design, which changes color based on the power status. Finally, you get safety features such as overcurrent, overvoltage, short-circuit, and overheat protection.  

4. JOYROOM 2000 mAh Apple Watch Power Bank

Another compact travel-friendly Apple Watch power bank with more backup. The 2,000 mAh battery inside can fully recharge most Apple Watch models 3–4 times (and up to 2 times for the Ultra model) before you need to plug it in again.  

With a built-in magnetic charger that snaps your watch into place with no cables or fuss. Additionally, its small, keychain-style design with double leather and a reinforced metal buckle lets you slip it into your pocket or clip it to your bag. You can see the precise battery status on the LED screen.   

Explore: The Best Apple Watch Chargers for Travel

5. i.VALUX 1000 mAh Portable Power Bank

For a minimalist like me, the i.VALUX Portable Wireless Charger is a solid choice. With a built-in 1,000 mAh battery and a magnetic wireless charging pad designed for your watch, it’s the backup that actually fits your lifestyle.  

You can get 1-1.5 times full charging for your Apple Watch from this. Moreover, its key-ring form factor helps you clip it to your bag or keys and carry it everywhere. The brand has used traditional LED indicators and safety features for convenient charging. 

6. INIU 5000 mAh Apple Watch Power Bank

If you’re tired of carrying multiple battery packs for your iPhone and Apple Watch, the INIU Portable Charger might just be for you. With a compact size that slips into your palm and a weight of just around 4.1 ounces, it’s made for on-the-go power.  

This power bank includes a wireless charging pad, built-in USB-C cable, and another USB-C port, so you can charge your Apple Watch, iPhone and AirPods together without juggling multiple cables. With 5,000 mAh capacity and 5W fast charging support, you can juice your watch 6 times.  

It’s an airline-approved size, easy to clip onto your backpack or toss in your jacket pocket. Plus, the brand touts fast, safe charging and offers a three-year warranty —nice to see in a budget power bank.  

Final Verdict: Which Apple Watch Power Bank Should You Buy?

If you’re looking to keep your Apple Watch powered and ready, choosing a quality power bank comes down to compatibility, portability, and peace of mind. A good model will feature a built-in magnetic charger, reliable output, and a travel-friendly size. 

  • On-the-go traveler or commuter: Go for a multi-device bank with decent capacity (~5,000-10,000 mAh).
  • Watch-only quick top-up: A compact, watch-centric bank (~1,000-2,000 mAh) is enough for peace of mind. 

So, pick one that meets your daily routine and fits your budget.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

@graph.name: Anker MagGo Power Bank for Apple Watch
@graph.description: If your Apple Watch always seems to run out of battery, the Anker MagGo Power Bank is the kind of backup you’ll actually want to carry. With a built-in Apple-certified magnetic charger, you can snap your watch in place instantly for fast charging; no extra cables or docks are needed.

@graph.name: LISEN 0.5 Ultra Slim MagSafe Power Bank
@graph.description: LISEN Ultra Slim MagSafe Power Bank is a portable charger that won’t weigh down your pocket but still gives serious backup. With a 10,000 mAh battery packed into a sleek, just-0.5-inch-thick body, it’s designed for those who carry light but expect big performance.

@graph.name: HUOTO Portable Charger for Apple Watch
@graph.description: If you’re always on the move and tend to misplace things, the HUOTO portable wireless charger brings a smart, travel-ready solution. With a built-in 1200 mAh battery, it’s compact enough (about the size of the watch itself) and ready to give your watch roughly 1-1.5 full charges.

@graph.name: JOYROOM 2000mAh Apple Watch Power Bank
@graph.description: Another compact travel-friendly Apple Watch power bank with more backup. The 2,000mAh battery inside can fully recharge most Apple Watch models 3–4 times (and up to 2 times for the Ultra model) before you need to plug it in again.

@graph.name: i.VALUX Portable Wireless Charger for Apple Watch
@graph.description: For a minimalist like me, the i.VALUX Portable Wireless Charger is a solid choice. With a built-in 1,000mAh battery and a magnetic wireless charging pad designed for your watch, it’s the backup that actually fits your lifestyle.

@graph.name: INIU 5000mAh Apple Watch Power Bank
@graph.description: If you’re tired of carrying multiple battery packs for your iPhone and Apple Watch, the INIU Portable Charger might just be for you. With a compact size that slips into your palm and a weight of just around 4.1 ounces, it’s made for on-the-go power.

title.rendered: Everything New in iOS 26.2 Beta 2

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Games app adds smarter tracking tools with real-time scores, easier library sorting, and better controller navigation for smoother gameplay discovery.
  • Measure and Lock Screen adopt Liquid Glass design as Apple deepens its UI overhaul with aesthetic tweaks and a more customizable clock slider.
  • Reminders and Health get functional boosts with alarms that bypass Focus modes and a clearer Sleep Score system rated up to “Very High.”
  • Podcasts and News introduce smarter discovery using AI-generated chapters and quick section links to make content browsing faster and more intuitive.
  • CarPlay and Vision Pro hint at broader integration, adding pinned message controls and prepping Logitech Muse support in Notes for future VisionOS hardware.

iOS 26.2 beta 2 has rolled out for developers and testers, and it brings a lot more to the table than typical incremental updates. Apple is enhancing several key apps, boosting AI-powered features, and introducing new capabilities as they gear up for the public release.

Games App Enhancements: Improved Navigation and Live Scores

Apple is upping its game with the Games app by providing tools that simplify browsing and tracking gameplay. Users can now sort and filter their game library with ease, navigate smoother using a controller, and even get real-time score updates while watching gameplay. Though the change might seem minor, it makes the experience livelier.

Measure App’s Level Tool Gets a Liquid Glass Makeover

The Level tool within the Measure app now embraces the Liquid Glass aesthetic that debuted in iOS 26. This update aligns the tool’s appearance with Apple’s latest design language, refreshing its look.

Messages on CarPlay Allows Disabling Pinned Conversations

Users now have the option to turn off pinned chats directly via CarPlay Settings. For those who prefer a less crowded messages list while driving, this tweak aids in reducing distractions and keeping the interface streamlined.

Smoother Animations and Preparations for Logitech Muse

Menus open with noticeably smoother animations, giving the UI a refined polish. Additionally, there are indications that Notes is prepping to support the Logitech Muse on Apple Vision Pro, suggesting broader accessory support might be on the way.

macOS 26.2: Edge Light Enhances Video Call Lighting

Complementing the iOS updates, Apple introduces Edge Light in macOS 26.2. Using your Mac’s display as a makeshift ring light, it promises better face lighting during calls without extra equipment. This feature, designed for Apple Silicon Macs, adjusts automatically via the Neural Engine.

Sleep Score System Overhaul in Health App

The Health app’s Sleep Score system is undergoing a tweak. The top rating will now be termed “Very High,” replacing what was known as “Excellent.” User feedback has led to recalibration since the previous scoring bands were deemed too broad.

Apple Podcasts Adds AI-Driven Features

In a significant upgrade, the Podcasts app will harness AI to automatically generate chapters for episodes, spotlight referenced shows, and gather related podcast links for easier exploration.

Apple News Introduces Quick Access to Sections

Redesign efforts in the News app continue as it now includes quick links to major sections. This feature allows users to dive into popular areas more swiftly without having to sort through various menus.

AirPods Live Translation Set for EU Launch in December

Apple has confirmed that in December, EU users will gain access to AirPods Live Translation. This timeline aligns with the expected end of iOS 26.2’s beta phase.

Lock Screen Flexibility: Liquid Glass Slider Enhancements

Users can now adjust the translucency of the Lock Screen clock through a newly enhanced Liquid Glass slider. This fine-tuning option works across all clock fonts, adding a layer of customization depth.

Reminders App Gains Alarming and Timed Alerts for Urgent Tasks

The Reminders app now includes alarms and timers for critical tasks, surpassing Time Sensitive notifications. It’s designed to break through Focus modes, ensuring users don’t overlook important reminders.

Though still in the beta phase, iOS 26.2 beta 2 brings meaningful refinements that impact nearly every corner of the system.

How do these updates impact you? Share your thoughts below.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

title.rendered: Apple Wallet Now Offers Digital ID with US Passport

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Digital ID now works with US passports letting Apple Wallet users create a verified ID without waiting on their state to support mobile licenses.
  • Setup takes minutes on your iPhone using a passport scan, chip read, selfie, and facial movements, with all data processed locally and privately.
  • Not a digital passport replacement—you’ll still need your physical passport for international travel and legal identification.
  • Works at 250+ TSA checkpoints across US airports for domestic flights; presenting it requires Face ID or Touch ID approval.
  • Rollout is gradual and has limits—you’ll need a valid passport, and it won’t work for travel abroad or in every app yet.

Apple has introduced its Digital ID feature within the Apple Wallet, enabling those in the United States with a valid US passport to create a secure digital identity on their iPhone. This feature, initially unveiled at the WWDC, is now being made available through a server-side update.

How Apple’s New Digital ID Works

This new Digital ID setup resembles the process for adding a driver’s license or state ID to Wallet, but it relies on verification from your passport. Users begin by opening the Wallet app, tapping the Add button, selecting Driver’s License or ID Cards, and opting for Digital ID. The setup procedure involves:

  • Scanning the passport
  • Reading the embedded chip within the passport
  • Taking a selfie
  • Performing quick head and facial movements

The system then verifies your identity within minutes and integrates your Digital ID into Wallet. Apple emphasizes that all processing is done privately on your device. Passport data remains on your iPhone, and Apple won’t know when or where you present the ID. Only the necessary information for specific verification is shared, so, for instance, if you’re confirming your age, just your age is shown, not other details like your address.

This Isn’t a Digital Passport Replacement

Apple makes it clear that the Digital ID is not a substitute for your physical passport. Instead, it uses your passport to create a verified digital identity for applicable situations. You’ll still need your physical passport for travel and legal situations. The feature allows you to set up a Digital ID regardless of whether your state has adopted mobile driver’s licenses, as long as you have a passport.

Where You Can Use Digital ID Today

Initially, this Digital ID support is available at TSA checkpoints at over 250 airports in the United States. It’s only applicable for domestic travel, necessitating a physical ID for international flights. To present the Digital ID, users double-click the side or Home button, select the ID, and hold the iPhone or Apple Watch near the identity reader. The specific information being requested is shown, requiring approval with Face ID or Touch ID.

Apple indicates more applications on the horizon, like:

  • Age verification within apps
  • Identity checks for various services
  • Approvals at certain businesses
  • Age verification for app-driven alcohol deliveries (e.g., Uber Eats)

The Digital ID addition will complement the existing option to include a driver’s license or state ID, which remains available in select US states.

Why This Launch Matters

This release is pivotal in advancing the acceptance of Digital ID in the US. The progression of mobile driver’s license support has been slow; thus, Apple’s passport-based system offers millions of rapid access to secure digital identities without needing state-level approvals. Apple Wallet users in the US can begin adding their Digital ID now, though the update’s gradual rollout might mean a short wait for some devices.

How does this impact you? Share your thoughts with us below.

title.rendered: Apple Extends 2025 Holiday Return Deadline to January 8, 2026

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Holiday return period runs through January 8, 2026 for purchases made between November 12 and December 25, extending Apple’s usual 14-day policy.
  • iPhones on carrier financing excluded as devices bought via T-Mobile or Verizon installment plans still follow standard return terms.
  • Gift cards, software, and developer items not eligible under the holiday extension, following Apple’s usual list of non-returnable products.
  • Early shoppers benefit most from the update, with nearly two months to exchange or return eligible products like iPhones, Macs, and Apple Watches.
  • Returns still subject to Apple’s standard sales policy, so damaged, opened, or misused items may be denied even within the extended window.

Apple has opened its annual holiday return policy, allowing customers a longer timeframe to return items bought during the festive season. This extended return period covers purchases made in-store and online starting November 12, 2025.

Holiday Return Window Now Runs Through January 8, 2026

Based on Apple’s official site, items purchased between November 12, 2025, and December 25, 2025, are eligible for return until January 8, 2026. Any purchases made after December 25 will revert to Apple’s usual 14-day return policy.

For those picking up a new iPhone, MacBook, or Apple Watch, this means nearly two months to decide if the gift works out, especially beneficial for those preferring to shop early. However, there are caveats: Apple notes that iPhones bought through T-Mobile or Verizon on finance are not included in this policy extension and must adhere to the regular terms. Apple’s standard Sales and Refunds Policy continues to govern all other aspects.

Standard Return Rules Still Apply to Certain Items

Many Apple products are covered by the extended policy, though some exceptions persist. Categories still excluded include Apple Gift Cards, opened software, electronic software downloads, software upgrades, and Apple Developer items like memberships or WWDC tickets.

While these exclusions typically aren’t major concerns for most holiday shoppers, Apple ensures the policy is clear to avoid any confusion over what’s eligible for return.

Apple Stores Embrace the Holiday Season

In tandem with the policy update, Apple’s retail locations and online storefronts have decked the halls, introducing festive decorations as part of the seasonal shift. This change aligns with Apple’s tradition of welcoming the holiday season with aesthetic updates and shopping-friendly policies.

This extended return window could motivate buyers to start their holiday shopping earlier, minimizing panic over unwanted gifts come December.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro Max May Become Apple’s Heaviest Phone Yet

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone 18 Pro Max may top 240 grams making it the heaviest iPhone ever, surpassing the iPhone 14 Pro Max’s 240g and iPhone 17 Pro Max’s 233g.
  • Thicker design hints at larger battery suggesting Apple is prioritizing battery life even if it means adding more bulk to the Pro Max line.
  • User preference drives the shift as heavier iPhones with stronger materials and better battery have outsold lighter models like the iPhone Air.
  • Goodbye to the thin era with Apple now leaning into durability, heat management, and performance instead of chasing ultra-slim builds.
  • Heavier build could affect usability for some users, especially those prioritizing comfort or one-handed use over all-day battery and titanium builds.

Apple’s next top-tier phone might set a new record, not for speed or camera innovation, but for weight. According to a recent leak from Instant Digital on Weibo, the iPhone 18 Pro Max is expected to be even chunkier and heavier than the iPhone 17 Pro Max, surpassing 240 grams.

Leak Suggests a Heavier Build

Instant Digital claims that the iPhone 18 Pro Max will weigh over 240 grams, positioning it as the heftiest iPhone ever. By comparison:

  • iPhone 17 Pro Max weighs 233 grams
  • iPhone 16 Pro Max comes in at 227 grams
  • iPhone 14 Pro Max also tipped the scale at 240 grams

If these figures hold up, next year’s model will outdo its predecessors, continuing Apple’s pattern of producing beefier Pro models.

The leak also notes a slight increase in thickness for the iPhone 18 Pro Max. This could mean Apple is upping the battery size again, which may be a welcome change for users, even if it adds some extra heft.

Apple’s Focus on “Thick and Heavy” Design

Apple’s recent moves appear calculated: consumers are leaning towards battery life and durability rather than lightness. The iPhone 17 series underscored this, the slimmer iPhone Air lagged behind in sales, while the more substantial Pro versions thrived.

The consumer feedback seems clear: bulkier phones with a longer battery life and quality materials justify the additional weight. Apple seems prepared to cement this approach with the iPhone 18 Pro Max.

Moving Away from “Thinner Is Better”

For several years, Apple pursued a thinner design at the expense of battery capacity and camera space. With the latest Pro models focusing on endurance, heat management, and robust materials like titanium, that previous philosophy is clearly becoming outdated.

Should this leak prove accurate, the iPhone 18 Pro Max might well mark a full transition, a phone crafted more for longevity and robustness than for slimness.

Would a heavier iPhone make a difference for you? Share your thoughts below.

title.rendered: 5 Best Apple Watch Chargers for Every Lifestyle in 2026

content.rendered:
Once you start using an Apple Watch, it becomes an integral part of your daily routine. It helps you track your workouts, manage notifications, and stay connected throughout the day, even when your iPhone isn’t around. But when the battery runs low, a reliable charger becomes essential.

While the charging puck you get in the box gets the job done pretty well, third-party options have evolved to offer faster charging, smarter designs, and even multi-device convenience. In this post, I’ve listed the top five third-party Apple Watch chargers that perfectly suit your desk setup and travel kit.

Table of Contents
  • How to Choose the Right Apple Watch Charger
  • 5 Best Apple Watch Chargers
    • 1. ￼Satechi Apple Watch Magnetic Charging Cable
    • 2. Belkin Portable USB-C Apple Watch Charger
    • 3. Anker MagGo UFO 3-in-1 Charger
    • 4. UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 3-in-1 Foldable Charger Stand
    • 5. Nomad Universal Charging Cable
  • Which Apple Watch Charger Should You Buy?

How to Choose the Right Apple Watch Charger

Before buying a new Apple Watch charger, it’s worth taking a few seconds to assess your lifestyle and charging habits. Third-party Apple Watch chargers come in several styles and configurations, and your ideal pick depends on how and where you plan to use it:

  • Charging speed: Look for fast-charging support when paired with a 20W or higher USB-C adapter.
  • Portability: Pick a compact or foldable design if you travel frequently.
  • Multi-device setup: Choose a multi-device charging station if you also need to charge your iPhone or AirPods simultaneously.
  • Certification: Always choose MFi-certified chargers for safe, efficient performance.
  • Build quality: Assess the cable’s sturdiness, the magnet’s stability, and the overall quality if you want long-term reliability.
  • Power source: Check if it includes a USB-C connector or requires a separate wall adapter.

5 Best Apple Watch Chargers

Now that you know the key points to keep in mind before buying an Apple Watch charger, here’s a comprehensive list of Apple Watch chargers that perfectly fit different routines, spaces, and charging needs:

1. Satechi Apple Watch Magnetic Charging Cable

The Satechi Apple Watch charging cable looks like a replica of Apple’s original, only smaller and more compact. You can use it with a wall adapter or directly with your MacBook, iPad, or even iPhone, making it a perfect choice for users who prefer a clean setup without bulky docks.

The braided cable resists tangles and fraying, while the magnetic puck aligns perfectly with your watch and supports fast charging.

2. Belkin Portable USB-C Apple Watch Charger

If you’re after portability, the Belkin BoostCharge Portable USB-C Charger is perfect. It even fits in your pocket. The charger features a no-cable design and plugs directly into your MacBook, iPad, or even iPhone.

It supports fast charging for Apple Watch Series 7 and later models, charging your watch from 0 to 80% in about 45 minutes. All this makes it the ideal choice for travelers and users who need top-ups on the go.

3. Anker MagGo UFO 3-in-1 Charger

If you own multiple Apple devices, the Anker MagGo UFO 3-in-1 Charger is a space-saving powerhouse. It charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously in a modern, round design that looks great on any nightstand.

It’s MagSafe-compatible, ensuring perfect alignment for your iPhone, and provides steady magnetic charging for your Apple Watch. The best part: the charger folds into a UFO shape when not in use, helping reduce clutter.

4. UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 3-in-1 Foldable Charger Stand

The UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 3-in-1 Foldable Charger Station is an excellent all-in-one option for those who want value and flexibility. It supports Qi2 fast charging and powers your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously.

Its foldable design makes it perfect for travel, and UGREEN’s built-in safety protections prevent overheating and overcurrent. This charger strikes the right balance between performance and portability.

5. Nomad Universal Charging Cable

The Nomad Universal Charging Cable combines versatility with craftsmanship. It’s a braided USB-C cable with an integrated Apple Watch magnetic puck, letting you charge both your watch and other devices from a single cable.

The 100W Power Delivery support allows it to handle everything from your Apple Watch to your MacBook. The high-quality materials make it ideal for travelers or minimalists who want one cable for all their devices.

Which Apple Watch Charger Should You Buy?

Here’s which of the listed options you should choose and why:

  • If you want a simple, no-fuss charger, go for Belkin’s portable charger or Satechi magnetic charging cable.
  • If you prefer a single station for all your devices, the Anker UFO and UGREEN MagFlow are unbeatable.
  • Frequent travelers should consider Belkin’s portable charger for its no-cable design and pocket-friendly build.
  • For users who prefer a minimal design, Satechi’s magnetic charging cable offers unmatched simplicity.
  • And for design enthusiasts, Nomad’s Base Station adds a premium touch to your setup.

The Apple Watch is designed to help you stay connected throughout the day, but to do so, it needs a reliable charger that can recharge it quickly. Since the Apple Watch launch back in 2015, its charging ecosystem has evolved far beyond the basic magnetic puck. You can choose one that supports fast charging, is portable for travel, or is an all-in-one solution for all your Apple gadgets.

Always invest in a reliable, MFi-certified charger from brands like Satechi, Belkin, Anker, UGREEN, and Nomad, and your Apple Watch will always be ready for your next run, meeting, or night out.

Got a charger you swear by? Drop your recommendation in the comments below.

  • Best Apple Watch bands
  • Apple Watch won’t turn on? 8 Fixes
  • How to Delete Workouts on Apple Watch

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

@graph.name: Satechi Apple Watch Magnetic Charging Cable
@graph.description: The Satechi Apple Watch charging cable looks like a replica of Apple’s original, only smaller and more compact. You can use it with a wall adapter or directly with your MacBook, iPad, or even iPhone, making it a perfect choice for users who prefer a clean setup without bulky docks.

@graph.name: Belkin Portable USB-C Apple Watch Charger
@graph.description: If you’re after portability, the Belkin BoostCharge Portable USB-C Charger is perfect. It even fits in your pocket. The charger features a no-cable design and plugs directly into your MacBook, iPad, or even iPhone.

@graph.name: Anker MagGo UFO 3-in-1 Charger
@graph.description: If you own multiple Apple devices, the Anker MagGo UFO 3-in-1 Charger is a space-saving powerhouse. It charges your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously in a modern, round design that looks great on any nightstand.

@graph.name: UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 3-in-1 Foldable Charger Stand
@graph.description: The UGREEN MagFlow Qi2 3-in-1 Foldable Charger Station is an excellent all-in-one option for those who want value and flexibility. It supports Qi2 fast charging and powers your iPhone, Apple Watch, and AirPods simultaneously.

@graph.name: Nomad Universal Charging Cable
@graph.description: The Nomad Universal Charging Cable combines versatility with craftsmanship. It’s a braided USB-C cable with an integrated Apple Watch magnetic puck, letting you charge both your watch and other devices from a single cable.

title.rendered: Best AirPods Cleaning Kits for 2026: Deep-Clean Your Buds & Case

content.rendered:
Keeping your AirPods sounding crisp isn’t just about the latest audio upgrades; it’s about properly maintaining them. Dust, earwax, and pocket lint can quietly ruin sound quality, shorten battery life, and even affect comfort. That’s why a good AirPods cleaning kit has become essential. 

In this guide, we’ve rounded up the best cleaning kits. Easy to use, safe for your device, and extremely effective, they will get your AirPods running again in minutes.

Table of Contents
  • What to Consider When Buying the Right AirPods Cleaning Kit
  • Top 5 AirPods Cleaning Tools & Kits
    • 1. Hagibis Cleaning Pen Multi‑Function Kit
    • 2. KeyBudz Air Care Cleaning Kit
    • 3. Ordilend Portable Cleaning Kit
    • 4. Belkin AirPods Cleaning Kit
    • 5. walrfid 20‑in‑1 Cleaning Kit
  • How to Clean Your AirPods Safely Using a Cleaning Kit
  • Keep Your AirPods Pristine!

What to Consider When Buying the Right AirPods Cleaning Kit

Choosing the right cleaning kit is all about safety, compatibility, and convenience. Here’s what to look for:

  • Compatibility: This ensures the tools are safe for your AirPods, mesh, grills, and charging case. Different models have delicate parts.
  • Tools Included: Look for essentials such as a soft brush, a cleaning pen, a microfiber cloth, and a safe cleaning solution. The kit should cover both earbuds and the case.
  • Safety: Avoid anything abrasive. The kit should be designed specifically for AirPods.
  • Effectiveness: It should be able to reach into small crevices, such as speaker mesh, charging ports, and inner-case corners.
  • Ease of Use: Simple tools, clear instructions, and reusable materials make frequent cleaning easy.
  • Price vs. Value: Choose a kit that makes a good balance between quality and price. Very expensive bundles are unnecessary unless they justify the price by adding value.

Top 5 AirPods Cleaning Tools & Kits

Here I have listed the best 5 cleaning kits that can help you clean the AirPods, the charging case, and ports safely. 

1. Hagibis Cleaning Pen Multi‑Function Kit

Hagibis cleaning tool has a clever three-in-one design: a soft flocking sponge for the charging case, a high-density brush for speaker holes, and a slim metal tip for crevices. So, you won’t need separate tools.  

Moreover, its compact pen-style format is easy to carry and use anytime. However, no sprays or liquids are included.  Therefore, it’s ideal only for cleaning dust and earwax. On the flip side, if you’re after deep sanitising, you’ll need to look further. 

Best for: Hagibis Cleaner Pen is lightweight, affordable, travel-friendly, and effective for the basics.

2. KeyBudz Air Care Cleaning Kit

Want to keep your earbuds and their case spotless like new? The KeyBudz Air Care Cleaning Kit is a solid, no-fuss option. Built for models like Apple AirPods and AirPods Pro, it focuses on deep-down cleaning and hygiene. 

You’ll get sticky putty pieces that lift out grime from speaker meshes and inner case corners. Then there’s a tool called UtilityStik with a precision metal tip, a bristle brush, and a microfiber swab. These loosen wax and residue. Finally, the disinfecting wet wipes and swabs focus on cleaning the exterior.  

Best for: If you use your AirPods or AirPods Pro regularly, the KeyBudz cleaning kit offers all-around maintenance on a budget.

3. Ordilend Portable Cleaning Kit

If you’re dealing with annoying charging woes, this Ordilend kit is built for that same problem space. The kit brings together a small multi-tool set designed to clean and maintain charging ports, Lightning connectors, earphone jacks and speaker meshes.  

All the tools are made from high-quality, sturdy ABS plastic. Additionally, the compact case design lets you carry the kit with you on the go. Along with the cleaning tools, you’ll get a cleaning putty and a microfiber cloth. If you use Lightning cables, this kit is a must-have. 

Best for: The Ordilend cleaning kit plays a valuable role as the port/connector specialist, along with AirPods cleaning. 

4. Belkin AirPods Cleaning Kit

The Belkin AirPods Cleaning Kit is a simple, purpose-built solution to keep your earbuds fresh, hygienic, and sounding clear. This kit comprises a gentle cleaning gel, wax softener, a precision brush, and a soft microfiber cloth. You’ll be able to clean earwax, dust, and grime without damaging fragile speaker meshes or charging contacts. 

Unlike DIY cleaning hacks, this kit is designed specifically for AirPods, ensuring safe use and reliable results. Moreover, Belkin has provided a step-by-step process in the kit package, so you’ll have no issues with cleaning. However, it’s not the cheapest option, and best for one or two deep cleans. 

Best for: If you want brand assurance and don’t mind spending on a one-time solution, go for the Belkin AirPods cleaning kit. 

5. walrfid 20‑in‑1 Cleaning Kit

If your workspace gadgets (earbuds, keyboards, charging cases, screens) start looking grimy, this walrfid 20-in-1 kit lets you clean everything in one go. It comes with a variety of tools, including a flocked sponge, a small brush, a lens/port cleaning pen, and other attachments.  

With so many delicate tools, you can easily tackle dust, lint, smudges and buildup on keyboards, earbuds, screens and cases. However, if you’re only focused on cleaning the earbuds, a more focused kit might suffice and be simpler. 

Best for: This Walrfid 20-in-1 kit offers the broadest coverage and more specialised cleaning options.

How to Clean Your AirPods Safely Using a Cleaning Kit

With the right cleaning kit, you can easily make your AirPods spotless and improve sound quality. Here’s a simple, safe process to follow, whether you’re using the Belkin, Hagibis, Ordilend, warlfid, or KeyBudz cleaning kits from our list. 

  1. Wipe off any visible dust with a dry microfiber cloth.
  2. Use a soft brush from the kit to gently loosen debris around the speaker mesh.
  3. If your kit includes cleaning putty or sticky pads, press them lightly over the mesh to lift out stubborn wax or lint.
  4. Use the flocked sponge to clean the inside of the charging slots and hinge area.
  5. Gently clean out dust or lint from the Lightning or USB-C port with a metal or plastic cleaning pen.

Make cleaning AirPods a monthly ritual. A 5-minute clean keeps them looking new, ensures clear sound, and prevents charging issues. You can also use AirPods case covers for more protection. 

Keep Your AirPods Pristine! 

That’s all! A good AirPods cleaning kit helps prevent muffled sound, poor charging, and bacteria buildup that come with daily use. A quick clean takes only a few minutes but makes a huge difference in sound clarity and comfort. 

Whether you choose a premium kit like Belkin, a compact tool like Hagibis, or an all-in-one option like walrfid, they keep your earbuds fresh and functioning like new. 

Do you use any other tools to clean your AirPods? Let me know in the comments below!

@graph.description: Hagibis cleaning tool has a clever three-in-one design: a soft flocking sponge for the charging case, a high-density brush for speaker holes, and a slim metal tip for crevices.

@graph.name: KeyBudz Air Care Cleaning Kit
@graph.description: You’ll get sticky putty pieces that lift out grime from speaker meshes and inner case corners. Then there’s a tool called UtilityStik with a precision metal tip, a bristle brush, and a microfiber swab. These loosen wax and residue. Finally, the disinfecting wet wipes and swabs focus on cleaning the exterior.

@graph.name: Ordilend Portable Cleaning Kit
@graph.description: The kit brings together a small multi-tool set designed to clean and maintain charging ports, Lightning connectors, earphone jacks and speaker meshes. @graph.name: Belkin AirPods Cleaning Kit
@graph.description: This kit comprises a gentle cleaning gel, wax softener, a precision brush, and a soft microfiber cloth. You’ll be able to clean earwax, dust, and grime without damaging fragile speaker meshes or charging contacts.

@graph.name: walrfid 20‑in‑1 Cleaning Kit
@graph.description: It comes with a variety of tools, including a flocked sponge, a small brush, a lens/port cleaning pen, and other attachments. With so many delicate tools, you can easily tackle dust, lint, smudges and buildup on keyboards, earbuds, screens and cases.

title.rendered: How to Zip and Unzip Files and Folders on Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What zipping does on a Mac: Compressing files into a .zip archive reduces their size and groups them together for easier sharing and storage, without losing any data.
  • Why creating ZIP files is useful: Zipping helps save disk space, speeds up file transfers, keeps content organized, and maintains folder hierarchy during sharing.
  • How to zip and unzip using Finder: Right-click files or folders in Finder and select Compress to create a ZIP file; double-click any ZIP to extract its contents.
  • Using Terminal for advanced control: Run commands like zip -r to create archives or unzip to extract them, offering more customization and automation options.
  • Creating password-protected ZIP files: Use the Terminal command zip -er to encrypt archives with a password, securing sensitive data during transfers.

Zipping and unzipping files is one of those simple yet essential tasks that both beginner and seasoned Mac users should know how to do. It helps you organize projects, share multiple files in one package, and save valuable storage space.

The good part is that you don’t need any complicated third-party apps, as your Mac has everything you need. From Finder to Archive Utility to Terminal, there are several quick and reliable ways to manage ZIP files on a Mac. This post details how to zip and unzip files and folders on your Mac.

Table of Contents
  • What Does Zipping a File or Folder Do on a Mac?
  • Benefits of Creating Zip Files or Folders on Your Mac
  • How to Zip and Unzip Files on a Mac Using Finder
    • Zip Files Using Finder:
    • Unzip Files Using Finder:
  • How to Zip and Unzip Files Using Terminal
    • Zip Files Using Terminal:
    • Unzip Files Using Terminal:
  • How to Create a Password-Protected ZIP File
  • How to Zip and Unzip Files Using Archive Utility
    • Zip Files Using Archive Utility:
    • Unzip Files Using Archive Utility:
  • Your Mac, Your Workflow…

What Does Zipping a File or Folder Do on a Mac?

When you zip a file or folder on a Mac, macOS compresses its contents into a single archive with the .zip extension. This process reduces the overall file size and bundles multiple items into one package for easier sharing or storage.

The compressed file contains all the original data, but in a more efficient format. When you unzip it, macOS restores the files exactly as they were, without any loss of quality or structure.

Zipping is handled automatically by the built-in Archive Utility, which uses standard ZIP compression that’s fully compatible with Windows, Linux, and other operating systems.

Benefits of Creating Zip Files or Folders on Your Mac

Zipping files on your Mac has several practical advantages:

  • Saves storage space: You get more disk space or can store more files on external drives, as compression reduces file size.
  • Simplifies sharing: Sending one ZIP file is faster and easier than sending multiple attachments or folders.
  • Keeps files organized: You can package related documents, images, or projects together for easy access later.
  • Speeds up uploads and backups: Smaller archives transfer faster to cloud services like iCloud Drive, Google Drive, or Dropbox.
  • Preserves structure: Zipping keeps the folder hierarchy intact, so everything stays organized when the recipient unzips it.

How to Zip and Unzip Files on a Mac Using Finder

The Finder offers the fastest and easiest way to zip and unzip files on a Mac without involving any technical steps. Here’s how:

Zip Files Using Finder:

  1. Open Finder and head to the folder containing the file or subfolder you want to compress.
  2. Now, Control-click the item and select Compress [File Name] or Compress if you’ve selected multiple files in the drop-down menu.
  3. Once done, macOS will create a new .zip file in the same location.

Your original file or folder remains untouched; you can keep or delete it if you want. The created .zip file has the same name as your original file. You can rename it later if you want.

Note If you select multiple files, macOS names the new archive “Archive.zip” by default.

Unzip Files Using Finder:

Unzipping files or folders on a Mac is as easy as zipping them. Here’s how:

  1. Locate the .zip file or folder you want to unzip, then double-click it.
  2. Once done, macOS will extract the contents into a new folder next to the original archive.

How to Zip and Unzip Files Using Terminal

For users who prefer precision and flexibility, macOS includes Terminal commands that give more control over how files are zipped and unzipped.

Zip Files Using Terminal:

  1. Open Terminal.
  2. Here, type in “cd” and drag & drop the folder that contains the file or subfolder you want to compress in the Terminal window and hit Return. This ensures you’re in the right directory before compressing.
  3. Now enter the following Terminal command code: zip -r ArchiveName.zip FolderName
    • Replace ArchiveName with the name you want for the ZIP file.
    • Replace FolderName with the exact name of the folder (case-sensitive).
  4. Press Return, and the Terminal will create the ZIP file or folder in your current directory.

Unzip Files Using Terminal:

  1. Open Terminal, type in “cd“, enter the folder path, and hit Return.
  2. Now, enter the command: unzip ArchiveName.zip
  3. Press the Return key.

The unzipped file will appear in the same directory; just ensure the original file is no longer there. Otherwise, the “replace Images/.DS_Store? [y]es, [n]o, [A]ll, [N]one, [r]ename:” prompt will appear asking whether you want to:

  • Overwrite any existing file.
  • Extract, but do not overwrite existing files.
  • Overwrite all existing files automatically without asking again.
  • Skip all existing files, leaving them unchanged.
  • Rename the extracted file to prevent overwriting the existing one.

How to Create a Password-Protected ZIP File

While Finder offers the fastest way to zip files, it cannot create encrypted ZIP archives. That’s where Terminal proves most useful, as it lets you create encrypted ZIP archives. Here’s how:

  1. Open Terminal, type in “cd“, enter the folder path and hit Return.
  2. Now enter the command: zip -er ProtectedFolder.zip FolderName
  3. Replace SecureArchive with the name you want for the password-protected ZIP file.
  4. Replace FolderName with the exact name of the folder (case-sensitive).
  5. Press Return.
  6. Enter the desired password, then press Return.

How to Zip and Unzip Files Using Archive Utility

Archive Utility is the built-in macOS tool that handles all compression and extraction tasks. It works quietly in the background whenever you create or open ZIP files using Finder. You can also use it directly, although it doesn’t have a visible interface.

Zip Files Using Archive Utility:

  1. Open Archive Utility on your Mac. The app will appear in your Dock but won’t display a window.
  2. Now, simply drag and drop the file or folder you want to compress onto its Dock icon.
  3. A ZIP file is instantly created in the same folder as the original item.

Unzip Files Using Archive Utility:

The fastest way to unzip a file on a Mac is still by double-clicking it. But, if you want to do so via Archive Utility, all you need to do is drag and drop the Zip file onto its Dock icon, and the app automatically expands the file into the same folder.

Your Mac, Your Workflow…

Now you know how straightforward it is to zip and unzip files on a Mac. In addition to the methods mentioned earlier, you can use third-party apps such as Keka or The Unarchiver to compress files and save them more effectively.

Have you tried using Terminal or Archive Utility for file compression? Tell us which method works best for you in the comments below.

Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

keyPoints.title: What Does Zipping a File or Folder Do on a Mac?
keyPoints.explanation: Zipping compresses files into a single .zip archive, reducing size and making sharing and storage easier, while unzipping restores files without any loss of data.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Creating Zip Files or Folders on Your Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Zipping saves storage space, simplifies sharing, keeps files organized, speeds up transfers, and preserves folder structure.

keyPoints.title: How to Zip and Unzip Files on a Mac Using Finder
keyPoints.explanation: Use Finder by right-clicking files or folders to compress them into ZIP files, and double-click ZIP files to unzip and extract contents.

keyPoints.title: How to Zip and Unzip Files Using Terminal
keyPoints.explanation: Terminal offers precise control through commands like 'zip -r' for creating ZIP files and 'unzip' for extracting, suitable for advanced users seeking flexibility.

keyPoints.title: How to Create a Password-Protected ZIP File
keyPoints.explanation: Terminal can be used with the 'zip -er' command to create encrypted ZIP archives, adding a password for secure file sharing.

title.rendered: Google Photos Expands AI Editing to iPhone With ‘Help Me Edit’ and Global ‘Ask Photos’

content.rendered:
Google is enhancing its Photos app with AI tools now available on iOS, including the interactive ‘Help Me Edit’ feature and the worldwide introduction of ‘Ask Photos.’ Originally, these updates aim to make personalizing photo edits more intuitive across platforms.

‘Help Me Edit’ Lands on iOS With Customized AI Capabilities

Following its Android introduction, the conversational editing tool ‘Help Me Edit’ is now live for iPhone and iPad users in the United States. Within the Photos app, users will find a revamped editor featuring a text field called “Help me edit” at the bottom when they tap Edit on a photo. This feature simplifies multi-step editing by allowing users to describe desired changes in ordinary language.

For instance, you can type phrases like, “Remove the glare from the glasses, brighten the sky, and make everyone smile.” The AI processes these instructions and applies the edits automatically. According to Google, this tech can even use private face groups to refine results, like adjusting expressions in group photos.

Additionally, the update introduces the Nano Banana model, which facilitates artistic edits. This model supports imaginative requests such as “make this look like a watercolor painting” or “turn it into a comic book cover.” A new Create with AI carousel in the Create tab offers ready-made prompts like “turn me into a magazine cover” or “create a holiday portrait.” The update begins its rollout in the US and India for Android next week, with iOS soon to follow.

‘Ask Photos’ Rolls Out to Over 100 Countries in 17 Languages

Initially launched in the US earlier this year, ‘Ask Photos’—Google Photos’ AI-driven search tool—is now expanding globally. The introduction of the Ask tab replaces the old Search tab, enabling users to perform natural language searches such as, “Show me pictures of my cat playing in the garden” or “Find my graduation photos.”

With enhanced context understanding, ‘Ask Photos‘ retrieves relevant images quickly, eliminating the need for manual scrolling. Google confirms that the tool is reaching more than 100 countries and will support 17 languages.

A new Ask button is also part of the update, available directly while viewing any image. Positioned between “Edit” and “Add to,” this button is marked with a Gemini icon. Clicking it provides an instant description of the photo and opens a conversation box for follow-up questions or editing requests.

Introducing Smarter AI Templates Soon

In the coming weeks, Google plans to deploy personalized AI templates that draw from insights about user habits or preferences based on their photo history, such as favorite pastimes. This feature could enable users to request, “Make a sketch of me hiking” or “Create a cartoon of me and my pet,” paving the way for more customized edits.

Google Photos is shifting from a simple storage solution to a dynamic AI assistant capable of arranging, understanding, and editing images through straightforward dialogue.

Are these changes important to you? Tell us what you think!

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

title.rendered: Apple Delays iPhone Air 2, Targets 2027 Redesign

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly postponing the iPhone Air 2 launch, aiming for a major redesign to win over consumers. According to a report from The Information, Apple has informed its engineers and partners that the next iPhone Air is off the production schedule without a set release date.

Apple Halts iPhone Air 2 Development

Originally set for a fall 2026 debut alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and the rumored iPhone Fold, the iPhone Air 2 has been removed from Apple’s schedule altogether, based on insights shared by The Information. However, it’s not completely shelved. Engineers and some manufacturing partners are said to continue their work behind the scenes.

The delay seems to stem from Apple’s decision to overhaul the iPhone Air 2 to enhance its appeal after disappointing sales of the first-generation model. Plans for the redesign reportedly include the addition of a second rear camera, a feature users felt was lacking in the original iPhone Air.

Revamp Eyes Spring 2027 Release

There are hopes among Apple engineers that the revamped iPhone Air 2 could launch in spring 2027, possibly alongside the base iPhone 18 and the budget-friendly iPhone 18e. Yet, the timeline remains uncertain, leaving some speculation in its wake.

Initially, Apple envisioned the iPhone Air 2 as a lighter version with an increased battery capacity and a vapor chamber cooling system, a feature initially introduced in the iPhone 17 Pro. These planned enhancements were meant to boost performance while maintaining the slim and lightweight profile that marked the original iPhone Air.

Production Slows Amid Lackluster Demand

As reported by The Information, Apple’s manufacturing allies, Foxconn and Luxshare, have already cut back production of the current iPhone Air due to tepid demand. Foxconn has dismantled most of its production setups, with assembly expected to cease by November. Luxshare already stopped production in October.

This strategic pivot echoes Apple’s past responses to underwhelming sales of models like the iPhone mini and iPhone Plus, suggesting a wider pattern of adjusting strategies based on market demand.

Uncommon Choice for Apple’s iPhone Roadmap

Apple’s decision to pull a product from its launch plans after entering production is decidedly rare, marking this as a noteworthy deviation. The move implies a strategic pullback as Apple reassesses its iPhone lineup expansion, prioritizing the refinement of the Air series before committing to further releases.

If this plan prevails, Apple’s 2026 lineup will likely consist of just three models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Fold, with the refreshed iPhone Air 2 arriving in 2027.

Would a redesigned iPhone Air 2 matter to you? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple hits pause on iPhone Air 2, eyeing a bold 2027 comeback with a redesigned model aimed at reigniting consumer interest.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

title.rendered: Apple Introduces Limited Edition iPhone Pocket with Issey Miyake

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple debuts the limited-edition iPhone Pocket: Created with the Issey Miyake studio, this rare accessory blends art and utility in a minimalist design.
  • Fashion meets functionality in a 3D-knit design: The iPhone Pocket uses stretchable fabric to hold an iPhone and small essentials, worn crossbody, over the shoulder, or around the wrist.
  • Two strap versions with vibrant color options: Available in short strap ($149.95) and long strap ($229.95) models, offering users flexible styling choices.
  • Apple’s first direct-to-retail limited edition release: Marks a shift in Apple’s retail strategy, making exclusive collaborations available directly through Apple Stores.
  • Global launch with limited availability: The iPhone Pocket arrives this Friday in select regions including the US, UK, France, China, Italy, Japan, Singapore, and South Korea.

Apple has introduced a new limited edition accessory for the iPhone called the iPhone Pocket, marking one of the few times the company has described a product as a limited release.

Designed in collaboration with the Issey Miyake design studio, known for crafting Steve Jobs’ famous black turtleneck, the iPhone Pocket reimagines the charm of the 2004 iPod Socks in a modern, fashion-forward form. The accessory uses a single 3D-knitted stretchable cloth to create a sleek, wearable pocket that can hold an iPhone along with other small items.

The iPhone Pocket can be worn in multiple ways, such as over the shoulder, around the wrist, or attached to a handbag. The fabric stretches enough to let users peek at the iPhone’s screen without fully removing it.

Apple is offering the iPhone Pocket in two versions:

  • Short strap version priced at $149.95, available in lemon, mandarin, purple, pink, peacock, sapphire, cinnamon, and black.
  • Long strap version priced at $229.95, available in sapphire, cinnamon, and black.

This launch appears to be the first limited edition accessory ever sold directly through Apple’s retail stores. In the past, Apple has offered seasonal or brand collaborations such as Hermès Apple Watch bands, but these were never marketed as limited-time releases.

Availability

The iPhone Pocket will be available this Friday in select regions, including the US, UK, France, China, Italy, Japan, Singapore, and South Korea. It will also be displayed in a small number of Apple Stores.

With the iPhone Pocket, Apple is once again merging fashion and technology, offering a collectible piece that reflects both style and innovation.

What do you think of Apple’s new iPhone Pocket design? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple has introduced the iPhone Pocket, a limited edition 3D-knitted accessory made with Issey Miyake’s design team. It’s a stylish, flexible pocket for your iPhone that comes in multiple colors and strap options.

mainEntity.name: Do AirTags interfere with credit cards?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AirTags use Bluetooth and Ultra-Wideband signals that operate on completely different frequencies than credit card chips or their magnetic strips. Apple designed them to be safe next to cards. Just ensure the AirTag isn’t pressing too hard on the card’s surface to prevent physical wear.

keyPoints.title: Apple Introduces Limited Edition iPhone Pocket
keyPoints.explanation: Apple has launched a new, limited-edition accessory called the iPhone Pocket, designed in collaboration with the Issey Miyake studio, emphasizing its rarity and unique appeal.

keyPoints.title: Design Inspired by Fashion and Functionality
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone Pocket features a sleek, 3D-knitted stretchable fabric capable of holding an iPhone and small items, worn in various ways such as over the shoulder or around the wrist.

keyPoints.title: Multiple Versions and Price Points**
keyPoints.explanation: Available in short strap ($149.95) and long strap ($229.95) versions, the accessory comes in various vibrant colors, offering flexibility and style options for users.

keyPoints.title: First Direct-to-Retail Limited Edition Accessory**
keyPoints.explanation: This marks the first time Apple has sold a limited-edition accessory directly through its retail stores, setting a new precedent for exclusive product releases.

keyPoints.title: Availability and Regions**
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone Pocket will launch this Friday in select regions including the US, UK, France, China, Italy, Japan, Singapore, and South Korea, with a limited presence in Apple Stores.

title.rendered: Affinity vs Photoshop: Canva’s Free Design Suite Tested

content.rendered:
Affinity just did something bold. Canva’s newly acquired design suite has merged all three of its apps: Affinity Photo, Affinity Designer, and Affinity Publisher into one unified platform. And the best part? It’s completely free. You can now edit photos, design graphics, and lay out documents inside a single app that feels professional, fast, and surprisingly bug-free.

No wonder everyone’s asking: is this the time to ditch Photoshop and its expensive monthly plan? I wondered the same. So I spent a week using both. Here’s what I found.

Table of Contents
  • Affinity App vs Photoshop: Quick Verdict
  • All-in-One Workflow: How the New Affinity App Works
  • Switching from Photoshop to Affinity: Key Workflow Differences
  • Ease of Use: How Affinity Compares to Photoshop for Beginners
  • Performance Test: Affinity vs Photoshop Speed and Stability
  • Pricing Showdown: Free Affinity App vs Photoshop Subscription
  • File Support and Ecosystem: Affinity vs Photoshop Compatibility
  • Final Verdict: Can the Free Affinity App Replace Photoshop in 2025?

Affinity App vs Photoshop: Quick Verdict

For 90% of everyday edits and design work, Affinity gets the job done. It feels fast, polished, and intuitive. You can retouch photos, design posters, or even prepare print layouts without hitting a paywall. But Photoshop still leads when it comes to:

  • Advanced AI tools like generative fill, harmonize, and depth-based editing.
  • Cloud sync and collaboration, which are deeply integrated into Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Plugin ecosystem, where Photoshop still offers unmatched third-party support.

Still, for anyone who doesn’t need every pro-level automation, Affinity now feels like a serious Photoshop replacement.

All-in-One Workflow: How the New Affinity App Works

Affinity’s biggest change is its all-in-one interface. The app has three “studios” you can switch between: Vector (for illustration), Pixel (for photo editing), and Layout (for publishing). It’s like getting Photoshop, Illustrator, and InDesign combined.

Each studio shares the same smooth interface. Switching between vector graphics and raster edits feels instant, no exporting, no lag. Even tools like object selection, inpainting (content-aware remove), and layer masks feel familiar if you’ve used Photoshop before. And just like Photoshop, it is also layered based editing if you are wondering. 

Photoshop, meanwhile, continues to expand its AI lineup. Adobe’s Firefly, Gemini, and Flux models now power things like smarter background removal, text-based editing, and the new Harmonize tool that matches lighting across images. Affinity also has Canva AI, however, it’s no close to what Photoshop is offering right now.

So if you work does not revolve around using these smart AI tools, your switch to Affinity will be smooth. And I would argue, few features like refining edges with brush, etc are actually better on Affinity than on Photoshop. 

Switching from Photoshop to Affinity: Key Workflow Differences

Small differences matter when you’re fast at Photoshop. Here are the ones that may trip you and how to adjust.

  • Clipping masks: In Photoshop, you clip the upper layer to the lower. In Affinity, create the fill layer below the target, then right‑click the target layer to create the clipping mask. Muscle memory fix: think “mask onto the layer I want.”
  • Gradients on fills: Photoshop creates a fill layer when you draw a gradient. In Affinity, create the Fill Layer first, then draw the gradient on it. Shapes already act as fill layers, so you can draw gradients directly on shapes—often simpler.
  • Live shapes: Affinity shapes stay “live” with on‑canvas orange handles and top‑bar options until you Convert to Curves. After converting, you edit every node like a pro, but lose the quick live controls.
  • Destructive tools: Background Erase, Flood Erase, Sponge, etc., can be destructive. Prefer masks, adjustment layers, and live filters when possible.
  • Occasional quirks: Rare UI hiccups with Fill Layers/gradients can be fixed by creating a new document and pasting layers across.

Ease of Use: How Affinity Compares to Photoshop for Beginners

This is where Affinity shines. Free tools like GIMP or Krita often feel cluttered or confusing. Affinity, in contrast, feels modern and easy to grasp.

Every slider and option is clear, and the workspace can be customized to match Photoshop’s layout almost perfectly. Even the default layout is pretty much close too. 

Even advanced tools like gradients, clipping masks, and path editing are logically organized. The live preview on tools like the shape builder and vector brushes feels responsive and immediate. 

Photoshop still wins in terms of depth. For example, if you’re doing 3D textures, advanced retouching, or massive batch editing. But for anyone working on web content, thumbnails, or social media designs, Affinity feels lighter and faster.

Performance Test: Affinity vs Photoshop Speed and Stability

In real use, Affinity feels snappy. I opened large RAW files and layered PSDs without slowdowns. The object selection worked nearly as fast as Photoshop’s AI-based one, and basic brushes and filters responded instantly. The app runs fully offline after a one-time Canva login, which means no cloud dependencies.

Photoshop is still smoother with high-end tasks, especially AI generation, color matching, or when using hardware acceleration on GPUs. But if you’re editing on a laptop or integrated graphics, Affinity’s performance feels more optimized and lighter.

Pricing Showdown: Free Affinity App vs Photoshop Subscription

Here’s the real shocker: Affinity is completely free. You just need a Canva account to activate it. All the editing tools, export options, and vector/pixel/layout studios are included. Only certain AI features like depth maps, colorization, and generative edit require Canva Premium ($15/month).

Photoshop, in contrast, starts at $22.99/month for just one app or $70/month for the full Creative Cloud suite. Even with discounts, you’re tied to a yearly plan, and canceling early costs extra.

If you only need Photoshop’s generative fill occasionally, Affinity’s model is far more flexible. You can work free all year, then activate Canva Premium for a month when you need AI tools.

File Support and Ecosystem: Affinity vs Photoshop Compatibility

Affinity can open and export PSD files, so you can move your old Photoshop projects over. It supports both Windows and macOS, and an iPad version is coming soon. The only missing piece? Linux support, which Adobe also lacks.  For now, Linux users have to rely on Wine or virtualization.

Photoshop still benefits from tight integration with Adobe’s apps, Lightroom, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, and Express. That ecosystem remains valuable for teams and pros working across media types.

Final Verdict: Can the Free Affinity App Replace Photoshop in 2025?

After a week with both, I’m convinced: Affinity finally feels like a real Photoshop alternative. It’s not perfect, but it’s close enough for almost everyone who isn’t working in large-scale professional environments. It’s fast, clean, and capable. And the fact that it’s free makes it almost impossible to ignore.

Photoshop will always be the industry giant. But if you’re tired of subscriptions and just want to create, edit, and design without limits, Affinity is the best free tool you can download right now.

  • Whoop vs Apple Watch: Which Fitness Tracker Wins in 2025?
