title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro May Feature One New Color Option

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple may drop black from iPhone 18 Pro palette as it tests burgundy, brown, and purple for a single new Pro-exclusive color.
  • Burgundy would mark a red-toned first for Pro models, standing apart from standard iPhones’ bright (PRODUCT)RED finishes.
  • Brown would be an entirely new shade for Apple, while purple could echo iPhone 14 Pro’s Deep Purple with a slight update.
  • Color shake-up continues Apple’s trend toward bold tones, following iPhone 17 Pro’s Silver, Cosmic Orange, and Deep Blue lineup.
  • Leaks come from a mixed-reliability source, so these iPhone 18 Pro color options remain speculative with plenty of time for changes.

Apple is reportedly in the midst of deciding on a new color palette for its upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max, but only one final shade may come into play. This speculation originates from Instant Digital, a prominent leaker on Weibo with a mixed but noteworthy record when it comes to Apple predictions.

Apple Reportedly Testing Burgundy, Brown, and Purple

The latest leak suggests Apple is trying out three potential hues: burgundy, brown, and purple. These shades would be reserved for the Pro and Pro Max models of the iPhone 18 series, anticipated to debut in September 2026. However, the leaker later noted that just one of these colors is expected to go into production. While specific details on the exact tones are scarce, concept images on social media offer a glimpse of the possibilities. A burgundy choice would introduce a red-toned option to the Pro lineup for the first time, differing from the bright (PRODUCT)RED seen on standard models. The brown option, should it be selected, would be entirely new territory for Apple. As for purple, it would echo the Deep Purple of the iPhone 14 Pro, albeit with a possible twist.

No Black Model This Time?

Along with these potential new finishes, there’s a suggestion that Apple may forego a black option altogether for the iPhone 18 Pro series. This aligns with the design choices of the iPhone 17 Pro lineup, which came in Silver, Cosmic Orange, and Deep Blue, favoring bold, jewel-toned colors over traditional ones like graphite or space black. Apple has been shifting towards these more vibrant metallic hues for its Pro models, signifying a trend that might continue with the iPhone 18 Pro, should one of these darker new shades take center stage in place of black.

Track Record of the Leaker

Instant Digital has previously provided accurate information regarding Apple products, such as the Yellow iPhone 14, the frosted back glass of the iPhone 15, and the Titanium Milanese Loop for the Apple Watch Ultra 2. Nonetheless, not all leaks have hit the mark, so it’s wise to consider this color rumor plausible yet unverified. Given the lengthy lead time before Apple’s next Pro models hit shelves, the company’s design decisions could still pivot. Nevertheless, this early insight into potential color offerings suggests Apple is maintaining its trajectory toward luxury-oriented finishes for its premium smartphones.

Would Apple’s potential color overhaul catch your interest? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple may replace black with a new Pro-only hue on the iPhone 18 Pro, testing burgundy, brown, and purple finishes for its 2026 lineup.

title.rendered: WhatsApp Arrives on Apple Watch: Key Details

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • WhatsApp now fully supports Apple Watch with a dedicated app that offers messaging, emoji reactions, voice notes, and media previews without using your iPhone.
  • Full chat access replaces limited notifications, letting you scroll entire conversations, send messages, and view stickers and images directly on the watch.
  • Call alerts and chat history are now visible, giving you real-time caller ID and a more complete record of past messages than the old mirrored alerts.
  • Works on Apple Watch Series 4 or newer running watchOS 10+, but still requires your iPhone nearby for syncing and connectivity.
  • Watch out for cellular model limitations — the app isn’t fully standalone yet, so remote use without your iPhone isn’t supported (but may come later).

Meta’s WhatsApp has officially arrived on Apple Watch, marking the end of its previously limited capabilities on the wearable. The fully-featured app is now available to download by all users following a brief beta period through TestFlight.

A Full Chat Experience on Apple Watch

Apple Watch users were previously restricted to reading and replying to notifications mirrored from their iPhones. This new official app changes that. In a report by Engadget, Meta notes that the app introduces a host of sought-after features, providing a more comprehensive chatting experience directly from the watch.

Users can now scroll through entire conversations, including long ones, without needing their iPhones. The app enables sending written messages, recording and sending voice notes, reacting with emojis, and viewing images and stickers more clearly on the watch.

Call Notifications and Chat History

Besides messaging, call notifications are now accessible, indicating who’s calling, which lets users decide swiftly whether to pick up their phone. The app also offers an extended view of chat history, overcoming limitations of earlier mirrored notifications.

Meta reassures that end-to-end encryption remains active for all communications through the Apple Watch app, maintaining user privacy and security.

Compatibility and Installation

Per TechRadar, the new WhatsApp app works with Apple Watch Series 4 and newer running watchOS 10 or later. Users need their iPhone nearby with the latest version of WhatsApp for proper syncing and connection.

To get the app, users can search WhatsApp in the App Store directly from their Apple Watch, or use the Watch app on their iPhone, navigate to the My Watch tab, find WhatsApp, and proceed with installation.

Why It Matters

The launch signifies a significant advancement for WhatsApp’s utility on wearables. Although messaging apps like Telegram and Messenger already offered dedicated Apple Watch apps, WhatsApp was lagging for years. Now, Apple Watch users can finally enjoy similar interactions and convenience that Android smartwatch users have had.

Meta has hinted that additional features are on the horizon, potentially introducing standalone app support for cellular Apple Watch models, which would enhance WhatsApp’s usability on the go.

How do you feel about this new WhatsApp feature on the Apple Watch? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: WhatsApp finally arrives on Apple Watch with full chat access, voice notes, emoji reactions, and media previews, bringing true messaging freedom to your wrist.

title.rendered: What’s New in the Phone App with iOS 26

content.rendered:
The humble Phone app that almost never gets any new features, finally got the complete redesign it deserves in iOS 26. And from a usage perspective, we really like everything about the new Liquid Glass design style, the useful AI features that handle spam calls, etc. In the article, we will dive into all the features Apple introduced in iOS 26, so you can take advantage of all of these new features.

Table of Contents
  • 1. A Fresh Unified Design
  • 2. Pin Your Favorites
  • 3. Call Screening Takes Over Unknown Calls
  • 4. Hold Assist Waits So You Don’t Have To
  • 5. AI-Powered Live Translation and Voicemail Summaries
  • 6. Call Filtering for Unknown Numbers
  • 7. SharePlay Over Phone Calls
  • 8. Personalized Monograms and Contact Posters
  • 9. Better Call Quality
  • Bonus: New Ringtones and Cross-Device Support
  • Final Thoughts

1. A Fresh Unified Design

The first thing you’ll notice is the new unified layout. Apple has merged the Recents, Favorites, and Voicemail tabs into one single screen called Calls. It’s cleaner, more organized, and fits right in with the new Liquid Glass aesthetic that gives iOS 26 its translucent, glossy finish. Your favorite contacts appear at the top, followed by your recent calls, voicemails, and missed numbers, all in one scrollable view.

The bottom navigation bar is simplified too, now showing only Calls, Contacts, Keypad, and Search. A small three-line icon at the top-right corner replaces extra tabs, giving you quick access to voicemail and other settings.

If you’re not a fan of change, Apple’s got you covered. You can switch back to the old tabbed interface any time by tapping the menu icon and selecting Classic view. The Phone app will immediately revert to the familiar iOS 18-style layout,  and yes, you can switch back again whenever you want.

2. Pin Your Favorites

You can now pin your most important contacts at the top of the unified Calls tab. Simply tap Edit > Edit Favorites, then add numbers, FaceTime contacts, or even message shortcuts. There’s no strict limit on how many you can pin, though more than six will be hidden behind a Show All button.

3. Call Screening Takes Over Unknown Calls

One of the most practical additions is Call Screening. When you get a call from an unknown number, your iPhone can now pick it up for you, ask who’s calling, and display their response live on your screen. You can then decide whether to answer or ignore it; no more awkward spam calls break your focus.

It’s available in multiple languages and regions, including English (US, UK, India, Australia), French, German, Spanish, Japanese, Mandarin, and more. You can enable the feature from Settings > Apps > Phone and set Screen Unknown Callers to Ask Reason for Calling or directly to Silence.

4. Hold Assist Waits So You Don’t Have To

We’ve all been there, stuck on hold with customer support for what feels like forever. Hold Assist finally fixes that. When a call puts you on hold, your iPhone will stay on the line for you and alert you the moment a human picks up. You can keep scrolling, working, or relaxing while your iPhone listens for your turn.

This feature is rolling out in several regions, including the US, UK, Canada, India, Germany, and Japan. It’s enabled by default, and you can change it in the Settings app > Apps > Phone and enable Hold Assist Detection.

5. AI-Powered Live Translation and Voicemail Summaries

With Apple Intelligence in iOS 26, the Phone app is getting smarter. Live Translation lets you talk to people who speak different languages, translating your voice and theirs in real time. It’s powered by on-device AI for privacy and works across calls and FaceTime.

Meanwhile, your voicemails now come with short AI-generated summaries, giving you a quick idea of what the message is about without having to play it.

6. Call Filtering for Unknown Numbers

If you’d rather not even see unknown numbers, iOS 26 lets you filter them out automatically. Turn on Call Filtering in Settings > Apps > Phone, and your iPhone will quietly move unknown numbers into a separate Unknown Callers list under the More menu in the Phone app.

7. SharePlay Over Phone Calls

Apple has extended SharePlay to regular phone calls, letting you do much more than just talk. While chatting, you can now share your screen to guide someone through settings, listen to music together via Apple Music, or even watch movies in sync through supported streaming apps, all without switching to FaceTime.

It uses the same smooth SharePlay interface you’ve seen before, and everything stays synced in real time. The feature works on both Wi-Fi and cellular, and participants can control playback individually while remaining connected on the call.

8. Personalized Monograms and Contact Posters

The new Monogram styles make it easy to personalize your Contact Poster without overcomplicating things. You can pick from a few clean designs, change colors or fonts, and preview your changes before saving. Edits sync through iCloud, so your chosen look appears on all your Apple devices and when you call others. It’s a small touch that makes calls feel more personal while keeping the interface simple and elegant.

9. Better Call Quality

Voice clarity gets a real upgrade in iOS 26 thanks to high-quality cellular calling. Apple has optimized how your iPhone handles audio over both 4G and 5G networks, using enhanced codecs and better noise isolation. This means crisper, more natural voices and fewer distortions, even when the signal isn’t perfect. The improvement is especially noticeable on older or narrowband connections, giving them near-HD quality.

It’s supported on iPhone 16e and later, and users will notice clearer calls in busy areas, during weak network coverage, or when switching between Wi-Fi and cellular.

Bonus: New Ringtones and Cross-Device Support

Apple has also added seven new ringtones, including Little Bird, alongside alternate versions of the popular Reflections tone. You’ll find them under Settings > Sounds & Haptics.

Final Thoughts

I have always been divided between Pixels and iPhones. With iOS 26, Apple finally gave most of the features, especially in the phone app, that made Pixel phones exciting to me. Most spam cannot reach me; my iPhone stays on hold for me, and I can contact anyone who does not speak the language I know. These are features that actually make sense to have when you need them.

title.rendered: How to View Shared Photos in iMessage on iPhone and iPad

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • How shared photos work in iMessage: Photos exchanged through iMessage are stored in each chat’s Photos section, letting you easily view all shared media in one place.
  • Enable ‘Shared with You’ for seamless access: Turn on Shared with You in Settings → Messages to automatically view shared images in the Photos app, with controls for each contact.
  • Where to find shared iMessage photos: Open chat details to see the Photos section, or go to the Photos app → Shared with You album to browse all shared images together.
  • Fix missing shared photos on iPhone: If photos don’t appear, ensure Shared with You is enabled, indexing is complete, and iOS is updated to the latest version.
  • Keep shared media organized: Save key images right away, clear outdated ones in chat details, and use Photos app filters to search and manage shared pictures efficiently.

Looking for that vacation photo your friend sent you on iMessage, but couldn’t find it? Don’t worry, your iPhone keeps them organized in one place, so you don’t need to scroll through hundreds of messages.

In this guide, you’ll learn the easiest ways to view all the photos shared with you in iMessage, whether you want to see them in a chat or access them from your phone’s library. Let’s get started.

Table of Contents
  • What Are Shared Photos in iMessage?
  • Step 1: Set Up the Shared with You Feature for iMessage
    • Enable Automatic Sync for All Shared Photos
    • Control Sharing for Individual Contacts
  • Step 2: View iMessage Shared Photos on iPhone
    • Via iMessage
    • Access Shared Photos in the Photos App
  • Can’t See Shared Photos? Check These Settings
  • Quick Tips for Managing Shared Photos
  • Revisit Memories in iMessage!

What Are Shared Photos in iMessage?

Whenever someone sends or receives a photo through the Messages app (a.k.a. iMessage), Apple automatically keeps a record of those images in that chat’s Photos section.

In iOS 26, Apple has refined this layout, making it faster and cleaner. You can now open a chat, tap a contact’s name, and see every image exchanged in one place. 

You can also access these images directly in the Photos app under the Shared with You section. So even if you forget who sent what, iOS has you covered.

Step 1: Set Up the Shared with You Feature for iMessage

The Shared with You feature automatically collects photos your contacts send through iMessage and displays them inside your iPhone’s Photos app.

Enable Automatic Sync for All Shared Photos

  1. Open the Settings app → Tap Apps at the bottom → Choose Messages.
  2. Scroll down to and tap Shared with You.
  3. In the app list below, toggle on Photos as well as any others you’d like.

Important:

  • If you delete a conversation in Messages, any photos and videos from that thread are also deleted from the Shared with You section. 
  • To keep them permanently, save them to your Library before deleting the chat.

Control Sharing for Individual Contacts

You can choose whose photos and videos are allowed to appear in the Share with You section automatically. It allows you to avoid cluttering your gallery with unnecessary memes and images.

  1. Open the Messages app → Select a conversation with your contact. 
  2. Tap your contact’s name at the top to display their details. 
  3. Scroll down a bit and toggle on Show in Shared with You to make sure you see that contact’s shared pictures in the Photos app.
  4. Tap the left arrow at the top to exit the contact details and return to the conversation in Messages.

Step 2: View iMessage Shared Photos on iPhone

You can check the shared photos collection for a dedicated contact or all in a single album. Here’s how to do both:

Via iMessage

  1. Launch the Messages app on your iPhone and open the conversation that includes the photo(s) you want to revisit. 
  2. Tap the contact’s name (or the group chat title) at the top. This opens the chat details screen. 
  3. Move to the Photos section. Here you will see all the photos exchanged in the thread.  
  4. Now, tap any photo to view it in full screen. Else, tap and hold it to save, copy, share, or delete it.

Pro Tip: From the context menu, select Show in Conversation to jump back to the original message where the photo was sent.

Access Shared Photos in the Photos App 

If you’d rather browse all shared iMessage photos in one place, you can also do it directly in the Photos app. 

  1. Open the Photos app and ensure you are in the Library view. 
  2. Tap the three-dot icon at the top. 
  3. Select Filter from the dropdown and tap Shared with You.

It will show all the photos and videos people have sent you via Messages. Now, you can edit the photo or video, create a slideshow, make a Live Sticker, and much more.

Can’t See Shared Photos? Check These Settings 

If your shared photos aren’t appearing, don’t panic. It’s often just a setting or sync issue. 

  • Ensure Shared with You feature is enabled in Settings and individual chats.  
  • In Photos, tap the three-dot icon → View Options and select Shared with You. So, it will appear under Filter. 
  • After updating to iOS 26, your phone might take a bit to re-index all your messages and attachments. Keep your iPhone connected to Wi-Fi and plugged in. It’ll sort itself out in the background.

Quick Tips for Managing Shared Photos 

We all exchange a lot of media on iMessage every day, so the Shared with You section quickly gets cluttered. 

  • Save what matters: When someone sends an important photo or video, save it immediately. 
  • Clean up easily: Use the Photos section in chat details to bulk-delete old media from large group chats. 
  • Organize smartly: Mark favorite photos or videos directly in the Photos app for long-term storage. 
  • Smart search filter: Try searching for a person’s name and a keyword (like “Tom beach”) in the search bar, then go to the Photos section.

Revisit Memories in iMessage! 

Finding shared photos in iMessage used to mean endless scrolling, but not anymore. With iOS 26, Apple’s made it simple to browse every photo shared in a chat, all in one tidy gallery view. So, your shared memories are just a few taps away. 

Have you tried the new iMessage features in iOS 26? Let me know in the comments below!

FAQs

How to search in iMessage?

When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

Do iMessage photos get saved?

Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

Read more:

  • How to Rearrange and Delete iMessage Apps
  • iMessage not working on Mac? How to fix it!
  • How to turn off read receipts on iPhone
  • Fix Slow Wi-Fi: Speed Up iMessage Photo Sharing on iPhone

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

keyPoints.title: Shared Photos in iMessage
keyPoints.explanation: Photos sent and received through iMessage are automatically saved in the chat's Photos section, making it simple to view all exchanged images.

keyPoints.title: Enabling 'Shared with You' Feature
keyPoints.explanation: Activate the 'Shared with You' setting in Settings > Messages to seamlessly collect shared photos in your Photos app and customize sharing options per contact.

keyPoints.title: .accessing Shared Photos on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: View shared images directly within the iMessage chat details under Photos, or see all shared photos in the 'Shared with You' album in the Photos app.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Shared Photos Visibility
keyPoints.explanation: If shared photos aren’t showing up, ensure 'Shared with You' is enabled in Settings and chats, and that your device has indexed the latest iOS updates.

keyPoints.title: Tips for Managing Shared Photos
keyPoints.explanation: Save key shared images immediately, delete old media from chat details, and use search filters in Photos to organize and revisit moments easily.

title.rendered: 15 Aesthetic Thanksgiving Wallpapers for iPhone

content.rendered:
Thanksgiving is just around the corner, making it the perfect time to get festive and give your iPhone a cozy new look! If you’re searching for the perfect Thanksgiving wallpaper, you’ve come to the right place. We’ve rounded up some of the best Thanksgiving wallpapers for iPhone.

From classic autumn vibes to stylish, modern looks, there’s something for everyone to bring a touch of holiday cheer to your iPhone screen. Let the Thanksgiving decorations begin—enjoy the season!

Table of Contents
  • Best 4K Thanksgiving Wallpapers for iPhone
    • Thanksgiving Pumpkin carving wallpaper
    • Stacked Pumpkins wallpaper
    • Cute Turkey Thanksgiving themed wallpaper
    • Fall season Thanksgiving aesthetic wallpaper
    • Classic American Thanksgiving dinner wallpaper
    • Wreath of Leaves Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Corn maze Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Pumpkin patch wallpaper
    • Vintage Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Rustic Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Classic cornucopia Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Preppy Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Thanksgiving thankful wallpaper
    • Stitch Thanksgiving wallpaper
    • Snoopy and Charlie Brown Thanksgiving wallpaper
  • Happy Thanksgiving!

Best 4K Thanksgiving Wallpapers for iPhone

Get into the festive spirit with our handpicked collection of cute and stunning Thanksgiving wallpapers.

1. Thanksgiving Pumpkin Carving

Capture the essence of fall harvest and festive joy with this intricately carved pumpkin on your iPhone screen. Tap the download button to embrace the warmth of this beautiful season.

Download

2. Stacked Pumpkins

This visual feast will surely please your eyes and uplift your festive spirit whenever you unlock your iPhone. Add a touch of charm to your phone’s appearance with this delightful Thanksgiving wallpaper.

Download

3. Cute Turkey Theme

Gobble up the cuteness of Turkey with this beautifully designed wallpaper. It will surely bring a smile to your face and set a warm mood for the holidays. Tap the download button now!

Download

4. Fall Thanksgiving Aesthetic

Embrace the aesthetic beauty of rich, warm hues and delicate autumn leaves, curating a visually pleasing and calming atmosphere on your iPhone. Tap the download button to enchant your iPhone screen.

Download

5. Classic Thanksgiving Dinner

Here’s a glimpse of a traditional Thanksgiving table set with delicious Apple Pie. Mouthwatering right? Evoke a sense of togetherness and gratitude by downloading this wallpaper.

Download

6. Leaf Wreath for Thanksgiving

Looking for a dark iPhone wallpaper to celebrate Thanksgiving? Download this simple wallpaper with a lush green wreath of leaves encircled by “Happy Thanksgiving” wishes. It brings a sense of gratitude without overwhelming colors or patterns.

Download

7. Corn Maze Adventure

Visiting a corn maze on Thanksgiving has become mandatory. To get the same fall essence, download this beautiful corn maze wallpaper for your iPhone. It shows a golden cornfield at sunset, creating a cozy and rustic ambiance.

Download

8. Pumpkin Patch

Get into the autumn spirit with this vibrant pumpkin patch iPhone wallpaper! It brings the beauty of fall harvest and Thanksgiving right to your iPhone screen. Tap the download button and enjoy the charm of the countryside every time you look at your phone.

Download

9. Vintage Thanksgiving

If you love antique designs, this vintage-inspired Thanksgiving wallpaper is perfect for your iPhone. The delicate design features classic fall elements, like rustic orange pumpkins, earthy pinecones, and golden brown leaves.

Download

10. Rustic Thanksgiving

Celebrate Thanksgiving in style with this rustic iPhone wallpaper. Featuring an earthy background adorned with autumn leaves, pumpkins, and acorns, the design offers a countryside vibe. Download the wallpaper now to get the cozy essence of fall.

Download

11. Classic Cornucopia

Thanksgiving is all about having fun harvesting. This elegant Thanksgiving wallpaper showcases a classic cornucopia overflowing with autumn’s harvest, like pumpkins, apples, grapes, and corn. Tap the download button and let this wallpaper remind you of the generosity of Thanksgiving.

Download

12. Preppy Thanksgiving

This vibrant preppy Thanksgiving wallpaper brings all the warmth and coziness of fall to your iPhone screen. The minimal design includes beautiful hand-drawn pumpkins, acorns, pinecones, and golden autumn leaves, perfect for setting a festive mood.

Download

13. “Thankful” Lettering

Thanksgiving is incomplete without potluck and family dinners. This heartwarming Thanksgiving wallpaper brings the spirit of togetherness with a bountiful feast. Download the wallpaper to embrace the appreciation for family, friends, and life’s blessings.

Download

14. Stitch’s Thanksgiving

This playful wallpaper brings a tropical twist to your screen with Stitch enjoying the holiday season. Set against a dark background, the colors pop, creating a fun and relaxed vibe, perfect for any Stitch fan.

Download

15. Snoopy & Charlie Brown Thanksgiving

If you are a classic cartoon fan, download this Thanksgiving wallpaper featuring the iconic Peanuts characters Charlie Brown and Snoopy. Enjoy Thanksgiving with fun in Snoopy style!

Download

Happy Thanksgiving!

As you navigate through the digital landscape of your iPhone, let the Thanksgiving spirit accompany you with every swipe and tap. These wallpapers not only add a festive touch to your device but also serve as a daily reminder of the blessings that surround you. So, as you gather with loved ones and indulge in the season’s delights, carry a piece of Thanksgiving with you wherever you go.

Thank you for reading. Please take a moment to share your favorite design in the comment section below.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

title.rendered: How to Clear Keyboard History on iPhone and iPad

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What iPhone keyboard history stores: Your iPhone learns frequently used words and phrases to improve predictive text and typing accuracy, which can be reset anytime.
  • Why you might clear keyboard history: Removing stored words helps eliminate awkward or personal suggestions, keeping predictive text more private and relevant.
  • How to reset keyboard history on iPhone: Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Reset → Reset Keyboard Dictionary to erase all learned typing data.
  • Alternative to deleting keyboard history: Disable Auto-Correction and Predictive Text under Settings → General → Keyboard to stop word suggestions without resetting history.
  • Extra customization for typing preferences: Add or change keyboards in Settings → General → Keyboard → Keyboards to tailor your typing experience for different languages or layouts.

Have you ever had your iPhone suggest a word or phrase you wish it didn’t remember? Apple’s keyboard learns from what you type to offer better suggestions, but sometimes it picks up things you’d rather not see again.

If your keyboard predictions have gotten a little too personal or just plain annoying, it might be time to clear your keyboard history. In this guide, you’ll learn how to delete your keyboard history on iPhone and iPad, reset predictive text, and start fresh with more accurate suggestions.

Table of Contents
  • What is the Keyboard History on iPhone, and How Does It Work?
  • Why Clear Keyboard History on iPhone and iPad
  • How to Delete Keyboard History on iPhone or iPad
  • Alternatives to Clearing iPhone keyboard History
    • 1. Disable Auto-Correction
    • 2. Disable Predictive Text
  • Signing Off…

What is the Keyboard History on iPhone, and How Does It Work?

The keyboard history is a repository of frequently typed words, including those pre-stored into your iPhone’s autocorrect dictionary by default.

Hence, when autocorrect is on, your iPhone tries to find the best correction from its dictionary to replace every word you type with a correct one. So, when you press the space bar or start the next word while typing, the previous one gets corrected.

While you can’t edit or correct the keyboard history, you can reset it altogether.

Why Clear Keyboard History on iPhone and iPad

Your iPhone keyboard keeps track of the words, phrases, and even emojis you use most often. Over time, this helps it predict what you might want to type next. However, it can also lead to unwanted suggestions, especially if you’ve made typos or used certain words you no longer want stored.

Clearing your keyboard history gives you a clean slate and helps your keyboard feel more accurate again.

How to Delete Keyboard History on iPhone or iPad

Deleting the keyboard history on an iPhone is pretty straightforward and can be done in just a few taps. Here’s how you can do this:

  1. Open Settings and tap General.
  2. Scroll down to the bottom and tap Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  3. Tap Reset.
  4. Choose the Reset Keyboard Dictionary pop-up menu, then enter your passcode when prompted.
  5. Finally, tap Reset Dictionary.

That’s it! You can now start afresh. However, if you don’t want to clear keyboard history repeatedly, you have other options. Read on!

Alternatives to Clearing iPhone keyboard History

1. Disable Auto-Correction

To stop your iPhone from correcting your words permanently, disable keyboard auto-correction. This will prevent your iPhone from making changes automatically while still suggesting words.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Keyboard.
  2. Toggle off Auto-Correction.

2. Disable Predictive Text

The other alternative is to disable predictive text. This will prevent your iPhone from learning new words and making new suggestions. Here’s how you can disable predictive text.

  1. Open Settings → General.
  2. Tap Keyboard.
  3. Toggle off Predictive.

Signing Off…

That’s how you can delete iPhone’s keyboard history! Whether you’re sending a text or typing for safe-keeping, the iPhone’s auto-correction can be annoying. It might replace words and, worse, change the meaning of your message. If you have more questions, share them in the comments below.

FAQs

Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn’t have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

Read next:

  • iOS 26 New Features for iPhone: Everything You Need to Know
  • How to add or change a keyboard on iPhone and iPad
  • How to fix a split or small keyboard on an iPad
  • What’s New in the Phone App with iOS 26

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

keyPoints.title: Understanding Keyboard History on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Keyboard history is a collection of frequently used words and phrases learned by the iPhone to improve suggestions, which can be reset if needed.

keyPoints.title: Reasons to Clear Keyboard History
keyPoints.explanation: Clearing keyboard history helps remove unwanted or personal suggestions, making predictive text more accurate and privacy-conscious.

keyPoints.title: How to Clear Keyboard History on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can delete your keyboard history by navigating through Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Reset > Reset Keyboard Dictionary.

keyPoints.title: Disabling Auto-Correction and Predictive Text as Alternatives
keyPoints.explanation: To stop unwanted suggestions, you can disable auto-correction and predictive text in Settings > General > Keyboard, without deleting history.

keyPoints.title: Additional Tips for Managing Keyboard Settings
keyPoints.explanation: Changing or adding keyboards involves going to Settings > General > Keyboard > Keyboards, providing further customization options for your typing experience.

title.rendered: Cannot Connect to App Store Error? 14 Proven Ways to Fix It

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why the App Store won’t connect: The error often stems from Apple’s server outages, weak internet, VPN interference, or incorrect date and time settings on your device.
  • Start with simple connection checks: Visit Apple’s System Status page, test your Wi-Fi or mobile data, and make sure your region, time, and location settings are correct.
  • Try basic fixes before advanced ones: Restart your iPhone, toggle Airplane Mode, clear the App Store cache, and review app permissions or network limits.
  • Use advanced troubleshooting if needed: Reset network or all settings, sign out and back into your Apple ID, or repair deeper iOS issues with trusted system recovery tools.
  • Contact Apple Support if the issue persists: If the App Store still won’t connect after all fixes, seek help from Apple Support or an authorized service center.

Have you ever opened the App Store on your iPhone or iPad, only to be greeted with the frustrating “Cannot Connect to App Store” error? You’re not alone. This issue can appear when you’re trying to download a new app, update your favorites, or even browse the store, and it can be caused by anything from a weak internet connection to a temporary glitch in Apple’s servers.

The good news is, you don’t have to panic. In this guide, we’ll walk you through 14 proven ways to fix the “Cannot Connect to App Store” error and get your App Store working again in minutes.

Table of Contents
  • Why Can't I Connect to the App Store?
  • Troubleshooting Strategy: How to Fix App Store Not Working
  • Step-by-Step Solutions to Fix "Cannot Connect to App Store"
    • 1. Check Apple's System Status
    • 2. Verify and Troubleshoot Your Internet Connection
    • 3. Retry the App Store Connection
    • 4. Check App Store Permissions and Cellular Data Settings
    • 5. Force Quit and Reopen the App Store
    • 6. Clear the App Store Cache (Hidden Power User Fix)
    • 7. Restart Your iPhone or iPad (Soft Reboot)
    • 8. Turn Off VPN, Proxy, and Remove Network Restrictions
    • 9. Adjust Device Settings: Date, Time, and Location
    • 10. Update iOS or iPadOS
    • 11. Sign Out and Back Into Apple ID (Reset App Store Account Session)
    • 12. Force Restart (Hard Reboot)
    • 13. Reset Network Settings
    • 14. Reset All Settings (Advanced, Optional)
  • Using Advanced Repair Tools: A Proactive, Data-Safe Solution
    • What Are Advanced Repair Tools?
    • Why Consider These Tools?
    • How Do These Tools Compare to Apple's Solutions?
  • Troubleshooting Escalation Table
  • What Happens When You Reset All Settings?
  • When to Seek Further Help
  • Conclusion

Why Can’t I Connect to the App Store?

Before you jump into the fixes, it’s helpful to know what’s really going on behind the scenes. There are a handful of sneaky reasons why you might see the “Cannot Connect to App Store” error pop up.

  • Apple’s Servers Are Down: Sometimes, the problem is on Apple’s end due to server maintenance, outages, or regional disruptions. No amount of troubleshooting on your device can solve this, so you simply have to wait.
  • Internet Connection Problems: Weak Wi-Fi or cellular data, misconfigured routers, or ISP-level filtering can all block App Store access. Even if other websites work, DNS issues or network restrictions could be at play.
  • Incorrect Date, Time, or Location Settings: Apple’s servers use your device’s clock and region to authenticate connections and enforce security. Even a small mismatch can block access.
  • VPN or Firewall Interference: VPNs, proxies, or firewalls may make it seem like you’re in a different country or block essential network ports, leading the App Store to reject your connection.
  • Device Management Profiles or Parental Controls: If your device is managed by a school, employer, or a parental control app, hidden profiles might block access to the App Store or restrict certain categories.
  • Software Glitches or Outdated iOS: Bugs, failed updates, or running a beta version of iOS can introduce compatibility issues or corrupt system files, preventing the App Store from loading.
  • App Store Permissions and Account Issues: If the App Store doesn’t have permission to use mobile data or if your Apple ID has unresolved billing or security issues, you may be locked out.
  • Regional or ISP-Specific Blocking: Rarely, your Apple ID region or device location doesn’t match your physical country (for example, after moving or traveling abroad), which can cause access issues.
  • Device Storage Full or Corrupted System Files: If your device is low on storage or has corrupted system files from a failed update, the App Store may fail to authenticate or function properly.
  • Temporary Software Glitches: Sometimes, a minor bug or background process can disrupt the App Store connection. These are often resolved with a simple restart or cache clear.

Troubleshooting Strategy: How to Fix App Store Not Working

You don’t always have to go nuclear with your fixes. It’s usually best to start with the easiest, least disruptive solutions and only move on to the bigger stuff if you need to. Here’s how to troubleshoot the smart way:

  • Quick refreshes and app restarts are best for minor, temporary glitches.
  • Device restarts and cache clearing are useful for persistent but non-critical bugs.
  • Settings resets are reserved for stubborn issues when other steps fail.
  • Network isolation and advanced checks help fix persistent or complex problems.
  • Advanced repair tools are for deep software issues that standard steps can’t resolve.

Step-by-Step Solutions to Fix “Cannot Connect to App Store”

Tip: Work through these solutions in order for the best chance of success with minimal disruption.

1. Check Apple’s System Status

Before making any changes to your settings or restarting your devices, verify whether the issue originates with Apple. Sometimes service outages or technical issues on Apple’s end can cause disruptions, so checking their system status can save you unnecessary troubleshooting.

  1. Visit Apple’s System Status page.
  2. Look for “App Store” in the list.
  3. If the indicator is green, the App Store is working. If it’s yellow or red, Apple is experiencing issues, so wait and try again later.

Why This Matters: Apple’s services are robust but not immune to outages. Social media and outage trackers may report problems before Apple’s page updates. Trust your instincts if you see widespread reports.

Pro Tip Bookmark the System Status page or add it to your iOS Home Screen for one-tap access.
Insight: Some outages are regional. If you suspect a local issue, check with friends nearby or search online communities for real-time updates.

2. Verify and Troubleshoot Your Internet Connection

A stable, unrestricted internet connection is essential for smooth browsing, streaming, and online communication. Here’s how to diagnose like a pro:

  1. Confirm Internet Access Beyond the App Store
    • Open Safari and try loading a few different websites. If none of them load, the issue is with your device’s connection, not the App Store.
  2. Isolate the Problem: Device or Network?
    Try the App Store on another device on the same Wi-Fi network.
    • If none of the devices can connect, it’s likely a problem with your router or ISP.
    • If your device can’t connect, focus on your device settings.
  3. Restart and Refresh Your Network
    • Unplug your router for 30 seconds, then plug it back in. Move closer to the router to rule out weak signals.
  4. Try a Different Network
    • Switch between Wi-Fi and cellular data. If one works and the other doesn’t, your network provider or router settings may be at fault.
  5. Advanced: Change DNS Servers
    • Switch to Google DNS (8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4) or Cloudflare (1.1.1.1) via Settings → Wi-Fi → [your network] → Configure DNS → Manual.
  6. Check for Network Restrictions and Security Apps
    • Look in Settings → General → VPN & Device Management for any installed profiles. Temporarily disable security or VPN apps to rule them out.
  7. Look for ISP or Regional Issues
    • Rarely, your ISP may block Apple’s servers. Contact your provider or check for regional outage reports online.

Why This Matters: Systematically isolating the problem saves time and avoids unnecessary steps. These advanced checks empower you to fix not just App Store issues, but any network hiccup.

3. Retry the App Store Connection

If you see the error message, tap Retry. Sometimes, a quick refresh is all it takes, especially after fixing your internet connection or toggling Airplane Mode.

4. Check App Store Permissions and Cellular Data Settings

The App Store requires your permission to access your data connection to download apps, updates, and other content. Allowing this permission ensures that the App Store can function properly and provide you with the latest features and services.

  1. Go to Settings → Cellular.
  2. Make sure the toggle next to App Store is ON.

Why This Matters: If this is off, the App Store can’t use your mobile data for downloads or updates.

5. Force Quit and Reopen the App Store

Temporary glitches, such as software bugs or connection issues, can cause the App Store to crash unexpectedly or freeze, preventing users from browsing or downloading apps until the problem is resolved.

  1. On iPhones with Face ID: Swipe up and pause to open the App Switcher. Find the App Store card and swipe it up to close.
  2. On iPhones with a Home button: Double-press Home, then swipe up on the App Store card.
  3. Reopen the App Store from your Home Screen.

6. Clear the App Store Cache (Hidden Power User Fix)

Why Clearing Cache Works

Like many apps, the App Store stores temporary files (also called cache) to help things load faster. But over time, this cache can become outdated or corrupted, slowing things down or causing weird connection errors. Clearing it out gives the App Store a fresh start, so it can grab new data straight from Apple’s servers.

How to Clear the App Store Cache

  1. Open the App Store.
  2. Tap any one of the bottom tabs (Today, Games, Apps) 10 times quickly.
  3. You won’t get a confirmation, but this action clears the cache.

What to Expect: After clearing the cache, the App Store may reload content and feel snappier. No apps, purchases, or account info will be lost.

When to Use: If the App Store seems slow or stuck, or displays outdated information, this simple trick can refresh it and often resolves connection issues that don’t respond to restarts.

Myth Busting: Clearing the cache does not delete your apps, purchases, or personal data. The lack of a confirmation message is normal.

Pro Tip: If you frequently troubleshoot the App Store, consider creating a Siri Shortcut or using Accessibility features to quickly launch the correct tab for cache clearing.

7. Restart Your iPhone or iPad (Soft Reboot)

A standard restart of your iPhone often clears minor device glitches by shutting down all running processes and refreshing the system, resolving temporary issues and improving overall device performance.

  1. Press and hold the Side (or Top) button and either Volume button until the power-off slider appears.
  2. Drag the slider to turn off your device.
  3. Wait a few seconds, then press and hold the Side (or Top) button until the Apple logo appears.

8. Turn Off VPN, Proxy, and Remove Network Restrictions

VPNs often reroute your IP address to servers in different locations. This process can create a mismatch between your actual location and the one detected by Apple’s regional verification system. As a result, you may experience issues accessing the App Store, such as being unable to download certain apps or encountering errors due to these regional conflicts.

  1. Go to Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.
  2. Tap VPN and toggle it off.

Extra Insight: Security apps, firewalls, or device management profiles can also restrict access. Disable them if possible.

9. Adjust Device Settings: Date, Time, and Location

Apple’s servers utilize your device’s date, time, and location information to verify your identity. This process helps ensure that only authorized users can access certain services and maintains secure, region-specific access to Apple’s features and content. By verifying these details, Apple can provide a safer, more personalized user experience.

  1. To set the Date and time automatically, go to Settings → General → Date & Time and toggle on Set Automatically.
  2. Enable Location Services: Go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services. Toggle ON. Scroll to App Store and choose your preferred option.

Advanced: Rarely, custom regional settings (like 24-hour time or non-Gregorian calendars) can cause issues. Reset to default if needed.

10. Update iOS or iPadOS

Outdated software can cause bugs and compatibility issues, such as unexpected errors, security vulnerabilities, and difficulties working with newer hardware or other updated programs.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. If an update is available, tap Download and Install.

11. Sign Out and Back Into Apple ID (Reset App Store Account Session)

Why Signing Out/In Works

Sometimes, the problem isn’t with your device or your internet connection. It’s your Apple ID session acting up. If there are authentication hiccups, expired logins, or other account issues, simply signing out and back in can give your device a clean, secure connection to Apple’s servers.

How to Sign Out and In

  1. Open Settings and tap your name at the top.
  2. Scroll down and tap Sign Out. Enter your password to confirm.
  3. Restart your device (recommended for best results).
  4. Sign back in.

To sign out of just the App Store: Go to Settings → [your profile] → Media & Purchases. Tap Sign Out, then sign back in.

What to Expect: You may need to re-enter your Apple ID password. No apps, purchases, or data will be lost, but you could temporarily lose access to Apple services if you forget your credentials.

When to Use: If you’re seeing account-related errors, repeated prompts for your Apple ID, or persistent connection issues after clearing the cache, try this step.

Pro Tip: If changes don’t take effect immediately, restart your device after signing in.

12. Force Restart (Hard Reboot)

A force restart can resolve stubborn software glitches by completely shutting down the device and restarting its operating system, which helps clear temporary errors and refresh system processes.

  1. iPhone 8 or later: Quickly press and release Volume Up, then Volume Down, then press and hold the Side button until the Apple logo appears.
  2. iPhone 7/7 Plus: Press and hold both the Volume Down and Sleep/Wake buttons until the Apple logo appears.
  3. iPhone 6s or earlier: Press and hold both the Home and the Top (or Side) buttons until the Apple logo appears.

13. Reset Network Settings

If your internet connection is working on other websites or apps but you are unable to access the App Store, try resetting your device’s network settings. This process can help resolve connectivity issues by restoring your network configurations to their default state, which may fix problems preventing the App Store from loading properly.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap Reset → Reset Network Settings.
  3. Enter your passcode if prompted and confirm.
Heads Up: This erases saved Wi-Fi passwords and Bluetooth connections, so have them handy.

14. Reset All Settings (Advanced, Optional)

If nothing else works, you can reset all settings to their default values. This will restore the system to its original configuration, removing any customizations or changes you have made. Use this option as a last resort if other troubleshooting steps have not resolved your issue.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap Reset → Reset All Settings.

What to Expect: This won’t erase your data, apps, or photos, but it will reset system preferences (Wi-Fi, privacy, accessibility, etc.) to their defaults.

Using Advanced Repair Tools: A Proactive, Data-Safe Solution

If you have tried all the steps above and the App Store still does not connect, there may be a more serious issue with your device. This could be caused by issues with your device’s software, network settings, or your Apple ID. You may need to restart your device, reset your network settings, or contact Apple Support for help.

What Are Advanced Repair Tools?

Third-party apps like Dr.Fone System Repair or MagFone iOS System Recovery can diagnose and repair core iOS components, often without erasing your personal data.

Why Consider These Tools?

  1. Fix persistent App Store errors that standard troubleshooting can’t resolve.
  2. Recover from failed updates or software corruption.
  3. Repair iOS without a full factory reset.

Best Practices:

  1. Only download repair tools from reputable sources.
  2. Always use the “standard repair” or “no data loss” mode first.
  3. Back up your device before using any repair tool.
  4. If prompted to use “advanced” or “deep” repair modes, back up first; these may erase your data.
  5. If your device is under warranty, check with Apple before using third-party tools.

How Do These Tools Compare to Apple’s Solutions?

Apple’s built-in diagnostics and resets work for most issues, but advanced third-party tools can fix deeper system corruption, often without causing full data loss.

Troubleshooting Escalation Table

What Happens When You Reset All Settings?

You’ll need to:

  1. Reconnect to Wi-Fi networks (passwords will be erased)
  2. Reconfigure Bluetooth pairings
  3. Adjust privacy, notification, and accessibility settings
  4. Re-enter VPN or custom configurations if used

Rest assured: Your personal content (photos, apps, messages, etc.) remains untouched.

When to Seek Further Help

If you’ve tried all these steps, including advanced repair tools, and still can’t connect to the App Store, the problem may be a deeper software or hardware issue.

Contact Apple Support or visit your nearest Apple Store for additional assistance.

Conclusion

Most of the time, you can fix the “Cannot Connect to App Store” message with a few practical steps. Start with the basics — checking Apple’s system status and your internet connection — then move through the other solutions from simplest to most advanced. Once you understand why each fix works, you’ll feel much more confident troubleshooting and preventing these issues in the future. If you’re still stuck, reach out to Apple Support, as they’re always ready to help.

Have another App Store issue? Leave a comment below, and I’ll be happy to help!

FAQs

Why does my iPhone say “Cannot Connect to App Store” even with good internet?

This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn’t erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

Why does the App Store need my location?

The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

What if I can’t change date/time or location settings?

If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

blockGraphs.question: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?
blockGraphs.answer: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

blockGraphs.question: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?
blockGraphs.answer: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

blockGraphs.question: Why does the App Store need my location?
blockGraphs.answer: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

blockGraphs.question: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?
blockGraphs.answer: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

keyPoints.title: Reasons for 'Cannot Connect to App Store' Error
keyPoints.explanation: Common causes include Apple's server outages, internet connection issues, incorrect device settings, VPN interference, or outdated software.

keyPoints.title: Initial Troubleshooting Steps
keyPoints.explanation: Start by checking Apple's system status, verifying your internet connection, and ensuring your device settings like date, time, and location are correctly configured.

keyPoints.title: Basic Fixes to Try First
keyPoints.explanation: These include restarting your device, toggling Airplane Mode, clearing the App Store cache, and checking app permissions and network restrictions.

keyPoints.title: Advanced Troubleshooting Methods
keyPoints.explanation: If basic fixes fail, consider resetting network or all settings, signing out and back into your Apple ID, or using third-party repair tools for deeper software issues.

keyPoints.title: When to Seek Professional Help
keyPoints.explanation: If all troubleshooting steps, including advanced repairs, do not resolve the issue, contact Apple Support or visit an Apple Store for further assistance.

title.rendered: Everything New in iOS 26.1: New Tweaks, Fixes, and Features

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Liquid Glass Customization and Transparency: iOS 26.1 adds a tint control letting you switch between Clear and Tinted styles for sharper contrast in apps and notifications.
  • Lock Screen Camera Swipe Disablement: You can now disable the Lock Screen camera swipe in Settings to avoid opening the camera by mistake while keeping it accessible.
  • Enhanced Phone Haptics and Alarm Interface: iOS 26.1 lets you turn off call connection vibrations and introduces a redesigned swipe-to-stop alarm motion for fewer accidental dismissals.
  • Expanded Language Support and Live Translation for AirPods: Apple Intelligence now supports more languages, and AirPods gain Live Translation in Japanese, Korean, Italian, and Chinese.
  • Refreshed Apple TV and Customizable Fitness Workouts: The Apple TV app gets a sleeker icon and layout, while the Fitness app now supports building personalized workout routines.

Apple continues its iOS 26 journey with the release of iOS 26.1, offering a range of enhancements aimed at improving the user experience for both iPhone and iPad holders. This update delivers a mix of user-driven tweaks, visual polish, and practical improvements.

Enhancements for Liquid Glass and Other Tweaks

With this release, Apple has included more flexible customization options for Liquid Glass, aligning with user requests. For those eager to disable the persistent Lock Screen camera gesture, there’s now a straightforward solution. Here’s what to expect from iOS 26.1 and iPadOS 26.1.

Liquid Glass Adds Transparency Options

Previously, anyone looking to adjust the liquid glass effect had to dive into Accessibility settings. iOS 26.1 makes it easier with a new tint control for Liquid Glass. Users can now toggle between Clear and Tinted styles, providing better contrast in notifications and apps. To access this, navigate to Settings, then Display & Brightness.

Lock Screen Camera Swipe Disablement

At last, users can deactivate the Lock Screen camera gesture. The newly added setting under Camera options lets you disable the left-swipe shortcut while still keeping the camera functional.

Modify Phone Haptics

The new update also lets users choose to turn off the subtle vibration that happens when a call connects or ends, providing more control over phone haptic feedback.

Alarm Interface Reworked

An updated swipe-to-stop gesture replaces the old tap-to-stop button for alarms, intending to cut down on accidental dismissals.

Expanded Language Support in Apple Intelligence

Apple Intelligence has broadened its language support, now accommodating Danish, Dutch, Norwegian, Portuguese (Portugal), Swedish, Turkish, Traditional Chinese, and Vietnamese.

AirPods Gain More Language Options for Live Translation

AirPods now support Live Translation in Japanese, Korean, Italian, and both Simplified and Traditional Chinese. This feature is compatible with AirPods Pro 2, Pro 3, and AirPods 4 that include ANC.

Refreshed Apple TV App

The Apple TV app has received a visual refresh, adopting a Liquid Glass-inspired icon while simplifying its branding to “Apple TV.”

Customizable Workouts in the Fitness App

In a bid to enhance fitness tracking, users can now design their own workouts in the Fitness app, tailoring them by workout type, caloric goals, effort, and duration.

Improvement in FaceTime Audio

FaceTime audio has been upgraded for better clarity in low-bandwidth scenarios, improving call quality under less-than-ideal network conditions.

Changes to Teen Account Safety

Apple has made adjustments to communication safety settings on teen accounts, removing automatic restrictions. Parents now need to manually review these settings for child accounts aged 13-17.

Local Capture Settings

A new Local Capture setting under Settings → General → Local Capture lets you choose a save location in the Files app for call recordings, including audio and video.

Enhancements for External Microphone Users

When using an external microphone with local capture, iOS 26.1 adds a control to adjust input gain. This gives you more flexibility to fine-tune your recording levels directly from the Settings app.

Software’s Subtle Interface Updates

iOS 26.1 also makes several minor but visible changes:

  • Text headers in both Settings and Home Screen folders switch to left alignment.
  • The Phone keypad integrates Liquid Glass elements.
  • The Photos app benefits from a redesigned video scrubber and improved selection menus.
  • Safari’s Tab Bar is wide and optimized for reduced transparency mode.
  • “Display Borders” replaces the former Button Shapes option in Accessibility settings.

Security and System Modifications

Apple has restructured the Privacy and Security section, allowing users to toggle automatic downloads and installations of security improvements. This change aims to ease the delivery of smaller security patches without requiring a complete iOS update.

iPadOS 26.1 Brings Back Slide Over

For iPad users, Slide Over functionality returns with iPadOS 26.1, permitting a floating app view when using multiple windows. The update also integrates the Vision Pro app, boosting Apple’s ecosystem synergy.

Downloading and Installing the Update

Ready to update? Simply head to Settings, General, then Software Update. iOS 26.1 is compatible with the iPhone 11 lineup and newer models, including the 2nd-generation iPhone SE and later. iPadOS 26.1 is available for all iPads running iPadOS 26.

Have you experienced iOS 26.1 yet? What’s your favorite feature in this update? Let us know below.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

aioseo_meta_data.description: Apple’s iOS 26.1 brings new Liquid Glass controls, Lock Screen fixes, smarter Apple Intelligence updates, and refined visuals for iPhone and iPad users.

keyPoints.title: Liquid Glass Customization and Transparency
keyPoints.explanation: iOS 26.1 introduces a new tint control for Liquid Glass, allowing users to toggle between Clear and Tinted styles for better contrast in notifications and apps.

keyPoints.title: Lock Screen Camera Swipe Disablement
keyPoints.explanation: Users can now deactivate the Lock Screen camera gesture in settings, preventing accidental camera activation while keeping the feature functional.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Phone Haptics and Alarm Interface
keyPoints.explanation: The update gives users control to turn off call connection vibrations and introduces a reworked swipe-to-stop gesture for alarms to reduce accidental dismissals.

keyPoints.title: Expanded Language Support and Live Translation for AirPods
keyPoints.explanation: Apple has broadened language support in Apple Intelligence, adding more languages, and now supports Live Translation on AirPods in Japanese, Korean, Italian, and Chinese.

keyPoints.title: Refreshed Apple TV and Customizable Fitness Workouts
keyPoints.explanation: The Apple TV app gets a new Liquid Glass-inspired icon and simplified branding, while the Fitness app now allows users to design personalized workouts.

title.rendered: How to Use Call Screening on iPhone in iOS 26

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What Is Call Screening on iPhone?: Apple’s new Call Screening in iOS 26 lets unknown callers announce their name and reason, showing a real-time transcript so you can decide whether to answer.
  • Why Call Screening Matters: It helps you avoid spam, scams, and robocalls while maintaining privacy and focus by only alerting you to meaningful or identified calls.
  • How to Turn On Call Screening: Go to Settings > Phone > Calls from Unknown Numbers > Call Screening, then toggle it on manually since it’s off by default.
  • How It Works in Real Time: When someone you don’t know calls, your iPhone prompts them to speak; you’ll see a live transcript and can answer, decline, or reply with a message.
  • Fixing Call Screening Problems: If it’s not working, update to iOS 26, check your region settings, disable Silence Unknown Callers, and restart your iPhone.

Tired of spam or unknown callers interrupting your day? With iOS 26, your iPhone can now screen calls for you such as automatically identifying unknown numbers, transcribing who’s calling, and letting you decide what to do.

This new Call Screening feature transforms how you handle phone calls, giving you more control, fewer distractions, and total privacy. Keep reading to learn how Call Screening works on iPhone, how to enable it, and how to troubleshoot it if needed.

What Is Call Screening on iPhone?

Call Screening is one of the standout iOS 26 features. It builds on the existing Live Voicemail functionality but takes it a step further. When someone unknown tries to call you, your iPhone via Call Screening asks for their name and the reason for the call.

You’ll see a live transcription of their response in real time. This gives you the freedom to decide whether to answer, decline, ignore, or respond with text, all without picking up the call.

It’s like having a polite assistant ask, “Who’s calling and why?” and then letting you decide.

Why Use Call Screening on iOS 26?

Call Screening isn’t just about blocking spam; it empowers you to manage calls on your terms. Here’s why you should enable this feature:

  • Avoid Distractions: Let your iPhone handle unknown callers while you stay focused.
  • Protect Your Privacy: Screen suspicious calls without revealing your identity or voice.
  • Filter Robocalls & Scams: Identify unwanted calls before you even hear a ring.
  • Stay Informed: Know who’s calling and why without answering.
  • Work Without Interruptions: Ideal for meetings, focus time, or relaxation.

How to Turn On Call Screening on iPhone

Unlike some other iOS 26 features, Call Screening is off by default. You’ll need to enable it manually:

  1. Open the Settings app, scroll down and tap Apps.
  2. Select the Phone app.
  3. Scroll down to the Screen Unknown Callers section and select Ask Reason for Calling.

That’s it! Your iPhone is now equipped to handle unknown callers intelligently.

What Happens When a Call Is Screened?

When you receive a call from an unknown number:

  • Call Screening steps in and asks the caller,” Hi, if you record your name and reason for calling, I’ll see if this person is available.”
  • Once the caller states their name and reason for the call, Call Screening responds with, ” Thanks [Caller’s Name]. Please stay on the line.”
  • During this time, you’ll see a live transcription of what they say on your screen and your iPhone will ring.

You can now:

  • Answer: Swipe right on the call slider or tap the Answer button to pick up the call.
  • Decline: Press the side button twice to hang up, or tap the Decline button and send it to voicemail.
  • Respond via text: Type a message if needed.
  • Ignore: Do nothing and review the transcript later in your Recents tab.

Related: Hold Assist in iOS 26: What It Is and How It Works

Call Screening Not Working in iOS 26? Try These Fixes

If Call Screening isn’t working on your iPhone, try these steps:

  • Update to iOS 26: Ensure you’re running the latest compatible version of iOS 26.
  • Turn It On: Confirm that Call Screening is enabled under Phone app settings.
  • Check Region and Language: As of now, Call Screening works in English (Australia, Canada, India, Ireland, New Zealand, Puerto Rico, Singapore, South Africa, the UK, and the US). Your language and region settings must match.
  • Check Silence Unknown Callers: If this is enabled (Settings > Apps > Phone > Silence), it may interfere with Call Screening by sending unknown calls directly to voicemail. Try turning it off and testing again.
  • Restart Your iPhone: A simple reboot can fix temporary glitches.

No More Guessing Who’s Calling

With Call Screening in iOS 26, your iPhone becomes your personal call assistant.
Whether you’re trying to reduce distractions, avoid spam, or just want to know who’s calling before answering, this smart tool puts you in control.

Now you can finally say goodbye to unwanted calls and hello to uninterrupted time. Have you tried the feature yet? Let me know your experience in the comments below!

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.
