mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

keyPoints.title: What Is Call Screening on iPhone?
keyPoints.explanation: Call Screening on iOS 26 improves call management by prompting unknown callers to state their name and reason, helping you decide whether to pick up based on a live transcription.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Using Call Screening on iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: This feature reduces distractions, enhances privacy, filters out robocalls and scams, and keeps you aware of who’s calling, allowing for a more relaxed and focused environment.

keyPoints.title: How to Enable Call Screening on Your iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: To activate Call Screening, navigate to Settings > Phone > Calls from Unknown Numbers and toggle on Call Screening, noting that it is disabled by default.

keyPoints.title: What Happens During Call Screening?
keyPoints.explanation: When you receive an unknown call, your iPhone asks the caller to record their name and reason, then shows a live transcription, giving you options to answer, decline, respond via text, or ignore.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting Call Screening Issues in iOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: If Call Screening isn’t functioning, ensure your iPhone is updated to iOS 26, verify the feature is enabled, check region and language settings, disable Silence Unknown Callers if enabled, and restart your device.

title.rendered: Apple TV+ to Apple TV Rebrand Official: Finneas Debuts New Intro

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple TV+ officially rebranded to Apple TV across web, apps, and social media, simplifying its identity ahead of upcoming OS updates.
  • New animated intro and sound by Finneas now plays before all Apple Originals, with versions tailored for shows, trailers, and theaters.
  • Rebrand supports Apple’s unified media vision, moving away from the “Plus” label to streamline how users recognize its streaming service.
  • Finneas composed around pre-made visuals, crafting a sound that balances cinematic flair with Apple’s clean design philosophy.
  • Visual and audio changes may lag in apps, with updates expected in iOS 26.1, iPadOS 26.1, tvOS 26.1, and macOS Tahoe 26.1.

Apple has made it official: the streaming service once known as Apple TV+ is now simply Apple TV. This rebranding comes with a fresh intro video boasting a sound composed by Grammy winner Finneas.

Apple TV Rebrand Officially Rolls Out

Apple quietly implemented these changes across its website, social media channels, and app platforms. Where it once said Apple TV+, it now reads Apple TV. A short YouTube video titled “This is just the beginning” reveals a new animated logo featuring vibrant rainbow tones, paired with an audio signature crafted by Finneas.

This new audio snippet will precede every Apple original film and series. In a chat with Variety, Finneas divulged there are three distinct versions of the sound. These include a five-second piece for TV shows, a one-second sting for trailers, and a 12-second version meant for theaters. His aim was to create something that felt both cinematic and magical, aligning with Apple’s sleek design sensibilities.

Finneas on Creating the Sound for Apple TV

Posting on Instagram, Finneas expressed his excitement over collaborating with Apple, acknowledging the importance of echoing what he appreciates about the brand—its creation of beautiful tools. He admitted that while the process was demanding, it was also highly rewarding, striving for a sound that balances simplicity with emotional depth.

According to David Taylor, Apple’s head of music, the sound Finneas delivered is “completely original and feels cinematic and magical.” Interestingly, the animation was completed before Finneas started composing, allowing him to shape the music around the visuals.

More Than a Name Change

This rebrand is more than just a facelift. In his discussion with Variety, Finneas noted that Apple aims to streamline its streaming identity, shedding the “Plus” to align with a broader strategy. While changes are gradually taking effect across Apple’s ecosystem, the Apple TV app still shows Apple TV+ at present. This is expected to transition with future software updates such as iOS 26.1, iPadOS 26.1, tvOS 26.1, and macOS Tahoe 26.1.

Pricing for Apple TV stands at $12.99 monthly, with its library offering popular series like Ted Lasso, Severance, The Morning Show, and Silo. With this new branding and distinct audio cue, Apple seems poised to embark on the next chapter of its storytelling venture.

Does this rebrand catch your eye, or is it just semantics for you? Share your take below.

title.rendered: Apple Launches New Web Version of the App Store

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Full App Store now on the web with search, categories, and “Today” tab for curated stories and top charts at apps.apple.com.
  • Unified platform toggle menu lets you explore iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Vision Pro, and Apple TV apps in one place.
  • New app pages mirror native App Store with high-quality screenshots, badges, ratings, and developer info for better browsing and discovery.
  • Web interface is read-only—you can’t install apps from the browser, only view or share listings and open them on your Apple device.
  • Best for non-Apple device users or those researching apps on Windows, but lacks download support so keep expectations clear.

Apple has introduced a revamped web version of the App Store, offering a comprehensive browsing experience to anyone using a web browser. This update transforms the formerly basic app listing pages into a full-fledged discovery hub for apps across various Apple platforms.

Full App Store Experience Comes to the Web

The newly designed apps.apple.com now closely resembles the App Store app that’s available on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Vision Pro, and Apple TV. Equipped with a proper search bar, category filters, and even the “Today” tab, which includes curated app stories, recommendations, and top charts—the site extends a familiar ecosystem into web browsers.

Users can delve into categories such as productivity, games, or entertainment, uncover featured collections, or explore ongoing events and editorials. Every app now has a dedicated page that features high-quality screenshots, ratings, and detailed information similar to what users experience in the app version.

Central Hub for All Apple Platforms

An innovative feature is the drop-down menu that enables users to toggle between platform-specific App Stores. Whether you’re hunting for an Apple Watch app or a Vision Pro title, this unified hub makes it easy to explore everything Apple has to offer in one spot. Prior to this, Apple only provided individual app pages, which users accessed through direct links or via search engines like Google, without any means to explore or search for apps directly on the web.

Design and Functionality Upgrades

The redesigned web interface boasts clear iconography, media previews, and improved navigation. App product pages now emphasize special badges like awards and events, adding layers of information. The search interface has undergone a makeover as well, letting users find apps by name, category, or developer without leaving the browser.

Yet, Apple’s web App Store doesn’t facilitate direct downloads. Instead, users can share app links or open them directly in the device’s native App Store.

Apple’s Growing Focus on Accessibility and Discovery

By extending the App Store experience to the web, Apple is aiming to simplify the process of exploring apps without needing to switch devices. While it might seem minor, this change significantly enhances app discovery, making it particularly advantageous for users who rely on Windows PCs or non-Apple gadgets to research apps.

This initiative appears to be part of Apple’s strategy to bridge its App Store ecosystem with the wider web, underscoring its commitment to improved app visibility and cross-platform accessibility.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

title.rendered: iOS 27 to Bring Major Updates to Apple Intelligence, Says Report

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Intelligence gets major upgrade in iOS 27 with expanded features across devices, previewing at WWDC 2026 alongside macOS 27 and watchOS 27.
  • Siri overhaul arrives earlier in iOS 26.4, expected spring 2026, with better task handling, more natural voice responses, and delayed features from iOS 18.
  • WWDC 2026 marks a strategic AI push, signaling Apple’s biggest leap in AI since Siri’s launch and rebounding from iOS 26’s underwhelming AI rollout.
  • Apple may shift to hybrid AI processing, combining on-device smarts with Private Cloud support to balance privacy with performance and catch up to rivals.
  • AI changes could affect privacy expectations, so users should watch how Apple blends cloud reliance without compromising its long-standing on-device promise.

Apple’s upcoming iPhone software update, iOS 27, is reportedly putting AI front and center. According to the latest insights from Mark Gurman at Bloomberg, this update will bring significant changes to Apple Intelligence, which is Apple’s existing suite of AI features spread across its devices.

Apple Intelligence to Evolve Further in iOS 27

Gurman explains that alongside the unveiling of iOS 27, macOS 27, watchOS 27, and other important system updates, Apple plans to introduce substantial enhancements to Apple Intelligence. This will happen during the company’s annual Worldwide Developers Conference (WWDC) slated for June 2026. While the specific details of these upgrades remain under wraps, the mention of “major updates” indicates a significant advancement for Apple’s AI systems, particularly following a rather uneventful year for Apple Intelligence in iOS 26.

Big Siri Upgrade Coming Before iOS 27

Ahead of iOS 27, Apple is gearing up for noteworthy AI changes in the iOS 26.4 update. Anticipated in the spring of 2026, this update is expected to finally deliver a comprehensive overhaul of Siri, something Gurman describes as Apple’s most ambitious upgrade since Siri first launched. Users should look out for more adept task handling, more natural conversation capabilities, and the expanded AI features that were initially promised for iOS 18 but delayed until 2026. If timelines hold, users will experience these crucial AI enhancements first in iOS 26.4, with even more slated to arrive in iOS 27 later that year.

A Broader Shift in Apple’s AI Strategy

Gurman also suggested that there may be broader shifts in Apple’s AI strategy, possibly extending beyond new features. Traditionally, Apple has leaned heavily on privacy-centric, on-device AI processing. Yet, as the tech realm veers towards cloud-augmented intelligence, Apple could be reconsidering its approach to blend privacy and performance more effectively. This shift might steer the company towards a hybrid processing model, where some tasks occur both on devices and within Apple’s secure Private Cloud, potentially boosting AI functions without sacrificing user privacy.

Would these changes make a difference to you? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple is doubling down on AI with iOS 27, introducing major Apple Intelligence upgrades at WWDC 2026 and an early Siri overhaul in iOS 26.4.

If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

title.rendered: Here are All the New Camera Features on the iPhone 17 Pro

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone 17 Pro brings major camera upgrades: Apple’s latest flagship introduces significant hardware and AI enhancements, redefining both professional photography and daily mobile shooting.
  • 48MP Fusion Telephoto lens replaces 12MP sensor: It delivers 4x to 8x optical zoom and up to 40x digital zoom with advanced stabilization and consistent color accuracy across lenses.
  • New 18MP front camera boosts selfie and video quality: Featuring a wider sensor, 4K Dolby Vision, ProRes, slow motion, and auto-framing, it ensures sharp, well-balanced videos and group shots.
  • AI-powered image processing with A19 Pro chip: Apple’s Photonic Engine and neural algorithms restore detail, balance exposure, and enhance color realism, even at high zoom levels.
  • Next-level zoom and pro video recording: The iPhone 17 Pro supports 8x stabilized zoom, ProRes RAW format, and improved audio capture—ideal for creators and mobile filmmakers alike.

Every year, Apple tweaks the iPhone camera to make it better, and this year is no different. While everyone expected Apple to simply add a few AI camera features like other companies, the iPhone 17 Pro surprised users with meaningful hardware upgrades as well. Some changes are clearly aimed at professionals, but even everyday users will notice the difference and benefit from them.

The new Pro Fusion system combines three 48MP cameras — Main, Ultra Wide, and Telephoto —plus a redesigned front camera. Together, they handle color, light, and focus more intelligently than before.

Table of Contents
  • 1. The New 48MP Telephoto Lens
  • 2. The New 18MP Front Camera
  • 3. Smarter Image Processing
  • 4. Better Zooming Experience
  • 5. Main and Ultra Wide Camera Improvements
  • 6. Pro Video Features
  • Real-World Improvements

1. The New 48MP Telephoto Lens

If you’ve ever tried zooming on older iPhones and ended up with a grainy photo, this one’s for you. The new 48MP Fusion Telephoto lens replaces the 12MP sensor from last year and brings 4x and 8x optical-quality zoom with up to 40x digital zoom. That means you can capture distant buildings, wildlife, or even text on signs, even from far away, and still see real detail.

Apple also added 3D sensor-shift stabilization, which keeps shots steady even when you’re zoomed all the way in. Reviewers say switching between lenses — from 0.5x to 8x — now feels smooth and color-matched. No more sudden changes in exposure or tone.

In short, the 17 Pro’s zoom lens finally feels reliable enough for everyday shooting, not just occasional use. And with improved color consistency, every zoom level feels part of one clean, connected camera system.

2. The New 18MP Front Camera

The 18MP Center Stage front camera is a big leap over the old one. It uses a square sensor like those found in pro cameras, capturing wider shots while automatically keeping you centered in the frame. So if you’re recording a vlog or joining a video call, it subtly reframes as you move, no need to adjust your phone.

It supports 4K Dolby Vision, ProRes, and 120 fps slow motion, and everything looks stable and clear thanks to built-in image stabilization. Selfies also look sharper, with smoother skin tones and more balanced lighting indoors or outdoors.

3. Smarter Image Processing

Most of the camera improvements happen behind the scenes. The A19 Pro chip and new Photonic Engine handle photos with smarter algorithms that rebuild details and manage lighting more accurately. Deep learning helps the iPhone understand each scene and adjust shadows, contrast, and textures in real time.

Even at high zoom levels like 8x, photos stay crisp without looking over-processed. The transitions between lenses are smoother, and colors look more natural across all cameras. The result is a more balanced image every time, whether it’s daylight or a dimly lit room.

4. Better Zooming Experience

Shooting at 8x zoom (200mm) used to be something only pro cameras could handle, but the iPhone 17 Pro makes it easy. You can zoom in on tiny architectural details or capture wildlife from afar without a tripod. The 3D stabilization and improved AI correction ensure your shots stay usable even at long distances.

In low light, Night mode now produces softer, cleaner photos instead of grainy ones. Portraits look especially good, with sharp faces, smooth backgrounds, and realistic lighting that doesn’t feel artificial.

5. Main and Ultra Wide Camera Improvements

The 48MP Main and Ultra Wide lenses might look unchanged, but both have been fine-tuned. The Main camera handles complex lighting more confidently; bright skies, dark streets, or sunset tones all look more accurate. The Ultra Wide captures expansive shots at 120° while maintaining color consistency with the Main camera.

Both lenses can now shoot 48MP high-resolution photos with less noise. Macro mode returns for close-up shots of flowers, food, or small textures. Though the Main lens still struggles to focus extremely close, Apple’s software blending helps fill in those gaps smoothly.

6. Pro Video Features

The iPhone 17 Pro’s video capabilities go well beyond casual use. It now supports ProRes RAW, Apple Log 2, Genlock, and Open Gate recording, the same formats used in professional film production. You can shoot 4K at 120 fps, record spatial video for Vision Pro, and enjoy cleaner audio from four studio-quality microphones.

Video stabilization is stronger, too. Whether you’re walking, panning, or zooming mid-shot, the footage stays smooth. It’s built to help both everyday users and creators shoot confident, high-quality videos right from the phone.

Real-World Improvements

People who’ve tested the camera are noticing the difference. Photos of faraway buildings, like the UN headquarters, show small details clearly even at 8x zoom. Color matching across lenses is now consistent, and even handheld long-distance shots remain stable.

With three 48MP lenses, a better front camera, and upgraded processing, it’s designed to deliver consistent results without extra effort. Whether you’re shooting everyday moments, long-distance photos, or cinematic videos, the iPhone 17 Pro feels effortless. It’s built for people who want quality without complication, a camera that just gets it right.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

keyPoints.title: Introduction to iPhone 17 Pro Camera Upgrades
keyPoints.explanation: Apple continues to improve the iPhone camera annually, and this year introduces significant hardware upgrades alongside AI features, benefiting both professionals and everyday users.

keyPoints.title: The New 48MP Fusion Telephoto Lens
keyPoints.explanation: Replacing the old 12MP sensor, the 48MP Telephoto lens offers 4x and 8x optical zoom with up to 40x digital zoom, enhanced stabilization, and unified color quality for reliable, detailed distant shots.

keyPoints.title: The New 18MP Front Camera
keyPoints.explanation: The upgraded 18MP front camera uses a larger sensor for wider shots, supports 4K Dolby Vision, ProRes, and slow motion, and features automatic framing that keeps users centered and steady during video recording.

keyPoints.title: Smarter Image Processing with New Chips and Algorithms
keyPoints.explanation: The A19 Pro chip and Photonic Engine use advanced AI algorithms to rebuild details, manage lighting, and produce natural colors, ensuring high-quality photos even at high zoom levels.

keyPoints.title: Enhanced Zooming and Video Capabilities
keyPoints.explanation: The iPhone 17 Pro now allows stable, high-quality 8x zoom for casual and professional use, supports professional video formats like ProRes RAW, and offers improved stabilization and audio for high-quality filmmaking.

title.rendered: Apple Glasses: Everything We Know So Far

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple developing lightweight smart glasses: Expected between 2026–2027, these glasses will complement the Vision Pro but feature a slimmer, everyday design for casual wear.
  • Design and functionality focus: Apple Glasses may include cameras, microphones, speakers, and AI integration, blending smart features with fashionable, customizable frame options.
  • Launch predictions from Ming-Chi Kuo: Analysts expect a 2026 reveal and 2027 release, with more advanced AR-focused versions possibly arriving by 2028.
  • Pricing and market strategy: Apple Glasses could start around $499, positioning them against Meta’s $380 Ray-Bans and potentially offering bundle options for added value.
  • Hardware and AI-powered features: Expected specs include MicroLED or OLED displays, Apple silicon, built-in sensors, and wireless connectivity for intuitive, hands-free smart experiences.

Apple is actively developing lightweight “smart glasses” to follow its Vision Pro headset. Reports suggest there will be at least one glasses product launch in 2026 with a broader lineup in 2027, though timing could still shift.

While Apple has not officially announced or confirmed the product, leaks and expert speculation have given us a solid idea of what may be in development. Here, I’ll share everything that we know about Apple Smart Glasses, highlighting its expected design, features, release date, price, and more.

Table of Contents
  • What's the Big Idea Behind Apple Glasses?
  • Apple Glasses Expected Release Date
  • Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo Predicts Three Types of Smart Glasses
  • Apple Glass Potential Price
  • Design and Hardware: What Will Apple Glasses Look Like?
  • Apple Glasses Key Hardware
  • Expected Apple Glasses Features
  • Other Rumors and What’s Next
  • Wrapping It Up: Are Apple Glasses Worth the Hype?

What’s the Big Idea Behind Apple Glasses?

We all have seen what Meta’s Ray-Ban Glasses can do. Apple is taking a similar approach in its own style.

Apple Glasses are expected to come equipped with cameras, mics, and speakers, all supercharged by Siri and Apple Intelligence. They’re not full-on AR headsets like the Apple Vision Pro. Instead, these are slim, eyewear gadgets meant for checking directions or snapping a quick pic without fumbling for your phone.

According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple seems to be ditching a cheaper Vision Pro sequel to laser-focus on this, betting it’ll be the next big wearable hit after AirPods and the Watch.

Apple Glasses Expected Release Date

Timelines have shifted a bit with Apple’s AI push. Mark Gurman states that Apple’s CEO, Tim Cook, is focused on creating true AR glasses. “It’s the only thing he’s spending his time on from a product development standpoint,” he added.

Here’s the latest scoop:

  • Announcement: Expect an unveiling sometime in 2026, possibly at WWDC 2026.
  • Launch: Most reports point to a full release by 2027 with camera-equipped AirPods.
  • Next Version: Insiders speculate that Apple is also developing an advanced AR version of Apple Glasses. It may launch in 2028 at the earliest.

Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo Predicts Three Types of Smart Glasses

In a recent blog post, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo shared that Apple is set to launch its first-generation Ray-Ban-style smart glasses in 2027, with mass production beginning in Q2 of that year. These glasses are expected to:

  • Come without a built-in display
  • Focus on microphones, speakers (possibly via or with AirPods), and AI-powered environmental sensing
  • Offer full support for photo/video capture and audio features
  • Enable hands-free operation via voice commands and gesture recognition
  • Include multiple frame designs and material choices to increase appeal

In addition, Apple is reportedly developing XR glasses with built-in displays, targeting a 2028 launch. These will likely feature LCoS with waveguide tech for color AR visuals and retain voice/gesture control.

Apple Glass Potential Price

Apple hasn’t spilled the beans, but rumors keep it affordable to compete with Meta’s $380 Ray-Bans. A 2020 leak from designer Jon Prosser pegged it at $499 (plus extra for prescription lenses), and that still feels spot-on.

However, the upcoming Meta smart glasses could carry a $ 1,000 price tag. And Apple may see it as a benchmark. If Apple nails the value (like they did with AirPods), expect bundles with iPhones to sweeten the deal.

Design and Hardware: What Will Apple Glasses Look Like?

Apple’s aiming for “Clark Kent chic” everyday eyewear that doesn’t scream sci-fi goggles. Expect a slim design in metal or plastic, with multiple frame options and color choices. Similar to Vision Pro, Apple may offer prescription-ready lenses.

Rumors suggest that there would be a LiDAR scanner on the right temple. Apple is currently considering adding a removable camera module to address privacy concerns and an LED light that blinks during recording.

Prototypes look a bit “plastic goggle-y” right now, but Apple’s testing 3D printing for sleeker production as per MacRumors.

Apple Glasses Key Hardware

The display is a big challenge for smart glasses. Samsung Securities suggests that Apple could use 1.4-inch MicroOLED or MicroLED screens to deliver bright, sharp visuals in a compact form factor. Users could see text, maps, or notifications directly on the lenses without obstructing the view. 

However, mass-producing microLEDs is tricky and costly, so Apple may begin with simpler displays. According to Ross Young, Apple Glass could integrate Sony OLED screens for AR. The components may include:

Expected Apple Glasses Features

This is where the magic happens. Apple Glasses will lean hard into AI, turning your view of the world into a smart assistant. No holographic overlays yet, but plenty to make daily life easier. Here’s a quick list of rumored features:

  • AI Smarts with Siri: Ask “What’s that plant?” and it’ll identify it. Describe surroundings, answer questions, and translate texts in real time with upgraded Siri.
  • Media on the Go: Snap photos/videos, especially spatial videos. Play music and podcasts, or take calls through the built-in speakers.
  • Navigation Help: Get turn-by-turn directions whispered in your ear or displayed in AR.
  • Find My Integration: Lost your keys? The glasses could spot them via camera and ping your iPhone.
  • Visual Intelligence: Spot landmarks, animals, or outfits? It’ll tell you. Plus, gesture controls via hand waves.
  • Privacy Perks: A patent hints at “blurring” your iPhone screen for others while keeping it crystal-clear through the glasses.
  • Controls: Voice commands rule, but touch the frame for quick actions.
  • Software: A custom version of visionOS dubbed as realityOS.

Apple may integrate its services, such as Apple Maps and Apple Music, for seamless use. According to MacRumors, Apple is conducting user surveys at its workplaces to determine the popularity of various features and interfaces.

These investigations, codenamed “Atlas,” are being overseen by Apple’s Product Systems Quality team. Additionally, the App Store could offer glasses-specific apps, making the device versatile for both work and play.

Other Rumors and What’s Next

According to the PowerOn newsletter, Apple is working on two versions of Apple Glasses. First up, the “N50” model, which might not feature a display and work with an iPhone in 2027. Later, AR lenses might launch with actual screens by 2028.

Also, there’s an eye-tracking patent indicating the glass may integrate invisible sensors to follow your gaze for seamless controls. However, Apple is struggling to balance battery life, AI chip heat, and privacy regulations.

Wrapping It Up: Are Apple Glasses Worth the Hype?

Right now, Apple Glasses feel like the missing link between your phone and a truly hands-free life. Rumors so far indicate it will be smarter than Ray-Bans and sleeker than any headset.

If rumors hold, 2026/2027 could mark the start of a new era of AI-capable eyewear. Of course, this is all based on leaks; Apple could surprise us. Keep an eye on our guide for the most updated news!

What feature excites you most? Drop a comment, I’d love to hear.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

keyPoints.title: Apple's Lightweight Smart Glasses Development
keyPoints.explanation: Apple is working on slim, wearable smart glasses expected to launch around 2026-2027, complementing its Vision Pro headset but with a more discreet design.

keyPoints.title: Expected Features and Design of Apple Glasses
keyPoints.explanation: The glasses are anticipated to feature cameras, microphones, speakers, AI integration, and various frame options, aiming for a stylish, everyday look rather than a bulky AR headset.

keyPoints.title: Release Timeline and Predictions by Analyst Ming-Chi Kuo
keyPoints.explanation: Apple might unveil the glasses in 2026, with a full release in 2027, and the development of advanced AR versions possibly launching in 2028.

keyPoints.title: Pricing and Market Positioning of Apple Glasses
keyPoints.explanation: Rumors suggest an affordable price around $499, competing with Meta's $380 Ray-Bans, with potential bundles to boost value.

keyPoints.title: Innovative Hardware and Features to Expect from Apple Glasses
keyPoints.explanation: Key hardware may include MicroLED or OLED screens, built-in cameras, microphones, custom chips, and Bluetooth/Wi-Fi connectivity, focusing on AI-powered smart functionalities.

title.rendered: Best 14-Inch MacBook Pro Cases You Should Buy Now (2026)

content.rendered:
The 14-inch MacBook Pro remains a favorite for professionals and students, thanks to its powerful M-series chips, stunning display, and compact design. But its premium aluminum build makes it a bit fragile to scratches, bumps, or drops.

So, you need a good case to keep it safe, portable, and stylish without adding too much bulk. In the following guide, I’ll share some of the best 14-inch MacBook Pro cases to buy in 2026.

Table of Contents`
  • What Should You Consider in a MacBook Pro Case?
  • 6 Best Cases for 14-Inch MacBook Pro
    • 1. Spigen Thin Fit Case
    • 2. SUPCASE Rugged Protective Case
    • 3. MOSISO Case with Keyboard and Screen Cover
    • 4. CASETiFY Impact Case
    • 5. Incase Dots Hardshell with Makrolon
    • 6. BlueSwan Flexible Cover
  • Our Verdict: Which Case is Best for You?

What Should You Consider in a MacBook Pro Case?

Choosing the right case begins with understanding your needs. Here’s what matters most:

  • Protection Level: Consider how and where you use your MacBook. If you are always on the go, look for a shockproof or drop-tested case.
  • Weight and Fit: As the 14-inch MacBook Pro is already quite compact, you won’t want a bulky case that ruins its portability.
  • Ventilation and Heat Management: A good case will have ventilation cutouts that allow your laptop to breathe properly.
  • Material and Feel: The options are vast-from polycarbonate shells to flexible TPU or hybrid builds. Choose one that suits your comfort and style.
  • Ease of Installation and Access: Ports, hinge movement, and screen opening shouldn’t be restricted. Also, if you remove your case often, it should snap on and off easily. 
  • Price and Extras: Keep a budget of $15-50 for quality. Perks like screen protectors add value, but skip flashy designs if they compromise function.

Thinking through these helps match a case to your lifestyle, whether you’re backpack-toting or desk-bound.

6 Best Cases for 14-Inch MacBook Pro

Now that we know what to look for, let’s go through some of the top-rated cases available. Each one has a slightly different approach to protection and usability. 

1. Spigen Thin Fit Case

If you are a minimalist like me, you will love this ultra-slim case. The Spigen Thin Fit case keeps your MacBook Pro sleek and adds little to no weight. It’s made from dIf you are a minimalist like me, you will love this ultra-slim case. The Spigen Thin Fit case keeps your MacBook Pro sleek and adds little to no weight. It’s made from hard polycarbonate for durability and longevity. Also, your new MacBook Pro remains scratch-proof and crystal-clear.

Besides, it has added bumps around the hinge, and TPU rubberized feet provide a non-slip grip and protect against drops. Finally, I liked its snap-on design that makes installation simple. The precise cuts ensure proper heat ventilation and easy access to USB-C ports and charging.

Spigen also offers a Knit Fabric case for a premium look.

2. SUPCASE Rugged Protective Case

The SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle MacBook Pro case offers military-grade protection from drops and scratches. The design includes shock-absorbing wraparound TPU bumpers, a transparent back panel, and a dual-layer hybrid polycarbonate exterior.  

The material is totally free from BPA, BPS, and BPF. Thanks to the two-piece snap-on installation system, you can easily attach it to your MacBook. Moreover, the raised rubber feet and honeycomb air vents aid in heat dissipation. After purchase, you will receive a 365-day warranty for this award-winning case. 

Overall, this one is ideal for travelers, students, or people who often move between offices and outdoor settings. 

3. MOSISO Case with Keyboard and Screen Cover

The MOSISO case for the 14-inch MacBook Pro comes with a color-matched keyboard cover skin, a screen protector, and a pouch. So, it protects against spills, dust, and smudges. The case is a polycarbonate shell with no cut-out design. Therefore, you can access all buttons and ports without removing it. 

Moreover, there are two rows of ventilation to avoid overheating. Also, the keyboard cover is detachable and waterproof. But the case sometimes gets scratches and stains due to its smooth texture. On the other hand, the brand offers a wide selection of solid-color cases, so browse them and choose the one that suits you best.

4. CASETiFY Impact Case

CASETiFY’s Impact Case comes in versatile designs especially for the aesthetic crowd. It combines scratch-resistant polycarbonate with shock-absorbing bumpers to offer strong protection without being overly bulky.

Enhanced ventilation slots align with the laptop’s fans, and anti-slip grips prevent slipping. You can choose among customizable prints or patterns to match your vibe. So, it makes your MacBook stand out while still keeping it safe.

5. Incase Dots Hardshell with Makrolon

Incase’s Dots Hardshell uses premium Makrolon polycarbonate for an ultra-durable yet lightweight cover, emphasizing minimalism. Its polka-dot texture adds grip and prevents scuffs. Moreover, you can show off your MacBook’s design with its clear or semi-transparent finish.

The case snaps on easily, with precise cutouts and rubberized feet for stability. If you want premium quality and don’t mind spending a little extra for a refined finish, this is a top-tier choice. 

6. BlueSwan Flexible Cover

The BlueSwan 14-inch MacBook Pro Flexible Cover is quickly gaining attention for its blend of flexibility and durability. Unlike stiff plastic shells, it uses a slightly soft yet ultra-tough polypropylene (PP) material that wraps the MacBook securely.

The specially treated PP surface gives the case a frosted matte finish. So, you don’t need to worry about fingerprints, grease, or other stains. Also, it feels great to hold. The cover is only 1mm thick, making it close to invisible on the Space Black model.

Strengths lie in easy installation, though it may stretch slightly over the years. If you want forgiving protection for casual use without rigid edges, this covers the essentials affordably.

Our Verdict: Which Case is Best for You?  

No single case rules them all, it’s about your lifestyle.

  • For slim, everyday carry without extras, the Spigen Thin Fit nails affordability and ease.
  • For rugged durability, SUPCASE wins easily.  
  • If spills and dust bug you, MOSISO’s bundle is a practical all-rounder.
  • Those who love style and personality should check out CASETiFY. 
  • For premium build and sleek design, Incase Dots is worth it.  
  • And if you want a comfortable, flexible option, BlueSwan is surprisingly solid.  

Ultimately, measure your risks according to your usecase. A well-chosen case extends your MacBook’s life, letting you focus on the work that matters.

What’s your setup like? Drop a comment below.

  • Best Sleeves for 14-inch MacBook Pro

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

@graph.name: Spigen Thin Fit Case
@graph.description: The Spigen Thin Fit case keeps your MacBook Pro sleek and adds little to no weight. It’s made from hard polycarbonate for durability and longevity. Also, your new MacBook Pro remains scratch-proof and crystal-clear.

@graph.name: SUPCASE Rugged Protective Case
@graph.description: The SUPCASE Unicorn Beetle MacBook Pro case offers military-grade protection from drops and scratches. The design includes shock-absorbing wraparound TPU bumpers, a transparent back panel, and a dual-layer hybrid polycarbonate exterior.

@graph.name: MOSISO Case with Keyboard and Screen Cover
@graph.description: The MOSISO case for the 14-inch MacBook Pro comes with a color-matched keyboard cover skin, a screen protector, and a pouch. So, it protects against spills, dust, and smudges. The case is a polycarbonate shell with no cut-out design. Therefore, you can access all buttons and ports without removing it.

@graph.name: CASETiFY Impact Case
@graph.description: CASETiFY’s Impact Case comes in versatile designs especially for the aesthetic crowd. It combines scratch-resistant polycarbonate with shock-absorbing bumpers to offer strong protection without being overly bulky.

@graph.name: Incase Dots Hardshell with Makrolon
@graph.description: Incase’s Dots Hardshell uses premium Makrolon polycarbonate for an ultra-durable yet lightweight cover, emphasizing minimalism. Its polka-dot texture adds grip and prevents scuffs.

@graph.name: BlueSwan Flexible Cover
@graph.description: The BlueSwan 14-inch MacBook Pro Flexible Cover is quickly gaining attention for its blend of flexibility and durability. Unlike stiff plastic shells, it uses a slightly soft yet ultra-tough polypropylene (PP) material that wraps the MacBook securely.

title.rendered: How to Restore Closed Safari Tabs on iPhone, iPad, and Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why Safari tabs close accidentally: Tabs may disappear due to accidental gestures, app crashes, automatic cleanup, software bugs, or shared device activity.
  • Use Shake to Undo to reopen closed tabs: Enable Shake to Undo under Accessibility settings, then shake your iPhone or iPad to instantly reopen the last closed Safari tab.
  • Recover tabs via the Tabs Switcher: Press and hold the “+” button in Safari’s Tabs view to see and reopen your recently closed tabs with one tap.
  • Find lost tabs in Safari History: Open the Bookmarks icon, select the History tab, and browse through your visited pages to reopen any missing sites.
  • How to restore closed tabs on Mac: Press Command + Z to undo a tab closure or check the History menu for a list of recently closed pages to reopen them.

Have you accidentally closed an important tab in Safari and can’t remember which page it was? Don’t worry; we’ve all been there. Whether it’s an unintentional tap, a glitch, or a crash, Safari makes it easy to reopen closed tabs on iPhone, iPad, and Mac.

Here’s your complete guide to restoring closed Safari tabs in iOS 26 and macOS Sequoia.

Table of Contents
  • Why Safari Tabs Close Accidentally on iPhone or iPad
  • How to Restore Accidentally Closed Safari Tabs on iPhone or iPad
    • 1. Use “Shake to Undo”
    • 2. Reopen Recently Closed Safari Tabs from Tabs Switcher
    • 3. Restore Closed Safari Tabs from History
  • Tips to Avoid Losing Tabs
  • How to Reopen Recently Closed Tabs in Safari for Mac
    • 1. Use Keyboard Shortcut
    • 2. Use the New Tab Icon
    • 3. Check Your Safari History
  • Get Back Your Tabs!

Why Safari Tabs Close Accidentally on iPhone or iPad

Before jumping into the fixes, it helps to understand why tabs disappear in the first place:

  • Accidental taps or swipes: When quickly switching tabs, it’s easy to hit the close button or swipe a tab away.
  • App crashes or low memory: A temporary freeze or crash can cause tabs to vanish when Safari reloads.
  • Automatic tab cleanup: Safari can automatically close tabs after a day, week, or month, depending on your settings. Go to Settings → Apps → Safari → Close Tabs → Manually to stop this.
  • Software bugs or updates: After a major iOS update, Safari may reset session data.
  • Clearing browsing data: Deleting Safari history or data removes open tabs.
  • Other users: If you share your device, someone may have closed your tabs or tab group.

How to Restore Accidentally Closed Safari Tabs on iPhone or iPad

Whatever the reason you mistakenly closed Safari tabs, these solutions will surely help.

1. Use “Shake to Undo”

Believe me, the iPhone’s Shake to Undo feature is a lifesaver. It’s an Accessibility feature that allows you to quickly undo or redo certain actions. For example, you can quickly undo or redo typing and restore recently closed Safari tabs.

This feature is enabled by default. So, when you accidentally close an active Safari tab, simply shake your iPhone → Pick the Undo Close Tab from the pop-up to reopen the web page.

If you are unable to use this feature for some reason, you may need to enable it manually. 

  1. Open Settings → Head to Accessibility.  
  2. Tap Touch under the Physical and Motor section. 
  3. Now, toggle on Shake to Undo if it is not already.

You can use the Shake to Undo feature to instantly restore the last closed tab. But what if you want to reopen multiple closed Safari tabs?

2. Reopen Recently Closed Safari Tabs from Tabs Switcher

Well, there’s a secret Safari trick that helps you do that. Safari has a hidden Recently Closed Tabs list that lets you access all your past browsing sessions.

  1. Open Safari → Tap the three-dot icon next to the address bar, then tap All Tabs.
  2. Tap and hold the + (plus) icon at the bottom left corner.  
  3. Doing so will open the list of all recently closed tabs.
  4. Then tap the web page you want to reopen.

3. Restore Closed Safari Tabs from History

If you can’t find your closed tab in the “Recently Closed Tabs” list, it may have been deleted many days ago. This trick for retrieving closed tabs works not only in Safari but also in most other iPhone browsers. 

  1. Open Safari → Tap the three-dot icon and select the Bookmark icon below the address bar. 
  2. Go to the Personal History tab (Clock icon 🕘) on the right. 
  3. Select your desired day or date. Select the Web Page you want to reopen.
  4. You can tap and hold the page and open the tab in a dedicated Tab Group.  

Accessing your Safari browsing history can also help if you are dealing with the disappearing Safari tabs issue on your iPhone.

Tips to Avoid Losing Tabs

While researching a topic, I sometimes accidentally close tabs in Safari. So, I use a few tricks to keep my tabs open. You may also follow these tips to mitigate the problem:

  • Enable iCloud Tabs: You may enable iCloud Tabs to sync your Safari open tabs and Tab Groups across devices. So, if you close tabs by mistake, you can often recover them from another device. To enable this, access Settings → Your Apple ID → iCloud → Saved to iCloud → Toggle on Safari.
  • Use Reading List: Save important tabs to keep them open and accessible. It also lets you read those saved webpages while offline.
  • Create Tab Groups: Group related pages (e.g., “Research” or “Shopping”) to organize them and reopen them at any time.
  • Be cautious with gestures: When using Safari on your iPhone, be mindful of your swipes and taps to avoid unintentionally closing tabs.

How to Reopen Recently Closed Tabs in Safari for Mac

If you have lost all your Safari tabs while browsing on a Mac, you can quickly restore them.

1. Use Keyboard Shortcut

The easiest way to restore accidentally closed Safari tabs is to use keyboard shortcuts. Simply press Command (⌘) + Z to undo closing the last tab.

However, if you have performed another action after the tab is closed, this shortcut will undo that action rather than reopening the tab. In this case, the Shift + Command (⌘) + T shortcut can reopen the most recently closed tab.

Whichever Keyboard shortcut you use, press it repeatedly to reopen multiple recently closed tabs on Safari.

2. Use the New Tab Icon

You can use Safari’s New Tab icon to get a list of recently closed tabs. Right-click on the + icon at the top right corner of the window. Then select the tab you want to reopen. It will restore it to the location where you first opened it. Thus, you can continue browsing the tabs as organized as before.

However, you accidentally closed the Safari window, so you can’t find the list of recently closed tabs. Therefore, move to the next solution.

3. Check Your Safari History

Safari records all your browsing activity under the History menu. While a Safari window is open, click History on the menu bar and select Recently Closed. Choose the tab you want to reopen. If your Safari app crashed or was closed accidentally, select Reopen All Windows from Last Session.

You can choose a method and restore all accidentally closed Safari tabs on a Mac based on the number of tabs.

Get Back Your Tabs!

That’s how you restore closed Safari tabs on your iPhone, iPad and Mac. I suggest following the tips I mentioned to avoid losing Safari tabs. Even if you accidentally hit the close (x) button on a Safari tab, use any of the methods shown in this article.

FAQs

Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

Yes, iCloud stores your Safari tabs if iCloud Sync is enabled for Safari, but they are not included in iCloud backups. When iCloud sync is enabled, your tabs are available on all Apple devices signed in with your Apple ID. To preserve Safari tabs, you should use an encrypted computer backup.

Does Safari back up iPhone tabs? 

Yes, but only if you allowed Safari to use iCloud in the first place. If you have, then all your Safari Bookmarks, Reading List, Tab Groups, and open browser tabs are automatically backed up.

How long does Safari History stay on iPhone or iPad?

iPhones can store Safari history for up to a month.

  • What are Safari Profiles and how to use them on iPhone, iPad, or Mac
  • How to change the default search engine in Safari
  • How to mute Safari tabs on Mac

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

acceptedAnswer.text: The App Store may use your location to provide region-specific content or comply with local regulations.

mainEntity.name: What if I can't change date/time or location settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: If your device is managed by your employer, school, or parental controls, some settings may be restricted. Check for device management profiles under Settings → General → VPN & Device Management.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Why does the App Store need my location?

mainEntity.name: Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, iCloud stores your Safari tabs if iCloud Sync is enabled for Safari, but they are not included in iCloud backups. mainEntity.name: Does Safari back up iPhone tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only if you allowed Safari to use iCloud in the first place. If you have, then all your Safari Bookmarks, Reading List, Tab Groups, and open browser tabs are automatically backed up.

He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."  About Dhvanesh Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity. From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple. A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development. Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience. Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

keyPoints.title: Why Safari Tabs Close Accidentally on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Tabs can close due to accidental taps, app crashes, automatic cleanup, software bugs, data clearing, or sharing devices.

keyPoints.title: Using Shake to Undo to Restore Tabs on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Shake to Undo is a helpful feature that allows you to quickly reopen the last closed Safari tab by shaking your device, which can be enabled in Accessibility settings.

keyPoints.title: Reopening Tabs via Tabs Switcher on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: You can access recently closed tabs in Safari by holding the '+' icon in the Tabs Switcher, then selecting the tab to reopen from the list.

keyPoints.title: Restoring Closed Safari Tabs from History
keyPoints.explanation: If recent tabs aren’t available, check Safari’s history by opening the Bookmark icon, navigating to the history tab, and selecting the desired page to reopen.

keyPoints.title: Restoring Closed Safari Tabs on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: On Mac, you can press Command+Z to undo closing the last tab or use the New Tab icon’s history option, and also check your browsing history under the History menu to reopen tabs.

title.rendered: New Apple TV and HomePod Mini Could Launch Soon

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Retail refresh hints at new hardware on November 12, as Apple schedules an overnight Apple Store update—a typical move ahead of launches.
  • Apple TV and HomePod mini supply is drying up, fueling speculation that updated models are on the verge of release.
  • Siri overhaul may be a key feature, with Apple expected to preview next-gen Apple Intelligence via refreshed home devices.
  • Late-year launch would be rare for Apple, but smaller home gadgets sometimes get quiet November updates via store changes.
  • No Mac or iPad updates expected in 2025, making Apple TV and HomePod mini the likely final hardware refreshes of the year.

Apple might be on the brink of releasing updated versions of its Apple TV and HomePod mini, potentially catching many by surprise. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman shares in his latest Power On newsletter that a notable overnighxt refresh in Apple retail stores is slated for November 11, which could herald new products hitting shelves the next day.

Apple Store Refresh Hints at Possible Launch

Per Gurman’s reporting, Apple retail staff are set to carry out an overnight refresh, marking a routine usually designated for launching new gadgets or revamping store displays. Although this could just be for sprucing up stores for the holiday season, the timing has ignited rumors that updated Apple TV and HomePod mini models might make an appearance on November 12.

Additional reports highlight that both devices are experiencing inventory shortages in various regions, often a telltale sign of forthcoming new models. Gurman further suggests that even if these launches aren’t imminent, they likely aren’t too far down the road.

Designed to Showcase Siri and Apple Intelligence

Should these new models emerge, they are anticipated to feature Apple’s upcoming Siri revamp alongside next-gen Apple Intelligence capabilities, set for introduction next year. This update aims to make Siri more adept at engaging in dialogue and better at managing everyday tasks. Having revamped home devices on the market preemptively would align with Apple’s overarching strategy to bolster its smart home presence.

In Apple’s recent earnings call, CEO Tim Cook referred to the current lineup as their “most extraordinary yet,” which seems to indicate no new Mac or iPad announcements are expected for the remainder of 2025. This leaves the Apple TV and HomePod mini as prime candidates for hardware updates before the year closes.

Also read: Apple Drops the “+” as Apple TV+ Becomes Just Apple TV

Why a November Launch Is Unusual for Apple

Apple doesn’t typically release new hardware late in the calendar year. The company generally wraps up major product announcements by October to gear up for the holiday shopping season. However, smaller scale updates, particularly for accessories and home devices, sometimes quietly roll out via store adjustments or press releases. This makes a subtle store changeover or an understated announcement plausible.

Even if the new models don’t surface immediately, all indicators point to updated versions arriving soon, especially as Apple gears up for its major Siri overhaul scheduled for early 2026.

Would a new Apple TV or HomePod mini interest you? Share your thoughts below.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

acceptedAnswer.text: When you want to find something specific in the Messages app, you can perform a search. On the main All Messages screen, swipe down slightly to display the Search box at the top. Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: How to search in iMessage?

Pop in your search term and you’ll see results from every conversation related to that term, including text, photos, links, or other items.

mainEntity.name: Do iMessage photos get saved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Even with the Automatic Sharing feature enabled, as explained here, photos and videos you receive in Messages are not saved by default. If you delete the conversation, the photos will be deleted too. You can check out our how-to for saving photos from Messages to your iPhone or iPad to hold onto those important pictures.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: How to change the keyboard on your iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Switching the keyboard on the iPhone is easy. Open Settings → tap General → Keyboard → Keyboards → tap Add New Keyboard → Edit → drag the preferred keyboard using the three lines. For more details, take a look at this comprehensive guide to changing the keyboard on iPhone.

mainEntity.name: Why does my iPhone say "Cannot Connect to App Store" even with good internet?

acceptedAnswer.text: This may happen due to incorrect date and time settings, issues with your Apple ID, or App Store server problems. Verify these settings first.

mainEntity.name: Will I lose my data if I reset the network or all settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Resetting network settings only erases Wi-Fi and Bluetooth settings. Resetting all settings doesn't erase personal data, but does revert all system settings.

mainEntity.name: Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, iCloud stores your Safari tabs if iCloud Sync is enabled for Safari, but they are not included in iCloud backups. When iCloud sync is enabled, your tabs are available on all Apple devices signed in with your Apple ID. To preserve Safari tabs, you should use an encrypted computer backup.

mainEntity.name: Does Safari back up iPhone tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only if you allowed Safari to use iCloud in the first place. If you have, then all your Safari Bookmarks, Reading List, Tab Groups, and open browser tabs are automatically backed up.

title.rendered: New Version of Siri to Depend on Google Gemini

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Siri overhaul arrives March 2026 with Apple’s most ambitious update yet, focused on natural conversation, task handling, and smarter web answers.
  • Google’s Gemini powers Siri silently through a custom model running on Apple’s Private Cloud, keeping Siri private, Apple-branded, and off Google’s ecosystem.
  • New Apple hardware to showcase Siri includes a smart home display, updated HomePod mini, and refreshed Apple TV, all launching alongside the upgraded assistant.
  • AI-driven web search comes to Siri, letting you get answers without opening Safari as part of Apple’s expanding Apple Intelligence initiative.
  • China launch faces ongoing delays, with Apple Intelligence rollout described as a “target,” not a guarantee, due to local regulatory hurdles.

Apple’s next major upgrade to Siri is arriving in early 2026, and this time, they’re not going solo. As per Mark Gurman’s latest Power On newsletter from Bloomberg, Apple’s upcoming Siri will tap into Google’s Gemini AI model to enhance its intelligence and web search functionalities.

Siri’s Biggest Overhaul Slated for March 2026

According to reports, Apple plans to unveil its overhauled Siri in March 2026, alongside a smart home display available in both speaker-base and wall-mount configurations. This update will coincide with the release of new HomePod mini and Apple TV models, both set to highlight the improved Siri and Apple Intelligence experience.

This upgrade is poised to be one of Siri’s most ambitious since its debut over a decade ago. Gurman suggests that Apple’s goal is for Siri to feel more natural, contextually aware, and proficient in managing real-world tasks beyond basic queries.

Powered by Gemini, But Fully Apple’s Own

Even though Siri will lean on Google’s Gemini for its backend AI model, Gurman notes that this doesn’t mean Apple is integrating Google’s ecosystem or directly using its services. Rather, Apple is financially engaging Google to develop a custom Gemini-based model that operates exclusively on Apple’s Private Cloud Compute servers. This ensures Siri gets the benefit from Gemini’s capabilities while maintaining Apple’s privacy commitments and user interface consistency.

So, users won’t notice any Gemini-branded elements; Siri will stay distinctively Apple in its design and user experience, just smarter on the inside.

Enhanced Web Search and Expanded Apple Intelligence

A key upgrade will be the introduction of AI-driven web search, enabling Siri to deliver more pertinent and detailed responses without needing to launch Safari. This change fits with Apple’s broader Apple Intelligence initiative, which continues to integrate across iPhones, iPads, and Macs.

Gurman mentions that during WWDC 2026, Apple is set to preview iOS 27, macOS 27, and watchOS 27, with an emphasis on deeper integration of Apple Intelligence. The new Siri is anticipated to be instrumental in this expansion, merging everyday practical use with generative AI capabilities.

Ongoing Delays for Apple Intelligence in China

Despite intentions for a global rollout, Apple faces regulatory obstacles in China. Even with local collaborations, Gurman reports that the launch of Apple Intelligence in China remains uncertain, describing it as a “rollout target.”

Apple’s collaboration with Google’s Gemini signifies a notable shift in its AI strategy, opting for functionality over self-reliance. Whether this new Siri will regain user trust after years of stagnation remains uncertain, but 2026 is gearing up to be a pivotal year for Apple’s AI endeavors.

Would you find this shift significant? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: Apple’s bold 2026 Siri upgrade blends Gemini AI power with Apple’s privacy-first design, ushering in the next era of intelligent, natural voice interaction.

mainEntity.name: Can I delete certain words from the iPhone keyboard?

acceptedAnswer.text: While you can reset your keyboard to remove words from iPhone Predictive text, the iPhone doesn't have a built-in method for deleting certain words from the keyboard. That said, some third-party keyboards allow you to do so.

mainEntity.name: Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, iCloud stores your Safari tabs if iCloud Sync is enabled for Safari, but they are not included in iCloud backups. mainEntity.name: Does Safari back up iPhone tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but only if you allowed Safari to use iCloud in the first place. If you have, then all your Safari Bookmarks, Reading List, Tab Groups, and open browser tabs are automatically backed up.
