title.rendered: WhatsApp for Apple Watch Is Finally Happening

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • WhatsApp expands testing to Apple Watch: Meta is trialing a dedicated Apple Watch app through TestFlight, marking its next step beyond the iPad companion rollout.
  • Core messaging tools on your wrist: You can now read chats, reply with emojis, and send voice messages directly from your Apple Watch during testing.
  • Works as a companion, not standalone yet: The Apple Watch version mirrors WhatsApp on iPhone and iPad, syncing chats automatically without manual QR setup.
  • Still tied to your iPhone: WhatsApp for Apple Watch requires an active iPhone connection for now, though future multi-device updates may enable standalone use.
  • Limited beta with no launch timeline: Meta hasn’t confirmed a public release date, keeping the Apple Watch app restricted to select TestFlight users for ongoing testing.

WhatsApp is gearing up to extend its reach to the Apple Watch. After the introduction of its iPad companion app, the messaging giant is now testing an app specifically for Apple Watch. This rollout is currently limited to select Testflight users.

Meta hasn’t delivered an official announcement regarding this development. However, WABetaInfo, a respected source for all things WhatsApp, first brought this information to light. The new Apple Watch app addresses the noticeable absence of complete WhatsApp support, which previously left users dependent on basic notifications or third-party apps.

Core WhatsApp Features Come to Your Wrist

The new Apple Watch app is set to bring essential WhatsApp functions directly to your wrist. With it, users can explore chats, read and reply to messages, send emoji responses, and share voice messages, all without having to open the app on their iPhone.

This app isn’t entirely standalone yet. It acts as a companion to the iOS version, mirroring the setup seen with the iPad app. This approach offers a more seamless and integrated messaging experience than previously available. To assist with usability, the app syncs automatically with your iPhone, removing the need for QR code scanning or manual linking.

Still Requires an iPhone for Now

Right now, the Apple Watch app relies on having an iPhone with WhatsApp installed, as it duplicates the connection, syncing messages and alerts in real time through the paired device. Although it isn’t entirely independent, this could potentially change as WhatsApp further develops its multi-device support—which already includes tablets, web browsers, and secondary phones.

No Word Yet on Public Release

Meta has not confirmed this feature in an official blog post, so there’s currently no timeline for a public release on the App Store. As it stands in Testflight, only a select group of beta testers have access. However, the beginning of testing could hint at a broader debut in the months ahead, depending on positive feedback.

We’ll keep you updated on the latest developments in WhatsApp’s journey towards Apple Watch integration. Would the addition of WhatsApp on your wrist matter to you? Share your thoughts.

title.rendered: Affinity Goes Completely Free with Unified Mac App

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Affinity merges all design apps into one platform, combining Designer, Photo, and Publisher into a unified free app for Mac and Windows users.
  • Canva integration enables seamless mode switching between Vector, Pixel, and Layout tools, preserving professional workflows within a customizable workspace.
  • Core tools remain completely free for all users, while Canva Premium members gain access to advanced AI-powered features like Generative Fill and Remove Background.
  • A universal file format improves compatibility, allowing smooth editing and exporting between Affinity and Canva without file conversions.
  • Move challenges Adobe’s subscription model, offering professionals a cost-free, high-performance alternative to Creative Cloud software.
  • Available now for Mac and Windows, with an iPad version slated for 2026 and continued support for existing iPad apps.

Affinity, under the ownership of Canva since a recent acquisition, combines its popular design applications Affinity Designer, Affinity Photo, and Affinity Publisher into a single, free app for both Mac and Windows users. This unified app will take over from the existing separate products, maintaining all key features.

Canva Combines All Affinity Apps Into One Platform

The newly minted app, known simply as Affinity, integrates the functionalities of all three former apps, allowing users to switch effortlessly among Vector, Pixel, and Layout modes with a single click. These modes deliver the same capabilities offered by Affinity Designer, Photo, and Publisher, now housed within a seamless workspace. Canva has redesigned the app considerably, featuring customizable toolbars to let users tailor their workspace as they see fit. Users also have the option to save and share their customized spaces, aiming to streamline team workflows.

Completely Free With No Subscriptions

Canva underscores that Affinity will be offered free of charge, forever, with no strings attached for core features. Access requires only a basic, free Canva account. However, those subscribed to Canva Premium gain access to advanced AI-enhanced functionalities like Generative Fill and Remove Background, alongside quick image expansion.

For those who have previously purchased the older Affinity apps, these will remain operational, although they’re now absent from Affinity’s website. While Mac and Windows versions of this new app are already available, iPad users will have to wait until 2026 for their version. Meanwhile, existing iPad apps will continue to function without disruption.

One Universal File Type and Native Integration With Canva

The revamped Affinity app introduces a universal file format compatible with all design workflows, simplifying the process of editing and exporting designs without the hassle of converting formats. The app also integrates seamlessly with Canva, ensuring smooth sharing and exporting between both platforms. Moreover, those paying for Canva’s services can employ AI-powered tools directly within Affinity, blurring the divide between Canva’s easy-to-use tools and Affinity’s more professional-grade environment.

Designed for Professionals, Guided by Creators

Affinity CEO Ash Hewson noted that this initiative was designed to eliminate financial barriers and provide full creative freedom. The app retains the precision and performance that designers expect but now opens up to everyone. The overhaul was informed by Canva’s Designer Advisory Board and influenced by feedback from professional users prioritizing reliability and creative control.

A Strategic Step Against Adobe

Canva’s strategy to offer Affinity at no cost sets it directly in contrast with Adobe, which remains reliant on subscription fees for its Creative Cloud services. Previously, individual Affinity apps were priced around $70 or $170 for the suite, but eliminating these costs suggests Canva’s bid to attract professionals who are possibly discontented with Adobe’s subscription model.

Although a Canva account is necessary to use Affinity, Canva assures that its integration won’t compromise user privacy, with AI features being optional and personal projects not used to train AI models.

Affinity’s comprehensive app is readily available for both Mac and Windows, with an iPad version planned for future release. Interested users can download the app from Affinity’s official site or the Mac App Store at no cost.

Does this change matter to you? Share your thoughts below.

excerpt.rendered: Canva unifies Affinity’s design suite into a single free app for Mac and Windows, blending professional-grade tools with optional AI features and cross-platform integration.

title.rendered: Threads for iPhone Gains Reply Approvals, Activity Feed Options

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Reply Approvals now control who gets seen on Threads posts, letting you review replies before they appear publicly to reduce spam or off-topic chatter.
  • Unapproved replies move to a new Ignored tab, so you can revisit and approve them later without losing full visibility or control.
  • Activity tab adds Mentions and People You Follow, making it easier to filter replies and focus on interactions that matter most to you.
  • Features are iPhone-only for now, but Meta confirms a broader rollout is coming and will continue tuning based on user feedback.
  • Precaution: Reply Approvals must be set during post creation—you can’t enable it retroactively after posting, so plan ahead.

Meta is enhancing its Threads app on iPhone with two features designed to improve user control over conversations and reply visibility. The update now includes reply approvals as well as new filters in the Activity tab. These tools aim to make the app more user-friendly and focused.

Big Change: Managing Who Can Reply

The standout addition is the Reply Approvals feature. This gives Threads users the ability to review and approve replies before they appear on their posts. Unapproved replies are kept out of public view but can be revisited later in an Ignored tab if users decide to approve them at a later time.

According to Meta, this feature is intended to help users maintain relevant discussions and cut down on inappropriate comments. It’s accessible when making a post, right where options for who can reply or quote your post are located. This is another step in ensuring discussions remain respectful and within users’ control before they go live.

Building on previous moderation tools like hiding offensive or spam replies, these updates showcase Meta’s intent to offer users a safer and more personalized space for interaction.

Also Read: Threads Introduces Ghost Posts That Disappear After 24 Hours

Customizing the Activity Feed

Threads is not stopping there. It also introduces new filters in the Activity tab, namely Mentions and People You Follow. These join the existing filters like All, Follows, Conversations, Reposts, and Verified, simplifying the tracking of important interactions.

For instance, if you prefer seeing replies exclusively from friends or followed accounts, the new filter facilitates this with just one tap. Meanwhile, the Mentions filter helps ensure you don’t overlook direct interactions pointing to your profile or posts.

Meta states that these features are rolling out gradually on iPhone and are likely to extend to other platforms soon. They’re also continually collecting user feedback to further refine the Threads experience.

Threads’ Continuing Growth

Introduced in 2023 as Meta’s counterpart to X (previously Twitter), Threads has grown quickly, boasting over 150 million daily active users. Over time, the app has seen updates like post editing, secret replies, fediverse sharing, and extended text limits. The latest improvements strengthen a pattern of focusing on user autonomy and interaction quality.

These changes underscore Meta’s ongoing efforts to make Threads a platform where users can freely express themselves while deciding what content is visible on their profiles.

Does this increase your interest in Threads? Share your thoughts below.

Check: Threads Rolls Out 100+ Topic Communities to Rival X and Reddit

title.rendered: How to Install watchOS 26 on Your Apple Watch

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple Watch models compatible with watchOS 26: The update supports Apple Watch Ultra, Series 11 through 6, and SE (2nd and 3rd gen) models, ensuring broad device coverage.
  • Requirements before installing watchOS 26: Your paired iPhone must run iOS 16 or later, both devices need at least 50% battery, Wi-Fi access, and close proximity for syncing.
  • How to update Apple Watch without an iPhone: Connect your Watch to Wi-Fi and a charger, then go to Settings → General → Software Update to install watchOS 26 directly.
  • How to update using your iPhone: Open the Watch app, select General → Software Update, connect both devices to Wi-Fi, and follow the prompts to complete the installation.
  • Why updating to watchOS 26 matters: The update delivers new features like Liquid Glass UI, Workout Buddy, and Live Translation, while improving stability, performance, and bug fixes.

Apple’s biggest watchOS update in years, watchOS 26, is finally here. The new update introduces the all-new Liquid Glass UI, Workout Buddy, Live Translation in Messages, and much more to your Apple Watch. If you’re ready to explore everything it has to offer, you must first ensure that your Apple Watch supports watchOS 26.

If yes, continue reading to learn how to install the latest watchOS 26 on your Apple Watch.

Table of Contents
  • Is Your Apple Watch Compatible with watchOS 26?
  • Requirements to update watchOS 26
  • How to Update Apple Watch Directly
  • How to Update Apple Watch with Your Paired iPhone
  • All Set with watchOS 26….

Is Your Apple Watch Compatible with watchOS 26?

While Apple typically provides 5 years of software updates for Apple Watch, watchOS 26 continues to support the Apple Watch Series 6, launched in 2020.

Here’s a complete list of Apple Watch models that support watchOS 26:

  • Apple Watch Ultra (1st, 2nd, and 3rd generation)
  • Apple Watch Series 11
  • Apple Watch Series 10
  • Apple Watch Series 9
  • Apple Watch Series 8
  • Apple Watch Series 7
  • Apple Watch Series 6
  • Apple Watch SE (2nd and 3rd generation)

Requirements to update watchOS 26

  • Update your iPhone to the latest iOS 16.
  • Ensure the battery is at least 50% on both the iPhone and the Apple Watch.
  • Connect your iPhone and Apple Watch to a Wi-Fi network.
  • Keep your Apple Watch within the connection range of your iPhone to prevent disconnection.

How to Update Apple Watch Directly

To update your Apple Watch without an iPhone, connect the Apple Watch to Wi-Fi and plug it in to charge, then follow these steps:

  1. Open Settings on your Apple Watch.
  2. Tap General.
  3. Navigate to Software Update.

  4. If an update is available, tap Download and Install.

  5. Tap Proceed.
  6. The Apple Watch will restart once the update is installed.

How to Update Apple Watch with Your Paired iPhone

You do not need the paired iPhone to update the Apple Watch. However, the paired iPhone will send you a notification whenever an Apple Watch update is available. If you intend to update through the iPhone, follow these steps:

  1. Open the Watch app on your iPhone.
  2. Make sure your iPhone and Apple Watch are connected to Wi-Fi.
  3. Tap General.
  4. Select Software Update.
  5. On the next page, tap Download and Install Now.
  6. Enter your iPhone passcode.
  7. Read the terms and conditions. Once you’ve read the terms and wish to proceed, tap Agree.
  8. You might be asked to enter the Apple Watch passcode; once you do, the update process will begin.
  9. A progress wheel will appear on the Apple Watch. Plug the Apple Watch into a charger to prevent it from dying during the update process.
  10. Once the update is installed, the Apple Watch will restart and run the latest software version.
Note While the update is in process, please do not restart your iPhone or Apple Watch.

All Set with watchOS 26….

Updating your Apple Watch to watchOS 26 ensures it benefits from the latest features and stays free of software bugs that could affect its performance. With just a few taps, you can have your watch running the newest version and enjoy everything Apple has packed into it this year.

Read more:

  • Unable to update watchOS 26? Here’s how to fix it
  • watchOS 26 vs watchOS 11: Is Apple’s Latest Update Really Worth It?
  • How to use Live Activities on Apple Watch

aioseo_head_json.title: How to Update Your Apple Watch to watchOS 26
aioseo_head_json.description: Learn how to install watchOS 26 on your Apple Watch, check compatibility, and update using iPhone or directly on the watch with step-by-step instructions.

itemListElement.name: How to Install watchOS 26 on Your Apple Watch

@graph.name: How to Update Apple Watch Directly
@graph.description: Update your Apple Watch right from your wrist using the Settings app so you can install the latest features and security fixes without your iPhone.

supply.name: Apple Watch with at least 50% battery

step.name: Open Settings on Apple Watch
step.text: Press the Digital Crown to see your apps, then tap Settings to get started.

itemListElement.text: Press the Digital Crown to open the app grid or list.
Tap the Settings app icon.

step.name: Tap General
step.text: In Settings, scroll and tap General to view device options.

itemListElement.text: Scroll with the Digital Crown.
Select General from the list.

step.name: Open Software Update
step.text: Tap Software Update to check for the latest watchOS version available for your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Tap Software Update under General.

step.name: Download and install the update
step.text: If an update appears, tap Download and Install to begin fetching and installing the software.

itemListElement.text: Tap Download and Install when an update is available.

step.name: Confirm and proceed
step.text: When prompted, tap Proceed to confirm. Keep your watch on charge and connected to Wi-Fi during the update.

itemListElement.text: Tap Proceed to start installation.
Leave the watch on its charger until the update finishes.

step.name: Wait for the restart
step.text: Your Apple Watch will restart automatically once the installation completes, and you can resume using it after the watch face reappears.

itemListElement.text: Do not interrupt the process while the watch restarts.

@graph.name: How to Update Apple Watch with Your Paired iPhone
@graph.description: Update your Apple Watch using the Watch app on your iPhone so you can install the latest watchOS features and security fixes with a few simple steps.

supply.name: Apple Watch on charger with at least 50% battery

step.name: Open the Watch app on your iPhone
step.text: Unlock your iPhone and open the Watch app to manage Apple Watch settings.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Watch app icon on your Home Screen.

step.name: Confirm both devices are on Wi-Fi
step.text: Make sure your iPhone and Apple Watch are connected to the same Wi-Fi network for a smooth download.

itemListElement.text: Verify Wi-Fi is turned on for your iPhone and Apple Watch.

step.name: Open General settings
step.text: In the Watch app, tap General to access software options.

itemListElement.text: Tap General from the main settings list.

step.name: Select Software Update
step.text: Tap Software Update to check for the latest watchOS version available for your Apple Watch.

itemListElement.text: Open Software Update to see available updates.

step.name: Download and install the update
step.text: If an update is available, tap Download and Install Now to begin the process.

itemListElement.text: Tap Download and Install Now when prompted.

step.name: Authenticate on iPhone
step.text: Enter your iPhone passcode when asked, then read the terms and conditions. If you agree, tap Agree to continue.

itemListElement.text: Type your iPhone passcode to proceed.
Tap Agree after reviewing the terms and conditions.

step.name: Authenticate on Apple Watch if prompted
step.text: You may be asked to enter your Apple Watch passcode. Enter it to start the installation.

itemListElement.text: Enter your Apple Watch passcode on the watch screen.

step.name: Keep the watch charging during the update
step.text: A progress wheel will appear on your Apple Watch while the update installs. Keep the watch on its charger and do not interrupt the process.

itemListElement.text: Leave Apple Watch on the charger until the update completes.

step.name: Wait for the restart
step.text: Once installation finishes, your Apple Watch will restart automatically and run the latest software version.

itemListElement.text: Wait for the watch face to reappear before using the device.

keyPoints.title: Compatibility of Apple Watch with watchOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Most Apple Watch models released from Series 6 onward, including Ultra, Series 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, and SE (2nd and 3rd gen), support the latest watchOS 26 update.

keyPoints.title: Requirements for updating to watchOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: To update, ensure your iPhone runs iOS 16, both devices have at least 50% battery, are connected to Wi-Fi, and are within range of each other.

keyPoints.title: Updating Apple Watch without iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: You can update directly from your Apple Watch by connecting it to Wi-Fi, charging it, and navigating to Settings > General > Software Update to install the latest version.

keyPoints.title: Updating Apple Watch via iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Use the Watch app on your iPhone to download and install updates by connecting both devices to Wi-Fi, then following the on-screen instructions, including entering passcodes if prompted.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Updating to watchOS 26
keyPoints.explanation: Updating ensures your Apple Watch has the latest features, fixes bugs, and optimizes performance, allowing you to enjoy new functionalities like Liquid Glass UI, Workout Buddy, and Live Translation.

title.rendered: Best Screen Protectors for Apple Watch Ultra 3, Ultra 2, and Ultra in 2026

content.rendered:
The Apple Watch Ultra is Apple’s most rugged and premium smartwatch to date. Built with aerospace-grade titanium and sapphire crystal glass, it’s designed to handle extreme conditions. Still, even the toughest watch deserves protection. A simple scratch can dull its stunning display, and since accidents can happen anytime, adding a quality screen protector helps keep your Apple Watch Ultra looking brand new for years.

In this guide, I’ve listed the best screen protectors for the Apple Watch Ultra 3, Ultra 2, and the original Ultra, along with some key buying tips to help you choose the right one.

Table of Contents
  • Key Things to Check Before Buying an Apple Watch Ultra Screen Protector
  • 5 Best Screen Protectors for Apple Watch Ultra Series
    • 1. ESR Armorite Screen Protector
    • 2. Spigen Glas.tR EZ Fit Tempered Glass
    • 3. Ringke Easy Slide Tempered Glass
    • 4. ZAGG InvisibleShield Glass Fusion 360
    • 5. Ailun Tempered Glass Film
  • Apple Watch Ultra Screen Protector Installation Guide
  • Conclusion: Give Your Apple Watch Ultra the Protection It Deserves

Key Things to Check Before Buying an Apple Watch Ultra Screen Protector

With hundreds of Apple Watch Ultra 3 screen protectors available in the market, make sure to look out for these points before purchasing one:

  • Compatibility: Only buy a screen protector that clearly mentions “for Apple Watch Ultra/Ultra 2/Ultra 3.” Protectors made for regular Apple Watches will not fit correctly and interfere with the titanium casing.
  • Material: Choose between tempered glass for strong impact protection or TPU film for flexible edge coverage.
  • Clarity and Touch Sensitivity: Pick the one that offers high transparency and good touch responsiveness. Having an anti-smudge coating is an added advantage.
  • Case Compatibility: If you use a bumper case on your Apple Watch Ultra, pick a case-friendly screen protector that doesn’t lift at the corners or create bubbles when paired with a case.
  • Installation and Durability: Watch screens are small, and even a tiny dust particle can ruin installation. Look for protectors that include alignment frames, cleaning kits, and bubble-free adhesives.

5 Best Screen Protectors for Apple Watch Ultra Series

Here are my top picks for the best Apple Watch Ultra screen protectors that balance durability, clarity, and ease of use.

1. ESR Armorite Screen Protector

For those who are always up for an adventure, the ESR Armorite screen protector is the perfect choice. It offers military-grade toughness with 9H hardness, making it capable of handling almost everything you throw at it.

Having this screen protector on your expensive Apple Watch Ultra ensures the display remains crystal-clear and touch response remains smooth.

2. Spigen Glas.tR EZ Fit Tempered Glass

Spigen is one of the best accessories brands for smartphones and smartwatches, and the Glas.tR EZ Fit Tempered Glass for the Apple Watch Ultra further strengthens its legacy. It’s 9H hardness easily protects your Apple Watch Ultra from everyday bumps and scratches, while maintaining flawless touch accuracy.

The screen protector is compatible with Spigen Apple Watch Ultra cases and comes with an auto-alignment installation kit for effortless application.

3. Ringke Easy Slide Tempered Glass

Ringke’s Easy Slide protector provides edge-to-edge clarity and smudge resistance in a slim profile. The included alignment tool ensures a perfect fit on the Ultra’s flat sapphire display without lifting at the corners.

It features oleophobic coating, so you don’t have to worry about fingerprints and smudges ruining your display.

4. ZAGG InvisibleShield Glass Fusion 360

It’s the only screen protector on this list that comes with an integrated bumper for extra protection. This screen protector features a premium hybrid glass film that combines the strength of tempered glass with flexible polymers, offering impact protection and self-healing properties.

Besides offering all-around protection, it’s also treated with an oleophobic coating to keep your display free of fingerprints and smudges.

5. Ailun Tempered Glass Film

Ailun offers a budget-friendly yet reliable option featuring 9H hardness and HD transparency. But since it’s a budget-friendly option, you don’t get an alignment tray in the packaging, making installation a bit tricky.

It’s perfect for those who want simple, effective scratch protection without spending too much.

Apple Watch Ultra Screen Protector Installation Guide

Most screen protectors nowadays come with detailed installation kits in the packaging, making the installation process pretty straightforward. Here’s how you can:

  • Remove the bumper case (if you use one).
  • Gently clean the screen with the provided alcohol wipes and microfiber cloth, ensuring no smudges or dust particles remain.
  • Use the alignment frame (if included) to ensure precise placement.
  • Apply the protector in a clean, dust-free space to prevent particles from getting trapped under the glass.
  • Press out air bubbles using a card or the included applicator.

Conclusion: Give Your Apple Watch Ultra the Protection It Deserves

The Apple Watch Ultra is built to handle the toughest adventures, but even the toughest gear benefits from a little extra protection. Adding a quality screen protector keeps your watch’s display flawless and guards it against scratches, chips, and scuffs.

If you’re a frequent traveler, hiker, or fitness enthusiast, go for a tempered glass protector for maximum durability. For everyday users who prefer something thinner and lighter, a TPU film works just fine.

Which Apple Watch Ultra screen protector do you use or plan to buy? Share your favorite in the comments!

  • How to Use Siren on Apple Watch Ultra

title.rendered: Game Mode on iPhone: What It Is and How to Turn It On

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Apple introduced Game Mode since iOS 18 and iPadOS 18: Game Mode optimizes system performance, reduces distractions, and delivers smoother, more responsive gameplay on supported iPhones and iPads.
  • Automatic or manual activation options: Game Mode turns on automatically when you launch a game but can also be manually controlled through the Control Center.
  • Performance and gameplay improvements: It prioritizes CPU and GPU power, minimizes controller latency, and syncs audio more precisely for an immersive gaming experience.
  • Battery usage and limitations: Game Mode may slightly reduce battery life, and there are currently no customization options or guaranteed compatibility with all games.
  • Tips for using Game Mode effectively: Launch a game to auto-enable it or toggle it manually in Control Center to ensure optimal performance during intense gaming sessions.

Apple has introduced a brand-new Game Mode for iPhone and iPad. This mode enhances your gaming experience by optimizing performance, reducing distractions, and providing smoother gameplay.

Here’s how to use Game Mode on your iPhone, what it does, and why it’s worth trying.

Table of Contents
  • What is Game Mode on iPhone and iPad?
  • How to Turn Game Mode On and Off on iPhone and iPad
  • What Does Game Mode Do?
    • 1. Better Performance
    • 2. Lower Latency
    • 3. Better Audio
  • Happy Gaming…

What is Game Mode on iPhone and iPad?

Interestingly, this isn’t Apple’s first introduction of a dedicated Game Mode. It first appeared as a hidden feature in macOS Sonoma. Now, it’s available on iPhones and iPads, which are more commonly used for gaming than Macs.

Think of Game Mode as your device’s best gaming buddy. It’s designed to boost performance, minimize lag, and deliver an all-around improved gaming experience. When active, it prioritizes system resources for your game, leading to smoother graphics, quicker response times, and more immersive gameplay.

The good news is that Game Mode isn’t exclusive to the latest models. As long as your device supports iOS 18 or later or iPadOS 18 or later, you’ll be able to use it.

How to Turn Game Mode On and Off on iPhone and iPad

  1. Launch a game on your iPhone.
  2. The Game Mode automatically turns on, and you will see it on the top of your screen.
  3. When you exit the game, the Game Mode will automatically turn off. Game Mode also turns off automatically when you quit the game on your iPhone or iPad.
  4. To disable Game Mode manually, tap the pop-up alert or swipe down to open the Control Center.
  5. Then, tap on Game Mode and turn it off.

What Does Game Mode Do?

When Game Mode is enabled, your iPhone or iPad makes several behind-the-scenes adjustments to deliver a better experience:

1. Better Performance

Game Mode minimizes background activity and prioritizes CPU and GPU resources for your game. The result is smoother graphics and more consistent frame rates.

2. Lower Latency

Wireless controllers become more responsive because Game Mode increases Bluetooth polling rate, reducing the lag between your button presses and in-game actions.

3. Better Audio

Wireless headphones often suffer from audio delays. With Game Mode, audio latency is reduced for a more immersive experience.

  • AirPods Pro (2nd gen) get the lowest latency.
  • AirPods (3rd gen), AirPods Pro, and AirPods Max support Personalized Spatial Audio for deeper immersion.

Happy Gaming…

Apple’s Bionic processors have consistently outperformed most Android chips, and Game Mode takes that performance even further. By optimizing system resources, it delivers smoother graphics, lower latency, and a superior overall gaming experience.

Whether you’re a casual gamer or a hardcore enthusiast, Game Mode is a feature well worth trying out.

FAQs

Does Game Mode drain the battery?

Not significantly. It may use a bit more battery since performance is prioritized, but the impact is minimal.

Can I customize Game Mode settings?

Currently, no. Apple hasn’t added customization options yet, though that could change in the future.

Will Game Mode work with all games?

It should work with most, but since Apple doesn’t allow manual selection, some titles may not trigger Game Mode automatically.

  • How to use the Delta emulator on an iPhone to play Nintendo games
  • Best shooting games for iPhone and iPad
  • Best fighting games for iPhone and iPad

mainEntity.name: Does Game Mode drain the battery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not significantly. It may use a bit more battery since performance is prioritized, but the impact is minimal.

mainEntity.name: Can I customize Game Mode settings?

acceptedAnswer.text: Currently, no. Apple hasn't added customization options yet, though that could change in the future.

mainEntity.name: Will Game Mode work with all games?

acceptedAnswer.text: It should work with most, but since Apple doesn't allow manual selection, some titles may not trigger Game Mode automatically.

keyPoints.title: Introduction of Game Mode on iPhone and iPad
keyPoints.explanation: Apple’s new Game Mode enhances gaming by boosting performance, reducing distractions, and ensuring smoother gameplay on supported devices with iOS 18 or later.

keyPoints.title: Automatic and manual activation of Game Mode
keyPoints.explanation: Game Mode turns on automatically when a game launches and can also be manually toggled via Control Center for user control.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Game Mode for gaming experience
keyPoints.explanation: It improves performance by prioritizing system resources, reduces controller lag through lower latency, and enhances audio sync for a more immersive experience.

keyPoints.title: Battery impact and customization status of Game Mode
keyPoints.explanation: While it may slightly affect battery life, Game Mode currently has no custom settings and may not activate with every game automatically.

keyPoints.title: Usage tips for Game Mode
keyPoints.explanation: To enable or disable Game Mode, launch a game to auto-activate, or use Control Center to turn it off or on manually, ensuring optimized gaming performance.

title.rendered: How to Set Up Two-Factor Authentication on Facebook

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) does on Facebook: 2FA adds a second verification step when logging in from unknown devices, combining your password with a one-time code or security key.
  • Why enabling 2FA is essential: It protects against unauthorized logins, phishing attempts, and password leaks, making your Facebook account far more secure.
  • How to turn on 2FA using an iPhone or iPad: Open the Facebook app, go to Settings → Accounts Center → Password and Security, then select Two-factor authentication and follow setup prompts.
  • How to enable 2FA on a Mac or PC: Sign in via a browser, open Settings → Accounts Center → Password & Security → Two-factor authentication, and choose your verification method.
  • Backup and recovery options: Facebook lets you use SMS codes, authentication apps, or physical keys, and you can generate recovery codes in case you lose access to your main method.

With the increase in online threats, protecting our personal data on social media platforms is crucial. This is why Facebook has incorporated two-factor authentication to keep away trespassers. When enabled, you must enter a special security code in addition to your password; for those who may wonder what it means and how to do that, they are on the right blog.

In this blog post, I will show you how to set up two-factor authentication on Facebook on an iPhone, iPad, Mac, or PC. I will also walk you through everything you need to know about this crucial security feature.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on Facebook?
  • Why Should You Enable 2FA for Your Facebook Account?
  • How to Set Up Two-Factor Authentication on Your Facebook Account
    • Turn On 2FA for Facebook on Your iPhone or iPad
    • Turn on 2FA for Facebook on your Mac or PC:
  • How Two-Factor Authentication Works on Facebook
  • How to Set Up Recovery Codes on Facebook
  • Bonus: Set up alerts about unrecognized logins on Facebook
  • Signing off…

What Is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on Facebook?

Two-factor authentication is a security feature that requires you to provide two different forms of verification when logging into your Facebook account from an unrecognized browser or mobile device.

The first factor is typically your password, while the second factor can be a one-time code sent to you via SMS, a security key, or a code generated by an authentication app. Unless you confirm your login attempt, no one can access your account.

Thus, it ensures that only you can access your Facebook account, even if someone else has your password. This extra step makes it much harder for hackers to break into your account. Let’s understand in brief.

Why Should You Enable 2FA for Your Facebook Account?

Since Facebook stores private information like your friends’ messages, your images, and your phone number, you should enable 2-factor authentication to protect your digital identity. It offers several advantages:

  • Enhanced security: Two-factor authentication significantly strengthens your Facebook account’s security, requiring an extra step when logging in from an unrecognized device.
  • Protection against unauthorized access: Even if someone manages to obtain your password, they won’t be able to access your account without the second factor of authentication.
  • Mitigation of phishing attacks: Attackers will find it more difficult to access your profile via phishing, as many of these codes are location- or time-specific.

Now that you understand how essential it is, let’s proceed to the steps.

Pro Tip If you want to protect your personal information on Facebook, you may also lock your Facebook account. It will restrict strangers from accessing your profile details and your social media posts and content. Only your friends on Facebook can interact with you after your profile is locked.

How to Set Up Two-Factor Authentication on Your Facebook Account

Setting up 2FA on Facebook is easy; you can do it from your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or PC. Below are step-by-step guides for each device.

Turn On 2FA for Facebook on Your iPhone or iPad

  1. Launch the Facebook app.
  2. Tap the menu icon (three lines) at the bottom right corner.
  3. Scroll down and tap on Settings & privacy. Select Settings from the context menu.
  4. Now, go to the Accounts Center.
  5. For iPhone, tap on Password and Security. On iPad, select Security and login.
  6. Next, tap Use two-factor authentication.
  7. If your Facebook and Instagram accounts are connected, select your Facebook account.
  8. Enter your Facebook account password if prompted and tap Submit.
  9. Select the preferred 2FA method (Text message, SMS code, third-party two-factor authentication app, or Security Key).
  10. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete the setup.

Turn on 2FA for Facebook on your Mac or PC:

  1. Open Facebook in a web browser and log in to your account.
  2. Click on your profile picture at the top right of the page.
  3. Now, select Settings & privacy and click Settings.
  4. In the left menu, click Accounts Center.
  5. Here, select Password & security from the sidebar.
  6. Click on Two-factor authentication on the right.
  7. Choose your Facebook account.
  8. Enter your password and click Submit.
  9. Choose your preferred authentication method, then follow the on-screen prompts to complete the setup.

If you want to know how authentication methods secure your account, keep on reading.

How Two-Factor Authentication Works on Facebook

I have already explained the basic working principle of Facebook’s two-factor authentication feature. Whenever someone tries to log into your account, they must provide an additional verification code. Facebook offers three main methods to authenticate your login attempts:

  • Text message (SMS or WhatsApp): While logging onto Facebook, you receive a unique six-digit security code via SMS or WhatsApp to your registered phone number. This code is valid for a limited time, such as 30 or 60 seconds. If you don’t have a number set on your account, you can add it while enabling the feature.
  • Security key: You can use a physical security key that plugs into your device’s charging port or connects via Bluetooth/NFC for authentication. As the security key is present with you, it becomes impossible to break into your account. Select Security keys as your authentication method and register your security key.
  • Two-factor authentication apps: Apps like Google Authenticator generate time-sensitive codes that you enter when logging into Facebook. You may download any third-party authenticator app on your device, then scan the barcode Facebook provided to set it up.

You may choose any method to enable two-factor authentication for your Facebook account that’s most convenient and secure for you. After that, you can add another backup authentication method or get Facebook recovery codes to ensure you never lose access to your account. We will discuss this later in the post.

Once the setup is done, you must enter the verification code each time you try to log in from an unrecognized device or browser. You may save the browser when prompted to ensure a smooth login from your primary devices. This way, Facebook will not ask for 2FA codes from that device again.

Also, you can get alerts and approve your next login attempts from recognized devices. However, you must always verify your login attempts when accessing Facebook in an incognito window.

Note You can review your authorized devices and remove the ones you don’t use anymore to increase security. Access the Use two-factor authentication settings and select Trusted devices at the bottom. Here you can see a device list you have approved. Select the device and hit Remove device.

How to Set Up Recovery Codes on Facebook

Facebook provides 10 recovery codes you can use to access your account if you lose access to your phone or security key. Moreover, if you have trouble using the two-factor authentication method you set up, you can still use it to log in to Facebook. To set up recovery codes:

  1. Go to your Facebook account settings and navigate to the Use two-factor authentication section.
  2. Select Additional methods.
  3. And choose Recovery codes.
  4. Facebook will generate 10 recovery codes, each 4 digits. You can use each code only once.
  5. Copy-paste the code or tap on Download codes.

Put down your recovery codes in a secure place. If anyone has access to them, they can log into your account. Setting up multiple alternatives, such as a backup phone number or email address, may also be advisable if you lose access to your primary authentication method.

Bonus: Set up alerts about unrecognized logins on Facebook

You can create alerts for unrecognized logins to increase the security of your Facebook account. This will notify you of any login to your account from unrecognized devices or locations.

To enable unrecognized login alerts:

  1. Go to your Facebook Accounts Center settings and navigate to the Password and security section.
  2. Select Login alerts.
  3. Now, choose your Facebook account.
  4. Check the box for the alert method you want (email or Facebook notifications).
  5. Get back to save your choice.

By receiving these alerts, you can quickly act if someone tries to access your account without permission. If you get a suspicious login alert, select This was me. After that, Facebook will help you secure your account.

Signing off…

Two-factor authentication on Facebook is essential to protect your personal information from prying eyes. Follow the guidelines provided to set up Facebook two-factor authentication on your iPhone, iPad, Mac, or PC, ensuring the safety of your account even if someone else knows the password. Remember to also set up recovery codes and alerts for unrecognized logins to further strengthen your account’s security.

FAQs

Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can’t recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

What should I do if two-factor authentication isn’t working?

If 2FA isn’t working, ensure you’re entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can’t turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

blockGraphs.question: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?
blockGraphs.answer: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

blockGraphs.question: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?
blockGraphs.answer: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

keyPoints.title: What Is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on Facebook?
keyPoints.explanation: 2FA requires you to provide two forms of verification when logging in from an unrecognized device, significantly enhancing account security by using a password plus a one-time code or security key.

keyPoints.title: Reason to Enable 2FA on Facebook
keyPoints.explanation: Enabling 2FA protects your private information, prevents unauthorized access even if someone has your password, and mitigates phishing attacks, making your account much safer.

keyPoints.title: How to Enable 2FA on iPhone or iPad
keyPoints.explanation: You can turn on 2FA through Facebook's app by navigating to Settings > Accounts Center > Password and Security, choosing your preferred authentication method, and following the prompts.

keyPoints.title: How to Enable 2FA on Mac or PC
keyPoints.explanation: Log into Facebook on a web browser, go to Settings > Accounts Center > Password & Security, select Two-factor authentication, choose your account, and follow the instructions to set up your authentication method.

keyPoints.title: How 2FA Works and Recovery Setup
keyPoints.explanation: When enabled, Facebook requires a verification code sent via SMS, security key, or app at login. You can also set up recovery codes to regain access if you lose your primary authentication method.

title.rendered: How to Use Safari iCloud Tabs on iPhone, iPad and Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • What Safari iCloud Tabs do: iCloud Tabs sync open Safari tabs across all Apple devices using the same Apple ID, letting you continue browsing seamlessly from anywhere.
  • How to enable iCloud Tabs on iPhone: Go to Settings → iCloud → See All → toggle Safari on to start syncing your Safari data across devices.
  • How to enable iCloud Tabs on Mac: In System Settings → iCloud → See All → enable Safari to allow your Mac’s tabs to sync with iCloud.
  • How to view iCloud Tabs in Safari: Tap the Tabs button in Safari, then scroll to see open tabs from your other Apple devices, like your Mac or iPad.
  • Tips for smooth syncing: Make sure all devices share the same Apple ID and have enough iCloud storage; this ensures tabs stay updated and easy to access.

For users with multiple Apple devices, keeping track of all the browser tabs across devices can get cumbersome, especially if you habitually switch devices. This is exactly where the Safari iCloud tab comes in handy. With Safari iCloud tabs enabled on your Apple devices, you can access all your active Safari tabs across all your Apple devices without breaking a sweat.

So, no matter which device you were working on earlier, you can easily continue where you left off on the device you currently have. Keep reading to learn what Safari iCloud tabs are, how to set them up and use them, and what benefits they offer.

Table of Contents
  • What are Safari iCloud Tabs?
  • How to Set Up iCloud Tabs for Safari
    • On iPhone
    • On Mac
  • How to Use iCloud Tabs in Safari
    • On iPhone
    • On Mac
  • Signing off…

What are Safari iCloud Tabs?

Safari iCloud tabs is an Apple Ecosystem feature that uses your available iCloud storage to sync your active Safari tabs across your Apple devices signed with the same Apple ID.

For instance, let’s say you were working on a webpage in Safari on your Mac, and the Mac ran out of battery juice. Frustrating, isn’t it? With Safari iCloud tabs enabled on your Apple devices, you don’t have to be.

As soon as your Mac’s battery runs out, you can pick up your iPhone or iPad, open the Safari app, and resume the same tab without having to navigate to it again.

The integration of Safari tabs into the Apple Ecosystem ensures that you don’t need to copy the URL links on one device and paste them into the other to access the same website; iCloud handles everything automatically.

How to Set Up iCloud Tabs for Safari

As the name suggests, the Safari iCloud tabs feature uses your available iCloud storage to sync all your active tabs across devices. This means you must allow Safari on your Apple device to sync with iCloud to use Safari iCloud tabs. Here’s how you can do this:

On iPhone

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone up and running on iOS 18 or later.
  2. Here, scroll down and tap iCloud.
  3. Next, tap on See All available next to Saved to iCloud.
  4. Now, turn on the toggle next to Safari if it isn’t already.

On Mac

  1. Open the Settings app on your Mac running on macOS Sequoia or later.
  2. Here, click on iCloud on the left, then click the See All button on the right.
  3. Now, make sure the Safari toggle is on and click Done.

How to Use iCloud Tabs in Safari

Now that you’ve enabled Safari iCloud tabs on your iPhone, iPad, and Mac, you’ll be amazed at how easy it is to access all your active Safari tabs across all your devices.

On iPhone

  1. Open the Safari browser and tap the Tabs button at the bottom right corner.
  2. Next, tap the “+” button in the bottom-left corner to open a new tab.
  3. As soon as a new Safari tab pops up, you’ll notice a new Safari iCloud Tabs section.
  4. Swipe right on the current viewable tabs to view iCloud tabs active on your other Apple devices.
  5. Now, choose the iCloud tab you would like to work on.

On Mac

  1. Open Safari and click the “+” button at the top right to add a new tab.
  2. Next, scroll down to the bottom to see active iCloud tabs.
  3. Click on Show All to view all your active iCloud tabs.
  4. Now, you can choose the one you want to continue with.

Signing off…

That’s pretty much it; by setting up and using Safari iCloud tabs on your Apple devices, you can easily keep track of all your online activities across your devices without missing a beat. So, the next time you read an article on Mac and need to head out, you don’t have to worry about sending the article’s link to your iPhone, as it will be done automatically.

You can comment below if you still have doubts, and I’ll happily respond.

FAQs

Why can’t I set up iCloud Tabs in Safari?

You must have enough free iCloud storage available so Safari can sync its data. If not, you won’t be able to set up iCloud tabs.

Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

Once you set up Safari for iCloud, all your Safari data, including active tabs, bookmarks, and reading lists, is stored in iCloud and can be accessed via your other Apple devices.

What to do if iCloud tabs are not syncing?

Ensure you have enough iCloud space and that all your Apple devices are signed in with the same Apple ID. You can also try to toggle the feature on and off.

  • How to reopen closed Safari tabs on iPhone, iPad, and Mac
  • What are Safari Profiles and how to use them on iPhone, iPad, or Mac

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I set up iCloud Tabs in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: You must have enough free iCloud storage available so Safari can sync its data. If not, you won't be able to set up iCloud tabs.

mainEntity.name: Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once you set up Safari for iCloud, all your Safari data, including active tabs, bookmarks, and reading lists, is stored in iCloud and can be accessed via your other Apple devices.

mainEntity.name: What to do if iCloud tabs are not syncing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ensure you have enough iCloud space and that all your Apple devices are signed in with the same Apple ID. You can also try to toggle the feature on and off.

@graph.name: How to Set Up iCloud Tabs for Safari On iPhone
@graph.description: Turn on iCloud sync for Safari so your open tabs and browsing data stay updated across your Apple devices.

supply.name: An iPhone running iOS 18 or later
Apple ID signed in on the device

step.name: Open Settings on your iPhone
step.text: Launch the Settings app on your iPhone that is running iOS 18 or later to manage iCloud options.

itemListElement.text: Tap the Settings app icon to open it.

step.name: Open iCloud settings
step.text: Scroll down and tap iCloud to view sync settings for your apps and data.

itemListElement.text: Scroll and select iCloud from the list.

step.name: View items saved to iCloud
step.text: Tap See All next to Saved to iCloud to expand the list of apps that can sync with iCloud.

itemListElement.text: Tap See All beside Saved to iCloud.

step.name: Enable Safari sync
step.text: Find Safari in the list and turn on the toggle so iCloud can sync your tabs and browsing data across devices.

itemListElement.text: Turn on the Safari toggle to enable iCloud Tabs.
Leave it on to keep tabs and bookmarks in sync.

@graph.name: How to Set Up iCloud Tabs for Safari On Mac
@graph.description: Enable iCloud Tabs on your Mac so your Safari browsing data, open tabs, and history stay synced across all your Apple devices.

supply.name: A Mac running macOS Sequoia or later
Apple ID signed in on the Mac

step.name: Open Settings on your Mac
step.text: Click the Apple menu, then open the Settings app on your Mac that’s running macOS Sequoia or later.

itemListElement.text: Click the Apple menu at the top-left corner of your screen.
Select Settings from the dropdown list.

step.name: Access iCloud settings
step.text: In the Settings sidebar, click iCloud, then click the See All button on the right to view all apps that sync with iCloud.

itemListElement.text: Click iCloud from the left-hand panel.
Click See All next to the list of synced apps.

step.name: Turn on Safari sync
step.text: Make sure the Safari toggle is switched on so iCloud can sync your browsing data and open tabs across all your Apple devices. Click Done to save your settings.

itemListElement.text: Find Safari in the list and switch the toggle on.
Click Done to confirm the changes.

@graph.name: How to Use iCloud Tabs in Safari On iPhone
@graph.description: Use iCloud Tabs in Safari on your iPhone to quickly open tabs that are active on your other Apple devices and keep your browsing in sync.

supply.name: An iPhone signed in with your Apple ID
iCloud sync for Safari enabled on all devices

step.name: Open Safari and view your tabs
step.text: Launch Safari on your iPhone and tap the Tabs button at the bottom right to open the tab switcher.

itemListElement.text: Open Safari from your Home Screen or App Library.
Tap the Tabs button in the bottom right corner.

step.name: Open a new tab
step.text: Tap the plus button in the bottom left corner to create a new Safari tab, which also reveals the iCloud Tabs section.

itemListElement.text: Tap the + button to open a new tab.

step.name: Find the iCloud Tabs section
step.text: When the new tab appears, look for the Safari iCloud Tabs section that lists tabs from your other Apple devices.

itemListElement.text: Scroll the start page to locate the iCloud Tabs section.

step.name: Browse tabs from other devices
step.text: Swipe right on the current viewable tabs to see the iCloud tabs that are active on your other devices using the same Apple ID.

itemListElement.text: Swipe right to move through the list of iCloud tabs.

step.name: Open an iCloud tab
step.text: Tap any iCloud tab from the list to open it on your iPhone and continue browsing from where you left off.

itemListElement.text: Choose the iCloud tab you want to work on and tap to open it.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development. Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience. Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. keyPoints.title: Safari iCloud Tabs Overview
keyPoints.explanation: Safari iCloud tabs sync your active Safari tabs across all your Apple devices signed with the same Apple ID, making it easy to continue browsing seamlessly.

keyPoints.title: Setting up iCloud Tabs on iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: To enable iCloud tabs on iPhone, go to Settings > iCloud > See All > toggle Safari on, ensuring your Safari data syncs across devices.

keyPoints.title: Setting up iCloud Tabs on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: On Mac, open System Settings > iCloud > See All > toggle Safari on to allow your Mac to sync tabs with iCloud.

keyPoints.title: Using iCloud Tabs in Safari
keyPoints.explanation: Access iCloud tabs by tapping the Tabs button in Safari, then swiping or scrolling to see active tabs from other devices, whether on iPhone or Mac.

keyPoints.title: Troubleshooting and Benefits
keyPoints.explanation: Ensure enough iCloud storage and that all devices use the same Apple ID for syncing; benefits include effortless continuation of browsing sessions and easy management of tabs.

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: App Store Missing on iPhone or iPad? How to Get It Back

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why the App Store disappears on iPhone: It may be hidden in a folder, restricted by Screen Time, moved to the App Library, or temporarily affected by a system glitch.
  • Use Spotlight Search to locate the App Store: Swipe down from the Home Screen and type “App Store” to open it instantly if you can’t find the icon.
  • Check the App Library for the missing icon: Swipe left past all Home Screens to the App Library, search for App Store, then drag it back to your Home Screen if needed.
  • Verify that Home Screen pages aren’t hidden: Long-press the Home Screen, tap the page dots, and make sure every page is enabled to reveal hidden app icons.
  • Reset iPhone settings if nothing works: Reset all settings or restore the Home Screen layout to bring back the App Store icon without deleting personal data.

Can’t find the App Store icon on your iPhone or iPad? Don’t worry, you’re not alone. The App Store is built into your device, so it cannot be deleted. If you can’t find it, it’s probably hidden or misplaced. In this article, we look at possible reasons why the App Store might have disappeared on your device and how to get it back in a jiffy.

Table of Contents
  • Why Did the App Store Disappear From My iPhone or iPad?
  • 6 Ways to Get the Missing App Store Back on iPhone or iPad
    • 1. Find the App Store Using Spotlight Search
    • 2. Check App Library to Find Missing App Store
    • 3. Check Hidden Home Screen Pages
    • 4. Turn Off App Restrictions for the App Store
    • 5. Reset Home Screen Layout
    • 6. Reset All Settings on iPhone and iPad
  • Signing off…

Why Did the App Store Disappear From My iPhone or iPad?

The App Store might be hidden from view due to the following reasons:

  • Inside a Folder: Maybe you accidentally moved the App Store icon into a folder that has hidden it from view on your Home Screen.
  • App Library: Similarly, the App Store might have been moved to your App Library, which appears on the last page of your iPhone’s home screen.
  • Restrictions: The App Store might be restricted due to some Screen Time restrictions in your settings.
  • Software Glitch: In rare cases, a technical glitch or bug could be the reason why you can’t see the App Store anymore.

6 Ways to Get the Missing App Store Back on iPhone or iPad

No matter the cause, here are some quick ways to get the App Store icon back on your iPhone and iPad.

1. Find the App Store Using Spotlight Search

Sometimes, the simplest solution is the best one. Using Spotlight Search can help you quickly find the App Store icon.

  1. Swipe down on your home screen to bring up Spotlight Search.
  2. Type App Store into the search bar.
  3. The App Store icon should appear. Simply tap on it to open the app.
  4. You can also check the location of the App Store icon in the search results and move it back to your home screen if needed.

2. Check App Library to Find Missing App Store

With iOS 14 and later, all apps are stored in the App Library. If your App Store icon is missing, it might be tucked away in the App Library. Here’s how to find it:

  1. Swipe left through your home screens until you reach the App Library.
  2. You can browse through the categories to find the App Store. Alternatively, you can use the search bar at the top of the App Library.
  3. Once you locate the App Store icon, you can drag it back to your home screen for easier access.

3. Check Hidden Home Screen Pages

Did you know that you can also hide the home screen pages on your iPhone and iPad? You might have accidentally hidden the page where the App Store icon is located. Here’s how to recover it:

  1. Long-press on the home screen until all the icons start shaking.
  2. Tap the dots at the bottom of the screen representing your home screen pages.
  3. Ensure that all your home screen pages are checked and not hidden.
  4. Once done, go back to the home screen and look through the pages to find your App Store icon.

4. Turn Off App Restrictions for the App Store

If you have set restrictions on your iPhone, it might be blocking the App Store. As a result, this can hide the App Store icon from your home screen. Here’s how to fix it.

  1. Navigate to Settings → Screen Time → Content & Privacy Restrictions.
  2. Enter your Screen Time passcode if prompted.
  3. Here, tap on iTunes & App Store Purchases.
  4. Ensure that Installing Apps, Deleting Apps, and In-App Purchases are set to Allow.
  5. Once done, go back to the home screen to check if the App Store icon has reappeared.

5. Reset Home Screen Layout

You can reset your home screen layout to return all default apps to their original locations, including the App Store. Here’s how to do it:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Reset.
  2. Tap on Reset Home Screen Layout.
  3. Select Reset Home Screen to confirm your choice.

That’s it. Your home screen layout will be reset to its default state, and the App Store icon should be back on your home screen.

6. Reset All Settings on iPhone and iPad

If you’ve tried all the steps above but the App Store is still missing, you can reset all settings on your iPhone to restore it to its default state. This will not erase your data or apps, but it will reset all your personalized settings, such as Wi-Fi passwords, wallpapers, and notifications.

  1. Open Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone → Reset.
  2. Now, tap on Reset All Settings.
  3. Enter your passcode to confirm your choice.
  4. Your iPhone will now restart and restore all the settings to their default state. Once done, check if the App Store icon has returned.

Signing off…

I know it’s frustrating not to find the App Store on your iPhone or iPad. But as I’ve explained above, it’s pretty simple to get it back. If you’re still facing problems, share them in the comments below, and I’ll try to help.

  • How to restore deleted apps on iPhone or iPad
  • How to manage App Store subscriptions and purchases on an iPhone or iPad

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

acceptedAnswer.text: You must have enough free iCloud storage available so Safari can sync its data. If not, you won't be able to set up iCloud tabs.

keyPoints.title: Why the App Store Might Disappear
keyPoints.explanation: The App Store can sometimes be hidden due to being inside a folder, moved to the App Library, restricted by Screen Time, or due to a software glitch.

keyPoints.title: Using Spotlight Search to Find the App Store
keyPoints.explanation: Swipe down on the home screen and search for 'App Store' to quickly locate and open the app if it's misplaced.

keyPoints.title: Check the App Library for the App Store
keyPoints.explanation: Swiping left through home screens to the App Library allows you to find the missing App Store and add it back to the home screen if needed.

keyPoints.title: Ensure Home Screen Pages Are Not Hidden
keyPoints.explanation: Long-press the home screen, tap the dots at the bottom, and verify all pages are visible, as the App Store might be on a hidden page.

keyPoints.title: Reset Settings to Restore the App Store Icon
keyPoints.explanation: Resetting all settings, including home screen layout, can restore the App Store icon without deleting data, if it is missing due to misplacement or restrictions.
