keyPoints.title: Apple Music to YouTube Music Playlist Transfer:**
keyPoints.explanation: Apple makes transferring playlists to YouTube Music simple, allowing you to retain your curated playlists when switching platforms.

keyPoints.title: What Data Can Be Transferred:**
keyPoints.explanation: Only playlists you created or own can be transferred; tracks not available on YouTube Music, music files, podcasts, and organized folders won't transfer.

keyPoints.title: Steps for Transferring Playlists:**
keyPoints.explanation: Transfer involves requesting data from Apple, selecting playlists, choosing your Google account, granting permissions, and confirming the export, with updates via email.

keyPoints.title: Benefits of Moving to YouTube Music:**
keyPoints.explanation: YouTube Music offers a larger library, better search, and ad-free videos, making it a compelling choice for users wanting a more extensive music experience.

keyPoints.title: Official Transfer Method & Tips:**
keyPoints.explanation: Apple provides an official way to transfer playlists, and the process may take some time depending on your playlist size, but it’s straightforward with clear instructions.

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Use iOS Shortcuts to Save Twitter GIFs: Shortcuts like DTwitter let you download Twitter GIFs directly from tweet links on iPhone or iPad, no third-party apps required.
  • Download via TweetSave App on iPhone: TweetSave allows GIF downloads by pasting tweet links, though free users may see ads unless they upgrade.
  • Save Twitter GIFs on Desktop Easily: Sites like Twitter Video Downloader let you paste tweet URLs to save GIFs directly to your computer in seconds.
  • Add Download Options with Chrome Extensions: Extensions such as Twitter Media Asset integrate a download button under tweets for quick browser-based GIF saving.
  • Multiple Ways to Store Twitter GIFs: Whether you use shortcuts, apps, or extensions, iPhone, iPad, and desktop users can save Twitter GIFs with minimal effort.

GIFs have exploded on social media platforms like X (formerly Twitter). Since people often use them to spice up their tweets and responses with fun animation, there may be occasions when you want to save the ones you find interesting.

In this article, we’ll show some simple methods to download a GIF from Twitter (X) on an iPhone, iPad, and desktop.

Table of Contents
  • How to save a GIF from Twitter (X) on an iPhone or iPad
    • 1. Download a GIF from Twitter with an iOS shortcut
    • 2. Download a GIF from Twitter using the TweetSave iOS app
  • How to save a GIF from Twitter (X) on desktop
    • 1. Download a Twitter GIF using third-party websites
    • 2. Download a Twitter GIF with a Chrome extension

How to save a GIF from Twitter (X) on an iPhone or iPad

Sadly, the Twitter app doesn’t come with a built-in option to download GIFs or any other media file. So, we’ll save Twitter GIFs using third-party apps and iOS shortcuts.

1. Download a GIF from Twitter with an iOS shortcut

iOS shortcuts offer the easiest ways to save Twitter GIFs on your iPhone or iPad. With it, you don’t need to install any third-party apps, which saves you storage and keeps your privacy protected. However, you can only download GIFs used on public tweet threads with this method.

To install the DTwitter (Twitter Tweet) shortcut on your device, follow these steps:

  1. Visit the RoutineHub website.
  2. Tap Get Shortcut, and it’ll redirect you to the Shortcuts app.
  3. Here select the Set Up Shortcut option.
  4. Tap Next and hit Add Shortcut.

Now that the shortcut is added to your Shortcuts library, let’s see how to use it to download GIFs from Twitter.

  1. Open the Twitter (X) app.
  2. Go to the tweet with the GIF you want to save.
  3. Tap the Share button below the tweet and select Copy Link.
  4. Open the Shortcuts app and run the DTwitter shortcut.
  5. Tap Allow on the prompt. The shortcut will automatically detect the copied GIF link.
  6. Now, select Always Allow.
  7. Finally, tap Allow to get notifications.
  8. Hit Always Allow to give the shortcut access to your gallery.

Wait for a few seconds, and the Twitter GIF will be saved to your Photos app.

The next time you want to download Twitter GIF on your iPhone, all you have to do is copy the link and then execute the shortcut.

2. Download a GIF from Twitter using the TweetSave iOS app

Another method of saving Twitter GIFs is using the TweetSave app. TweetSave is an easy-to-use app that lets you download images, videos, and GIFs from Twitter. Let’s see how to use this Twitter GIF downloader app.  

  1. Download and install the TweetSave app from the App Store. 
  2. Just like before, copy the link to the tweet containing the GIF. 
  3. Launch the TweetSave app. For the first time, tap Continue. 
  4. In the search box, tap the cursor and select Paste. 
  5. Tap Find to fetch the GIF. 
  6. Once the GIF appears, hit Save.
  7. When the download finishes, you’ll get a popup. Tap OK to go back.

TweetSave helps you save GIFs on your iPhone for free. However, the number of ads is quite annoying. You can remove the ads by upgrading to TweetSave Premium.

How to save a GIF from Twitter (X) on desktop

Saving GIFs from Twitter on a desktop is straightforward, thanks to a few handy tools.

1. Download a Twitter GIF using third-party websites

One of the simplest methods to save GIFs on your desktop is by using third-party websites. This method is easy and doesn’t require any additional software installation.

  1. Locate the tweet with the GIF you want.
  2. Click the Share icon and select Copy link.
  3. Visit Twitter Video Downloader in your preferred browser.
  4. In the provided text field, paste the copied tweet link and click Download.
  5. The site will process the link and show the searched GIF. Click Download GIF.
  6. The GIF will open in a new window. Click the three-dots icon and select Download from the menu.
  7. Enter a name for the GIF, select where you want to save it on your computer, and click Save.

2. Download a Twitter GIF with a Chrome extension

If you prefer using the Chrome browser, you can use an extension to download a GIF from Twitter. This extension adds a download button to each tweet, making it easy to save or download Twitter videos, GIFs, and images.

Here is how to use it:

  1. Visit the Twitter Media Asset extension page on Chrome Web Store.
  2. Click Add to Chrome and select Add Extension.
  3. Go to Twitter using the Chrome browser.
  4. Find the tweet containing the GIF and click the Download button below it to download the GIF.

Once the GIF is downloaded, it’ll be saved to the Downloads folder on your computer, unless you’ve changed the default download folder in Chrome.

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

@graph.name: How to Download GIF from Twitter with iOS shortcut
@graph.description: Use the DTwitter shortcut on iPhone or iPad to quickly download GIFs from Twitter without third-party apps.

step.name: Install the DTwitter shortcut
step.text: Visit the RoutineHub website, tap Get Shortcut, then choose Set Up Shortcut to begin installation.

itemListElement.text: Open RoutineHub in Safari and find the DTwitter shortcut.
Tap Get Shortcut and you’ll be redirected to the Shortcuts app.
Select Set Up Shortcut and then tap Next.
Tap Add Shortcut to complete the installation.

step.name: Copy the tweet link with the GIF
step.text: Open the Twitter app, navigate to the tweet with the GIF, tap Share, and copy the tweet link.

itemListElement.text: Launch the Twitter (X) app on your iPhone or iPad.
Find the tweet that contains the GIF you want to download.
Tap the Share icon below the tweet and choose Copy Link.

step.name: Run the DTwitter shortcut
step.text: Open the Shortcuts app, run the DTwitter shortcut, and grant necessary permissions to save the GIF to your gallery.

itemListElement.text: Open the Shortcuts app and tap on DTwitter to run it.
Tap Allow when prompted to let the shortcut access the copied link.
Select Always Allow to grant access to your gallery.
Confirm permission for notifications if prompted.

@graph.name: How to Download GIF from Twitter using TweetSave iOS app
@graph.description: Easily save Twitter GIFs to your iPhone using the TweetSave app with just a few simple steps.

step.name: Install the TweetSave app
step.text: Download and install the TweetSave app from the App Store on your iPhone.

itemListElement.text: Open the App Store and search for TweetSave.
Download and install the app on your device.

step.name: Copy the tweet link
step.text: Just like with shortcuts, copy the link to the tweet containing the GIF you want to save.

itemListElement.text: Open the Twitter app and go to the tweet with the GIF.
Tap the Share icon and select Copy Link.

step.name: Paste the link and download the GIF
step.text: Launch TweetSave, paste the tweet link, find the GIF, and hit Save to download it.

itemListElement.text: Open the TweetSave app and tap Continue if prompted.
Tap the search bar, place the cursor, and choose Paste.
Tap Find to fetch the GIF from the link.
Once the GIF appears, tap Save.
When the download completes, tap OK to return to the app.

@graph.name: How to Download Twitter GIF using third-party websites
@graph.description: Save Twitter GIFs to your desktop using free third-party downloader sites, without needing any app installation.

step.name: Copy the tweet link
step.text: Find the tweet with the GIF you want to download, tap the Share icon, and choose Copy link.

itemListElement.text: Open Twitter in your browser or app and locate the tweet with the GIF.
Click the Share icon under the tweet.
Select Copy link from the menu.

step.name: Paste the link on a downloader site
step.text: Go to Twitter Video Downloader, paste the tweet link in the field, and click Download.

itemListElement.text: Open Twitter Video Downloader in a web browser.
Paste the copied tweet link into the search field.
Click the Download button to process the tweet.

step.name: Download the GIF
step.text: Click the Download GIF button, then in the new tab, click the three-dots icon and choose Download from the menu.

itemListElement.text: Click on the Download GIF button once the preview appears.
A new tab will open with the GIF preview.
Click the three-dots icon at the bottom right.
Select Download from the dropdown menu.

step.name: Save the file
step.text: Rename the GIF file, choose the folder where you want to save it, and click Save.

itemListElement.text: Enter a name for the GIF in the save dialog box.
Choose your desired save location on your computer.
Click Save to download the file.

@graph.name: How to Download Twitter GIF with a Chrome extension
@graph.description: Install the Twitter Media Asset extension in Chrome to download GIFs directly from tweets in one click.

step.name: Install the Twitter Media Asset extension
step.text: Open the extension's page in the Chrome Web Store, click Add to Chrome, and then confirm by selecting Add Extension.

itemListElement.text: Visit the Twitter Media Asset extension page in the Chrome Web Store.
Click Add to Chrome.
Select Add Extension when prompted.

step.name: Download a GIF from a tweet
step.text: Visit Twitter in the Chrome browser, locate a tweet with a GIF, and click the new Download button below it.

itemListElement.text: Open Twitter in Chrome and find a tweet that contains a GIF.
Click the Download button that appears below the tweet.
The GIF will download automatically to your device.

keyPoints.title: Downloading GIFs with TweetSave App on iPhone

keyPoints.title: Chrome Extensions for Downloading Twitter GIFs

keyPoints.title: Overview of Methods to Save Twitter GIFs

title.rendered: Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro Could Feature DSLR-Style Variable Aperture Lens

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Variable Aperture Technology Coming to iPhone 18 Pro: The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are rumored to include a redesigned 48MP Fusion camera with a variable aperture, allowing users manual control over light intake, a first for iPhones.
  • Industry Confirmation of the Feature: Analysts like Ming-Chi Kuo and reports from ET News confirm that Apple is developing this feature, with major suppliers like Sunny Optical, Luxshare, and Largan involved in the production process.
  • Advantages of Variable Aperture in Photography: A variable aperture physically adjusts the lens opening size, enabling better low-light performance and depth of field control, similar to DSLR cameras, and offering more manual photography options.
  • Apple Partners with Samsung for Camera Sensors: Apple may start using 200MP sensors supplied by Samsung for the iPhone 18 lineup, marking a significant upgrade in detail and low-light performance, and showing collaboration even with competitors.
  • Expected Release and Impact: Anticipated to launch in September 2026, the iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to introduce the most significant hardware change in years, delivering DSLR-like aperture control for advanced photography.

Apple could finally bring variable aperture technology to the iPhone 18 Pro, giving users DSLR-style control over how much light enters the lens. According to Digital Chat Station on Weibo, the next-generation iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will feature a redesigned 48MP Fusion camera with an adjustable aperture, a first for any iPhone.

Current iPhones, including the iPhone 17 Pro, use a fixed f/1.78 aperture. A variable aperture would let users manually adjust the lens, opening it wider for low-light shots or narrowing it for brighter scenes and more depth. Both the main and telephoto cameras are also rumored to get larger apertures, improving light capture and overall image clarity.

Analysts and suppliers confirm the feature

Industry analyst Ming-Chi Kuo first predicted the addition of a variable aperture lens in 2024, and ET News has now reinforced it. The report says Sunny Optical will lead lens production, while Luxshare and Largan Precision assist with manufacturing. Apple is reportedly finalizing supply chain preparations, indicating the feature is well into development.

The iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to maintain the iPhone 17’s design but could introduce minor visual tweaks, possibly including a transparent back design, while focusing on internal camera upgrades.

How variable aperture improves iPhone photography

Unlike fixed lenses, a variable aperture physically adjusts the size of the lens opening. A lower f-number (like f/1.4) allows more light, producing a natural background blur, while a higher f-number (like f/4) keeps more elements sharp and in focus. This is optical depth of field, not software-generated blur.

Think of shooting a close-up at night, widening the aperture brightens the subject and softens the background. During the day, narrowing it helps maintain crisp details across the frame. It’s the kind of manual control that bridges smartphone and DSLR photography.

Apple partners with Samsung for new sensors

BE Semiconductor will provide the assembly equipment for the new aperture mechanism. Sunny Optical remains Apple’s main component partner, but in a surprising move, Samsung might supply 200MP sensors for the iPhone 18 lineup, the first time Apple has used Samsung camera hardware. PhoneArena reports production could begin by March 2026.

This would mark a leap from the current 48MP setup, offering better detail, dynamic range, and low-light performance. The partnership shows Apple’s willingness to prioritize camera quality, even if it means collaborating with its biggest rival.

Apple isn’t the first to use variable aperture. Samsung debuted it with the Galaxy S9 in 2018, and Huawei and Honor later refined the technology in their flagships. Apple’s delayed entry could pay off, combining this proven hardware with its strong computational processing to deliver richer, more realistic images.

Expected release window

Based on current leaks, the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are expected to debut in September 2026. If accurate, this feature would mark one of Apple’s most meaningful hardware changes in years, bringing true DSLR-like aperture control to the iPhone lineup.

keyPoints.title: Variable Aperture Technology Coming to iPhone 18 Pro
keyPoints.explanation: The upcoming iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are rumored to include a redesigned 48MP Fusion camera with a variable aperture, allowing users manual control over light intake, a first for iPhones.

keyPoints.title: Industry Confirmation of the Feature
keyPoints.explanation: Analysts like Ming-Chi Kuo and reports from ET News confirm that Apple is developing this feature, with major suppliers like Sunny Optical, Luxshare, and Largan involved in the production process.

keyPoints.title: Advantages of Variable Aperture in Photography**
keyPoints.explanation: A variable aperture physically adjusts the lens opening size, enabling better low-light performance and depth of field control, similar to DSLR cameras, and offering more manual photography options.

keyPoints.title: Apple Partners with Samsung for Camera Sensors**
keyPoints.explanation: Apple may start using 200MP sensors supplied by Samsung for the iPhone 18 lineup, marking a significant upgrade in detail and low-light performance, and showing collaboration even with competitors.

keyPoints.title: Expected Release and Impact**
keyPoints.explanation: Anticipated to launch in September 2026, the iPhone 18 Pro models are expected to introduce the most significant hardware change in years, delivering DSLR-like aperture control for advanced photography.

title.rendered: Threads Introduces Ghost Posts That Disappear After 24 Hours

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Introduction of Ghost Posts: Threads now allows users to share temporary thoughts called ghost posts, which disappear from the timeline after 24 hours to promote spontaneous sharing without permanence.
  • Auto-Archiving of Ghost Posts: Ghost posts automatically move to an archive after 24 hours, accessible only by the author, enabling quick, unfiltered sharing without long-term visibility.
  • Private Replies and Likes: Replies to ghost posts are sent as private messages to the author, and likes are also visible only to the post creator, blending public sharing with private feedback.
  • How to Create a Ghost Post: To create a ghost post, tap the ghost icon before publishing; it appears with a dotted speech bubble and is ideal for testing ideas or sharing thoughts without long-term visibility.
  • Part of Broader Threads Update: Ghost posts are part of Meta’s efforts to make Threads more expressive, alongside new features like longer text posts and spoiler hiding tools, accommodating diverse conversation types.

Threads is introducing a new way to share temporary thoughts without worrying about them staying on your profile forever. The platform has officially launched ghost posts, a new type of post that disappears from the timeline after 24 hours.

Threads Introduces Ghost Posts That Auto-Archive After 24 Hours

As announced by Meta in an official blog post, ghost posts are automatically archived a day after publishing. The idea is simple, let users share quick, unfiltered thoughts without the pressure of permanence. Meta says it wants people to feel free to post spontaneous opinions and real-time reactions without overthinking how long they’ll stay visible.

When a ghost post expires, it doesn’t vanish completely, it’s simply archived, so only the author can access it later.

Replies Turn Into Private Messages

Unlike regular posts, ghost posts work a bit differently when it comes to interaction. If someone replies to your ghost post, their response goes straight to your Threads inbox as a direct message. Only you can see it. The same applies to likes, only the author can view who liked the post.

This unique design blends public sharing with private feedback, and it could also help drive more activity to Threads’ new standalone inbox, which hasn’t seen much traction since launch.

How to Create a Ghost Post on Threads

Creating a ghost post is simple. When composing a new post, tap or toggle the ghost icon before publishing. Once posted, it will appear on the timeline with a dotted speech bubble style, slightly faded to help differentiate it from normal posts.

The feature is ideal for testing ideas, sharing personal thoughts, or starting low-pressure conversations that don’t need to live on your profile forever.

Part of a Bigger Threads Update

Meta noted that ghost posts are part of its continued effort to make Threads more expressive. Over the past few months, the app has also added text attachments (allowing posts up to 10,000 characters) and tools to hide media or text containing spoilers. These updates show that Meta wants Threads to be a more flexible place for every kind of conversation, from quick thoughts to long discussions.

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

keyPoints.title: Introduction of Ghost Posts
keyPoints.explanation: Threads now allows users to share temporary thoughts called ghost posts, which disappear from the timeline after 24 hours to promote spontaneous sharing without permanence.

keyPoints.title: Auto-Archiving of Ghost Posts
keyPoints.explanation: Ghost posts automatically move to an archive after 24 hours, accessible only by the author, enabling quick, unfiltered sharing without long-term visibility.

keyPoints.title: Private Replies and Likes
keyPoints.explanation: Replies to ghost posts are sent as private messages to the author, and likes are also visible only to the post creator, blending public sharing with private feedback.

keyPoints.title: How to Create a Ghost Post
keyPoints.explanation: To create a ghost post, tap the ghost icon before publishing; it appears with a dotted speech bubble and is ideal for testing ideas or sharing thoughts without long-term visibility.

keyPoints.title: Part of Broader Threads Update
keyPoints.explanation: Ghost posts are part of Meta's efforts to make Threads more expressive, alongside new features like longer text posts and spoiler hiding tools, accommodating diverse conversation types.

title.rendered: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 17e Designs Revealed by Reliable Leaker

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • iPhone 18 Pro to Retain the Camera Plateau Design: The iPhone 18 Pro will continue to feature the same full-width camera plateau introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro, maintaining visual continuity but with minor finish updates and new color options.
  • iPhone 17e to Adopt Dynamic Island but Keep 60Hz Display: The budget-friendly iPhone 17e will introduce the Dynamic Island design in early 2026, but will retain a 60Hz display, leaving ProMotion technology exclusive to higher-end models for now.
  • Expected Variable Aperture Camera on iPhone 18 Pro: The iPhone 18 Pro is anticipated to feature a variable aperture lens, allowing users more control over focus depth, which benefits photography and filmmaking, marking a first for iPhones.
  • Gradual and Strategic Design Evolution: Apple’s design updates for 2026 seem to focus on refined, incremental changes—retaining familiar layouts like the camera plateau while making internal camera improvements and modernizing display styles.
  • Reliable Leaker Digital Chat Station’s Insight: Digital Chat Station, a trusted source with a strong track record, leaked detailed insights from Weibo about upcoming iPhone models, including design continuity and new features planned for 2026.

Reliable Weibo leaker Digital Chat Station (DCS) has shared new details about Apple’s upcoming iPhone designs. Following his earlier report on a variable aperture camera system for the iPhone 18 Pro, DCS now says Apple will retain the same overall rear design as this year’s iPhone 17 Pro.

iPhone 18 Pro to Retain the Camera Plateau Design

The iPhone 18 Pro is expected to keep the full-width camera plateau, a design Apple introduced with the iPhone 17 Pro lineup. This means the rectangular glass strip housing the three cameras will remain, offering visual continuity across two generations. However, DCS adds that the lower transparent glass section may feature a slightly different finish, giving the phone a refreshed but familiar appearance. As usual, Apple will introduce new color options to mark the update.

This continuation of the design shows Apple’s focus on consistency. The company often sticks to a design for multiple years, gradually refining it rather than making drastic changes annually.

iPhone 17e to Adopt Dynamic Island but Stick With 60Hz Display

Alongside the flagship model, DCS also revealed early details about the iPhone 17e, expected to launch in early 2026. This more affordable model will finally move away from the traditional notch and adopt the Dynamic Island, bringing it in line with the rest of Apple’s lineup.

However, the display will still be limited to 60Hz, meaning the smooth ProMotion technology seen in higher-end iPhones will remain exclusive to the Pro models for now. This isn’t surprising, as Apple only recently brought ProMotion to its base iPhones, and the feature typically takes time to trickle down to budget variants.

Variable Aperture Lens Still Expected on iPhone 18 Pro

Earlier today, 9to5Mac reported that DCS and analyst Ming-Chi Kuo both expect the iPhone 18 Pro to feature a variable aperture main camera lens, a first for iPhones. This feature would let users control the depth of field in photos more precisely, switching between shallow and deep focus depending on the scene.

The technology could also benefit filmmakers by reducing the need for neutral density filters when shooting in bright environments. While it’s unclear whether both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max will get this feature, DCS’s track record with camera-related leaks makes the claim notable.

Incremental But Strategic Design Evolution

Apple’s approach for 2026 seems clear: small, calculated updates that focus on refinement rather than reinvention. The iPhone 18 Pro keeps its recognizable plateau camera layout but evolves internally with potential camera upgrades, while the iPhone 17e finally modernizes its display design.

The information about both models comes from Digital Chat Station, a reliable leaker with a strong history of accurate Apple-related reports, and was first shared on Weibo and later covered by 9to5Mac and PhoneArena.

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to generate a Personal Voice on iPhone?

acceptedAnswer.text: Recording your voice clips takes about 15 minutes. Creating the voice model can take up to 24 hours of background processing, usually completed while your iPhone charges overnight.

mainEntity.name: Can I use my Personal Voice on other Apple devices?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. You can use your Personal Voice across iPhone, iPad, and Mac linked with the same iCloud account. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Personal Voice and enable Share Across Devices.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, cellular data won't work but you can use Wi-Fi.

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. It's often temporary, but if it persists, it may indicate a hardware issue.

mainEntity.name: How can I prevent my iPhone from showing SOS Only?

title.rendered: Try These iPhone Accessibility Tips to Make Your Life Easier!

content.rendered:
Apple has always been a pioneer when it comes to making tech everyone, and iOS 26 accessibility features takes inclusivity to the next level. From Braille Access and Head Tracking to Accessibility Reader and improved VoiceOver, iPhones continue to evolve as devices that anyone can use comfortably.

Whether you have visual, auditory, or motor challenges or simply want to make your device easier to navigate, this guide covers every major iPhone accessibility feature in iOS 26, with step-by-step instructions so you can start using them today.

Table of Contents
  • iPhone Accessibility Tips for the Visually Impaired
    • 1. VoiceOver
    • 2. Accessibility Reader
    • 3. Magnify Content
    • 4. Display & Text Adjustments
    • 5. Vehicle Motion Cues
    • 6. Braille Access
    • 7. Reduce UI motion
  • Physical and Motor Accessibility Features on iPhone
    • 8. AssistiveTouch
    • 9. Eye Tracking
    • 10. Head Tracking
    • 11. Back Tap and Side Button Shortcuts
    • 12. Tap to Wake and Haptic Feedback
    • 13. Voice Control
  • iPhone Accessibility Features for Hearing and Sound Disabilities
    • 14. Sound & Name Recognition
    • 15. Music Haptics
    • 16. Audio/Visual Settings
    • 17. Pair Hearing Aids
    • 18. Personal Voice
    • 19. Live Listen with Live Captions
    • 20. Subtitles & Captioning
  • Advanced Accessibility Tools
    • 21. Guided Access
    • 22. Share Accessibility Settings
    • 23. Per-App Accessibility Settings
    • 24. Accessibility Shortcut
    • 25. Assistive Access
  • Wrapping Up

iPhone Accessibility Tips for the Visually Impaired

These features help users with visual impairments or reading difficulties interact with their iPhones more comfortably.

1. VoiceOver

VoiceOver reads aloud every item on the screen, including text, buttons, and icons. So, when you tap a button or an app, a voice tells you what it is. In iOS 26, typing feedback and Braille Screen Input have been improved.

  1. Open Settings → Accessibility.
  2. Tap VoiceOver.
  3. Toggle VoiceOver on.
  4. Customize speech rate, pitch, and verbosity, or enable Braille Screen Input.

2. Accessibility Reader

iOS 26 introduces Accessibility Reader, a system-wide feature that simplifies and highlights text for easier reading. You can also listen to the text thanks to its Spoken Content support. Apple has designed it for people with dyslexia, low vision, or other reading challenges.

  1. From Accessibility menu, select Read & Speak.
  2. Tap on Accessibility Reader and toggle on Accessibility Reader.
  3. Open any app with text and tap the Reader icon to simplify the content.

It’s also integrated into the Magnifier app to read real-world text like restaurant menus or books by pointing your device’s camera.

3. Magnify Content

You can use Zoom to magnify the entire screen while using apps or typing on your iPhone or iPad. I recommend this option if you have difficulty seeing small texts. Or if you need a more precise focus on icons.

To activate:

  1. In Accessibility settings, select Zoom.
  2. Toggle on Zoom.

Once active, double-tap with three fingers to switch between zooming in and out. Swipe across the screen with three fingers to move around your device when you zoom icons.

4. Display & Text Adjustments

Control text size, boldness, contrast, and button shapes. New in iOS 26, you can reduce transparency in the Liquid Glass UI for better visibility.

  1. Go to Accessibility → Display & Text Size.
  2. Toggle options such as Bold Text, Button Shapes, Increase Contrast, or Reduce Transparency.
  3. Use Larger Text to adjust the font size system-wide.

5. Vehicle Motion Cues

If you experience motion sickness while using your iPhone while traveling by road or plane, the Vehicle Motion Cues feature can help. It provides visual cues when the iPhone detects movement during travel. iOS 26 allows more customization.

To set it up:

  1. Open Settings → Accessibility → Motion.
  2. Tap on Vehicle Motion Cues.
  3. Select Automatically in Vehicle.
  4. Now, tap Customize Appearance and choose the cue size, color, density and pattern that works best for you.

6. Braille Access

iOS 26 enables the iPhone to act as a full-featured braille notetaker that can easily open any app by typing with a connected braille display. It supports Nemeth math code, live conversation transcription, Braille Screen Input, external braille displays, and BRF (braille) files.

To use Braille Access:

  1. From Accessibility menu, select VoiceOver → Braille.
  2. Here, you can setup commands and customize settings from Braille Access and Braille Screen Input.

7. Reduce UI motion

It can be hard to visually catch up when actions and movements are too quick on your iPhone. You can slow them down for better comprehension and follow-up. So at least, you’ll know what’s happening next on your device.

To do this:

  1. From the Accessibility menu, tap Motion.
  2. Toggle on Reduce Motion.

Physical and Motor Accessibility Features on iPhone

These features support users with motor impairments, limited dexterity, or those seeking hands-free control.

8. AssistiveTouch

Provides a floating menu for gestures like taking screenshots, switching apps, or activating the torch without complex motions.

Turn on AssistiveTouch:

  1. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Touch.
  2. Select AssistiveTouch and toggle it on.
  3. Tap Customize Top Level Menu to set your most used gestures. Also, set up Single-Tap, Double-Tap, Long Press actions.

9. Eye Tracking

Use your gaze to control the iPhone pointer or select items. Ideal for hands-free operation. In iOS 26, Eye Tracking provides switch and dwell gestures for typing.

  1. From Accessibility list, tap Eye Tracking.
  2. Toggle on Eye Tracking.
  3. Follow the on-screen calibration guide.

10. Head Tracking

In iOS 26, Head Tracking is a remarkable feature that helps individuals with limited mobility. Control the pointer or trigger actions like tapping on something or taking screenshots using head or facial movements like blinking, smiling, or raising eyebrows.

To enable Head Tracking:

  1. Go to Accessibility → Head Tracking.
  2. Toggle on Head Tracking.
  3. Customize gestures for specific actions.

11. Back Tap and Side Button Shortcuts

Perform actions by tapping the back of your iPhone or pressing the side button three times.

Steps to set up Back Tap and Side Button shortcuts:

  • Back Tap:
    1. Settings → Accessibility → Touch → Back Tap

    2. Now, Select Double Tap or Triple Tap and assign an action.
  • Side Button: Settings → Accessibility → Side Button → Customize click speed or long-press behavior.

12. Tap to Wake and Haptic Feedback

Like the raise to wake feature on iPhone, you can also configure your device to turn on the screen light whenever you tap it. Vibration keeps your iPhone in vibration mode even when the screen is off. So, at least, you can get emergency alerts even when you’re not actively using them.

To activate these features:

  1. Go to Settings.
  2. In the Accessibility menu, select Touch.
  3. Toggle on the Tap to Wake and Vibration options.

13. Voice Control

Perhaps another lazy feature that the iPhone has added to our lives. Use voice commands for hands-free navigation, dictation, or app control. iOS 26 improves dictation accuracy and spelling support.

Setup Voice Control on your iPhone:

  1. From Accessibility settings, select Voice Control and toggle it on.
  2. Follow setup for personalized commands.

iPhone Accessibility Features for Hearing and Sound Disabilities

iOS 26 enhances audio accessibility for people with hearing challenges.

14. Sound & Name Recognition

Get alerts for specific sounds like alarms, sirens, or crying babies. In iOS 26, you can also train your iPhone to recognize names so you can get alerts when those name
is being called.

To activate Sound Recognition:

  1. Scroll down the Accessibility menu, tap Sound & Name Recognition.
  2. Select and toggle on Sound Recognition.
  3. Tap Sounds to choose which alerts to activate.
  4. Next, tap Name Recognition and set it up.

15. Music Haptics

Music Haptics is an immersive feature that enhances your music streaming experience by providing tactile feedback that syncs with the type of music playing on your iPhone. In iOS 26, it lets you sync haptics with vocals or full songs, and adjust intensity and textures.

To enable it, go to Settings → Accessibility → Music Haptics and turn it on.

16. Audio/Visual Settings

Adjust sound balance, reduce background noise, and receive headphone notifications. iOS 26 adds audio equalizer presets like Comfort and Focus.

To adjust this setting:

  1. Access Accessibility → Audio/Visual.
  2. To play sounds from the left and right speakers, toggle on Mono Audio.
  3. To reduce background noise while making calls, toggle on Phone Noise Cancellation.
  4. Toggle on Headphone Notifications to spin up a warning when the earpiece becomes too loud.
  5. Choose equalizer presets to enhance clarity.

17. Pair Hearing Aids

If you use made-for iPhone hearing aids, you can pair them with your iPhone from the Accessibility menu. When you do so, you can improve sound quality on your iPhone while listening to podcasts, music, or making calls.

To pair a hearing aid on an iPhone:

  1. Open Settings → Accessibility.
  2. Scroll down and select Hearing Devices.
  3. Select your hearing aid device from the result.
  4. Now, go back and toggle on Hearing Aid Compatibility.

Also read: How to Use AirPods Pro 2 as Hearing Aids

18. Personal Voice

Personal Voice allows users to create a synthesized version of their own voice. This is particularly useful for people who may lose the ability to speak due to medical conditions, ensuring their digital voice sounds natural and personal.

  1. In Accessibility settings, select Personal Voice.
  2. Tap Set Up Personal Voice.
  3. Follow the prompts to record a series of phrases. iOS will generate a synthetic voice that mimics your natural speech.
  4. Once complete, your Personal Voice can be used with Text-to-Speech, Voice Control, or messaging apps that support speech synthesis.

19. Live Listen with Live Captions

Live Listen amplifies audio from your surroundings through your AirPods or compatible hearing aids. Combined with Live Captions in iOS 26, you can see real-time transcription of conversations, making communication easier for users with hearing difficulties.

To set it up:

  1. Enable Live Listen: Settings → Accessibility → Hearing Devices → Select your AirPods or hearing aid → Toggle Live Listen on.
  2. Enable Live Captions: Settings → Accessibility → Live Captions → Toggle on.
  3. Open Control Center, tap the hearing icon, and select Start Live Listen.
  4. Conversations will be amplified and transcribed on-screen in real time. You can also adjust caption text size and style in the Live Captions settings.

20. Subtitles & Captioning

iOS 26 provides more control over subtitles and captions, improving readability for videos, streaming content, or live events. You can customize font, size, background color, and even apply transparency adjustments.

  1. Navigate to Accessibility → Subtitles & Captioning.
  2. Toggle Closed Captions + SDH on.
  3. Tap Style to customize it.
  4. Changes apply system-wide, including videos in apps like Apple TV, YouTube, or streaming platforms that support captions.

Advanced Accessibility Tools

These features enhance overall usability, privacy, and multitasking.

21. Guided Access

For an added layer of privacy, you can lock your iPhone to a single app when you don’t want others (your kids, for instance) to access other parts of your phone when they’re using a particular feature.

  1. From Accessibility, tap Guided Access and toggle it on.
  2. Triple-click the side button to start a session in any app.

Once activated, all you need to do when your kid is inside an app is freeze your device with your passcode. Want to know more? Here’s a guide on how to use guided access on iPhone and Pad.

22. Share Accessibility Settings

Temporarily share your accessibility setup with another device, useful when lending your iPhone.

To transfer the settings:

  1. Scroll down the Accessibility settings and select Share Accessibility Settings.
  2. Tap Share Accessibility Settings and hold your iPhone’s head near another one.
  3. Follow the steps to share.

23. Per-App Accessibility Settings

If you want visual adjustments only in certain apps rather than across the entire UI, the Per-App Settings in Accessibility can help. This feature allows you to individually customize settings like Bold Text, Increase Contrast, and more on a per-app basis.

  1. Go to Accessibility → Per-App Settings → Add App.
  2. Select an app and adjust options like Bold Text, Reduce Motion, or Increase Contrast.

24. Accessibility Shortcut

Accessibility shortcuts let you access commonly used gestures whenever you press the side button thrice. To activate:

  1. Open Settings → Accessibility.
  2. Scroll down and select Accessibility Shortcut.
  3. Select an option from the list to activate it when you hit the side button thrice.

    Note: When you select many options at a time, the selected options appear in a list when you press the side button thrice. You can then pick one to activate it.

25. Assistive Access

Assistive Access offers a simplified iPhone experience with large buttons, clear text, and streamlined apps. It’s made for users with cognitive challenges, seniors, or anyone who prefers a clutter-free interface.

To use Assistive Access on iPhone:

  1. From Accessibility settings, select Assistive Access.
  2. Tap Set Up Assistive Access.
  3. Choose which apps to include (Phone, Messages, Camera, Music, etc.) and select your preferred layout between Grid or List.

Once enabled, the iPhone switches to a clean, easy-to-use layout focused on just what matters most.

Wrapping Up

Accessibility in iOS 26 is smarter, more intuitive, and more inclusive than ever. From visual enhancements to hearing improvements and hands-free control, Apple continues to make the iPhone a device anyone can enjoy.

Take a few minutes to explore these features, and let me know which ones made your daily usage more enjoyable!

Read more:

  • How to use Point and Speak on your iPhone and iPad
  • How to use Accessibility Shortcut on Apple Watch
  • How to use RTT or TTY on iPhone

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

acceptedAnswer.text: If 2FA isn't working, ensure you're entering the correct code within the specific time limit. To log in, you must be connected to the internet. If your device is acting up, restart it and try again. You may also use a recovery code if you have one saved. To contact Facebook Support, select Need another way to authenticate? On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I turn off two-factor authentication on Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, you can turn off Facebook two-factor authentication at any time if you no longer want to use it. Navigate to Settings & privacy, select Settings, and access Accounts Center. Now, select Password and security and choose Use two-factor authentication. Select your account and enter your password. Next, choose the authentication method and toggle it off. However, you can't turn off two-factor authentication if you have enabled Advanced Protection for Facebook.

mainEntity.name: Why can't I set up iCloud Tabs in Safari?

acceptedAnswer.text: You must have enough free iCloud storage available so Safari can sync its data. If not, you won't be able to set up iCloud tabs.

mainEntity.name: Does iCloud back up Safari tabs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Once you set up Safari for iCloud, all your Safari data, including active tabs, bookmarks, and reading lists, is stored in iCloud and can be accessed via your other Apple devices.

mainEntity.name: What to do if iCloud tabs are not syncing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ensure you have enough iCloud space and that all your Apple devices are signed in with the same Apple ID. You can also try to toggle the feature on and off.

mainEntity.name: Can I use the Personal Hotspot while my iPhone is connected to another Wi-Fi network?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, you can't. To use your iPhone as a hotspot, it needs to be connected to cellular data instead of Wi-Fi.

mainEntity.name: Will using Personal Hotspot affect my iPhone's battery life?

title.rendered: How to Password Protect a Folder on Mac

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Why protect folders on macOS: Locking sensitive folders prevents snooping on shared Macs, keeps work and personal files private, and limits unwanted sharing through sync.
  • Disk Utility method: Create an encrypted disk image of your folder, choose a password you remember, then mount, move files inside, and eject to lock.
  • Terminal ZIP encryption: Use zip with encryption to wrap a folder into a passworded archive. Quick, scriptable, and opens on macOS without installing extra apps.
  • Third-party apps on Mac: If Terminal feels tedious, apps like Encrypto, Hider Pro, or Privaulty offer simple interfaces for locking folders securely with encryption.
  • Hiding folders vs encryption: chflags hidden only hides items from Finder. Anyone can reveal them. For stronger protection on macOS, encrypt and avoid weak passwords.

Having your important folders password-locked ensures your private and sensitive files are secured from unauthorized access if you often share your Mac with others. But unlike Windows, macOS doesn’t offer a direct “password-protect folder” option. However, a few workarounds that use the built-in Disk Utility and Terminal to protect any folder with a password do exist.  
 
This post details multiple methods to password-protect a folder on your Mac.

Table of Contents
  • Why Password-Protect a Folder on Mac
  • 3 Ways to Password-Protect a Folder on Your Mac
    • 1. Using Disk Utility
    • 2. Create a Password-Protected ZIP File via Terminal Window
    • 3. Using Third-Party Apps
  • Alternative Solution: Hide Sensitive Folder on Mac
  • Tips for Managing Password-Protected Folders
  • Secure Your Files the Right Way…

Why Password-Protect a Folder on Mac 

Privacy, confidentiality, and security are typically the three main reasons to password-protect folders on a Mac: 

  • Privacy: Keep personal files safe from others using your Mac. 
  • Confidentiality: Protect work documents, financial records, or client files. 
  • Security: Prevent unauthorized access in case your Mac is lost or stolen.

3 Ways to Password-Protect a Folder on Your Mac

There are three ways to password-protect a folder on your Mac: using the Disk Utility app, via the Terminal window, or through third-party apps.

1. Using Disk Utility

You can use the Disk Utility tool on your Mac to create a disk image of the folder you want to password-protect. 
 
For those unaware, a disk image is a special file (with the .dmg extension), that acts like a virtual hard drive. When you double-click to open it, you’re required to enter the password. Once done, it mounts on your desktop like an external drive, giving you access to its content. When you eject the drive, the files inside become invisible, and anyone attempting to open it must enter the password. 
 
With that said, here’s how you can create a disk image of a folder using Disk Utility on your Mac:

  1. Open the Disk Utility app on your Mac. You can do so by heading to Finder → Applications or using the Spotlight search.
  2. Now, click on File in the top menu bar. 
  3. Next, in the drop-down menu, select New Image → Image from Folder. 
  4. Then, select the folder you wish to create the disk image of.
  5. In the dialog box: 
    • Name your new disk image. 
    • Choose a location to save it.
    • Under Encryption, select 128-bit AES (faster) or 256-bit AES (more secure).
    • Enter and verify your password.
  6. Finally, click Save and wait for the disk image to be created.

Once the .dmg file is ready, you can delete the original folder. To access your files in the future, double-click the disk image, enter the password, and it will open like a secure drive.

Note Simply closing the disk image will create unprotected copies of the files alongside the .dmg file. To prevent this, always use the eject option to close the disk image, just as you would when removing an external drive. To do so, go to File → Eject.

2. Create a Password-Protected ZIP File via Terminal Window

If ejecting the disk image every time you close it feels like a hassle, and you’re familiar with Terminal commands, you can use the Terminal window to create a password-protected ZIP file of the folder instead. Here’s how: 

  1. Open Terminal and type the following command: zip -er ProtectedFolder.zip FolderName
  2. Before hitting the Return key, make sure: 
    • Replace ProtectedFolder.zip with your desired filename. 
    • Replace FolderName with the actual folder’s name.
  3. Once done, hit Return and enter your password.

This creates a password-protected ZIP file. You’ll need to enter the password whenever you unzip it. 
 
Now, you can either delete the original folder if you no longer need it or save it somewhere safe away from prying eyes.

3. Using Third-Party Apps

Not everyone is good at writing Terminal commands; even one wrong character can wreak havoc in the system. If you prefer a simpler interface or extra features, consider trying third-party apps like Privaulty, Hider Pro, or Encrypto.  
 
These apps make it easy to lock files and folders, but may come with a cost. Since macOS already provides Disk Utility and Terminal, many users stick with the built-in options.

Alternative Solution: Hide Sensitive Folder on Mac

If password-protecting a folder natively on Mac feels complex and you don’t wish to spend on third-party apps, another simple way to keep files out of sight is to hide the folder using Terminal. While this doesn’t provide actual security like password protection, it’s useful for keeping sensitive files away from casual snooping. Here’s how you can do it: 

  1. Open Terminal. 
  2. Type in ‘chflags hidden‘ and drop the folder you want to hide onto Terminal, and the folder path will appear next to the command.
  3. Press the Return key, and the folder will disappear from the Finder.

To view the hidden folder:

  1. Open Finder and press the Command + Shift + . (period) keyboard shortcut to toggle hidden files and folders. 
  2. The hidden folder will appear slightly faded, but you can open it normally. 
  3. Press the same keyboard shortcut to hide the folder again.

To permanently unhide the folder, simply replace the ‘chflags hidden’ command with ‘chflags unhidden‘ and hit Return.

Tips for Managing Password-Protected Folders

Now that you know how to password-protect your files and folders on a Mac, use these tips to manage them:

  • Use a strong password combining letters, numbers, and symbols.
  • Store your password safely (e.g., in iCloud Keychain or a password manager).
  • Remember that if you forget the password, you may lose access permanently.
  • Always delete the original folder after securing it.

Secure Your Files the Right Way…

And that’s it; now you know how easy it is to password-protect a folder on a Mac once you know which tool to use and how. Disk Utility is the most secure option, while Terminal offers a quick solution for creating encrypted ZIP files. For a user-friendly experience, consider opting for third-party apps.

Which method do you prefer for securing your folders on Mac? Let us know in the comments.

FAQs

Can I lock a folder in macOS without third-party software?

Yes. macOS includes built-in tools like Disk Utility and Terminal that let you create encrypted disk images or compress folders without relying on third-party apps. Disk Utility is the most secure option for password protecting a folder.

Is it possible to decrypt a locked folder if I forget the password?

No. If you lose or forget the password for an encrypted disk image, there’s no built-in way to recover it. Apple doesn’t provide a password reset option for encrypted folders, so it’s important to store your password securely (e.g., in the Password app).

How to increase the size of an encrypted disk image container?

You can create a new larger disk image and transfer the contents of the old one to it. Currently, macOS doesn’t allow direct resizing of encrypted disk images. When creating the new image, select a larger size to give yourself room for future files.

Which encryption option (128 vs 256 AES) is best on Mac?

Both are secure. 128-bit AES encryption is faster and sufficient for most users. 256-bit AES encryption provides a higher security level but may slightly reduce performance. If you’re protecting highly sensitive data, 256-bit is the better choice.

Can someone else open my encrypted folder on another Mac?

Yes, as long as they have the .dmg file and know the correct password, they can open the encrypted folder on any Mac. macOS handles the decryption process natively, so no additional software is required.

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: Can I lock a folder in macOS without third-party software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. macOS includes built-in tools like Disk Utility and Terminal that let you create encrypted disk images or compress folders without relying on third-party apps. Disk Utility is the most secure option for password protecting a folder.

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to decrypt a locked folder if I forget the password?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If you lose or forget the password for an encrypted disk image, there’s no built-in way to recover it. Apple doesn’t provide a password reset option for encrypted folders, so it’s important to store your password securely (e.g., in the Password app).

mainEntity.name: How to increase the size of an encrypted disk image container?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can create a new larger disk image and transfer the contents of the old one to it. Currently, macOS doesn’t allow direct resizing of encrypted disk images. When creating the new image, select a larger size to give yourself room for future files.

mainEntity.name: Which encryption option (128 vs 256 AES) is best on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are secure. 128-bit AES encryption is faster and sufficient for most users. 256-bit AES encryption provides a higher security level but may slightly reduce performance. If you’re protecting highly sensitive data, 256-bit is the better choice.

mainEntity.name: Can someone else open my encrypted folder on another Mac?

blockGraphs.answer: You can create a new larger disk image and transfer the contents of the old one to it. Currently, macOS doesn’t allow direct resizing of encrypted disk images. When creating the new image, select a larger size to give yourself room for future files.

blockGraphs.question: Which encryption option (128 vs 256 AES) is best on Mac?
blockGraphs.answer: Both are secure. 128-bit AES encryption is faster and sufficient for most users. 256-bit AES encryption provides a higher security level but may slightly reduce performance. If you’re protecting highly sensitive data, 256-bit is the better choice.

blockGraphs.question: Can someone else open my encrypted folder on another Mac?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, as long as they have the .dmg file and know the correct password, they can open the encrypted folder on any Mac. macOS handles the decryption process natively, so no additional software is required.

keyPoints.title: Why Password-Protect a Folder on Mac
keyPoints.explanation: Protecting folders on Mac ensures privacy, confidentiality, and security of sensitive files from unauthorized access.

keyPoints.title: Method 1: Using Disk Utility
keyPoints.explanation: Create a password-protected disk image (.dmg file) that acts like a virtual hard drive, requiring a password to open or eject, safeguarding your files.

keyPoints.title: Method 2: Creating Encrypted ZIP Files with Terminal
keyPoints.explanation: Use Terminal commands to generate a password-protected ZIP file of your folder, providing quick encryption without third-party apps.

keyPoints.title: Method 3: Using Third-Party Apps
keyPoints.explanation: Employ user-friendly third-party apps like Privaulty, Hider Pro, or Encrypto for easier folder locking, especially if you're uncomfortable with Terminal commands.

keyPoints.title: Alternative: Hiding Sensitive Folders
keyPoints.explanation: Hide folders via Terminal using 'chflags hidden', which doesn't encrypt but keeps files out of casual sight, requiring a keyboard shortcut to view.

title.rendered: Buddy Passes on Snapchat? Everything You Need to Know

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Snapchat Buddy Pass gives friends free access: Snapchat+ subscribers can gift friends a 7-day free trial to explore premium features without paying.
  • Three passes per billing cycle: Each Snapchat+ member gets three Buddy Passes monthly, and unused ones expire when the cycle ends.
  • Full access to premium perks: Friends who redeem a Buddy Pass can use custom icons, BFF pins, Story rewatch counts, and early-access tools.
  • Designed to boost organic growth: Snapchat created Buddy Pass to encourage word-of-mouth sharing and turn subscribers into natural promoters.

Snapchat Plus, the app’s premium subscription, started out with just a few exclusive perks but has now grown into a feature-packed experience with over 30 premium benefits. Still, many subscribers find themselves having to explain, “What’s so special about it?” when trying to convince friends to join Snapchat Plus.

That’s exactly why Snapchat rolled out Buddy Passes. This feature lets Snapchat+ subscribers hand out free trials of Snapchat Plus to their friends, giving them a firsthand look at the premium experience before deciding to subscribe.

Here’s everything you need to know about Snapchat Buddy Passes, how they work, and why Snapchat decided to introduce them.

Table of Contents
  • What is a Buddy Pass on Snapchat?
  • How to Send a Buddy Pass on Snapchat
  • What Your Friends Get When They Claim a Buddy Pass
  • Why Snapchat Introduced Buddy Passes
  • Sharing Premium Fun Made Simple

What is a Buddy Pass on Snapchat?

Exclusive to Snapchat Plus subscribers, a Buddy Pass lets you gift your friends a 7-day free trial of Snapchat Plus. Think of it like sending a VIP invite, you’re giving your friend access to premium Snapchat features for a full week without any cost.

Each Snapchat+ subscriber receives 3 Buddy Passes at the start of every billing cycle: on the first day of the month if you’re on an annual plan or the first day of your billing cycle if you’re on a monthly plan.

You can send these passes to anyone who isn’t already using Snapchat Plus. Once your friend accepts the invite, they instantly unlock Snapchat+ features for seven days.

Keep in mind, unused Buddy Passes don’t roll over to the next billing cycle. If you don’t use them before the cycle ends, they simply expire, so don’t let them go to waste.

How to Send a Buddy Pass on Snapchat

Sending a Buddy Pass is quick and easy. Here’s how you can do it right from your Snapchat app:

  1. Open Snapchat and tap your Bitmoji in the top left corner.
  2. Here, tap the Snapchat+ banner.
  3. Next, tap the Buddy Passes banner at the top.
  4. Now, tap the Send Buddy Passes button.
  5. Select the friend who doesn’t have Snapchat+.
  6. Tap the Send button, and your friend will receive a link to start their free trial. Repeat the process to hand out the remaining available Buddy Passes.

Snapchat will also notify you when your friend redeems their Buddy Pass, so you’ll know exactly who’s trying out Snapchat+ through your invite.

What Your Friends Get When They Claim a Buddy Pass

Once your friend redeems your Buddy Pass, they’ll instantly gain access to the full Snapchat Plus suite of features for seven days. This includes:

  • Custom app icons and themes to personalize their Snapchat look.
  • The Best Friends Forever (BFF) pin to mark their top friend.
  • Story rewatch counts to see who’s rewatching their Stories.
  • Snapchat Planets, showing their place in your friendship solar system.
  • Story view notifications for selected friends.
  • Early access to new and experimental features.

It’s a complete Snapchat+ experience, just like a paid subscriber gets.

Why Snapchat Introduced Buddy Passes

The Buddy Pass program isn’t just a giveaway, it’s a clever growth strategy. Instead of relying on ads or pop-ups, Snapchat turned its loyal subscribers into ambassadors who promote Snapchat Plus through personal recommendations.

Here’s why this approach works so well:

  • Friends trust recommendations from people they know more than from ads.
  • Free trials eliminate the risk of paying for something you haven’t tried.
  • Engaged users are more likely to convert into paying subscribers after testing premium features.

By empowering users to share their subscription benefits, Snapchat is fostering a more social and organic way to expand its premium user base.

Sharing Premium Fun Made Simple

Snapchat’s Buddy Pass turns premium sharing into a social experience. Instead of just telling your friends what Snapchat+ can do, you can show them. It’s an easy, fun, and personal way to help them discover what they’ve been missing out on.

So, if you’re a Snapchat+ subscriber, make sure those Buddy Passes don’t go unused. Share them with your closest friends and let them experience the upgraded Snapchat world firsthand.

Have you tried a Buddy Pass yet? Share your experience in the comments below, it might just inspire someone else to give Snapchat Plus a try.

  • Snapchat Home Safe: Let Friends Know You’re Home Safely
  • What Does the Green Dot Mean on Snapchat? The Hidden Truth
  • How to Add Music to Your Snapchat Story
  • Snapchat Memories Storage Plans: What You Need to Know!

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

title.rendered: How to Change Date and Time on Your iPhone in Just a Few Steps

content.rendered:
Key Takeaways:

  • Manual date and time setup: You can disable Set Automatically in Settings to manually choose your preferred time zone on your iPhone.
  • Automatic time zone adjustment: Turning on Location Services lets your iPhone update the time zone automatically when you travel.
  • Grayed-out option causes: The Set Automatically toggle may be restricted by Screen Time, carrier settings, or device management profiles.
  • Why accuracy matters: Keeping the correct date and time helps apps, alarms, and calendar events sync properly without glitches.

Having the right date and time on your iPhone isn’t just about knowing what hour it is. It’s what keeps everything on your device running smoothly. From your Calendar events to Reminders and even email syncing, accurate time settings make sure nothing slips through the cracks. Usually, your iPhone handles this automatically by detecting your current location and adjusting for daylight saving time.

But if you’ve noticed your clock showing the wrong time or date, don’t worry. I’ve got you covered. In this guide, I’ll walk you through how to manually or automatically change the date and time on your iPhone so it stays perfectly in sync wherever you are.

Table of Contents
  • How to Change the Time on Your iPhone or iPad Manually
  • How to Change the Time Zone on Your iPhone Automatically
  • Why You Can't Change the Time Settings on Your iPhone

How to Change the Time on Your iPhone or iPad Manually

By default, your iPhone configures the time zone when you set up the device for the first time. But if you prefer setting it yourself, here’s what you need to do:

  1. Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
  2. Go to General → Date & Time.
  3. Turn off Set Automatically.
  4. Tap Time Zone and select your preferred city.
  5. Adjust the date and time manually at the bottom of the screen.
Note The 24-hour time option isn’t available in all regions.

If the Set Automatically toggle is grayed out, it could be due to certain restrictions or settings, which I’ll explain later in this article.

How to Change the Time Zone on Your iPhone Automatically

If you travel frequently and don’t want to keep changing the time manually, you can allow your iPhone to update it automatically based on your current location. Here’s how:

  1. Open the Settings app.
  2. Tap Privacy & Security.
  3. Select Location Services and make sure it’s turned on.
  4. Scroll down and tap System Services.
  5. Turn on Setting Time Zone.
  6. Go back to Settings → General → Date & Time.
  7. Toggle on Set Automatically and make sure your iPhone has an active internet connection.

If you see a message saying “Updated time zone information available,” restart your iPhone to apply the changes.

Pro tip

Once you’ve updated your time and date settings, you can now change the font color and style of the clock on your Lock Screen. Follow our detailed guide to learn how to customize your iPhone Lock Screen.

Why You Can’t Change the Time Settings on Your iPhone

If you find that the Set Automatically option is dimmed or disabled, it could be due to one of the following reasons:

  1. Screen Time Restrictions: Screen Time prevents users from changing the clock to bypass app limits. To fix this, disable Screen Time or wait for the restriction period to end.
  2. Carrier Settings: Some network providers control automatic time updates. You can try updating your carrier settings or contacting your service provider for assistance.
  3. Location Services Disabled: Make sure Location Services are enabled, as your iPhone uses them to determine your time zone.
  4. Device Management Policies: If your iPhone was issued by your workplace or school, the administrator might have restricted the ability to change the date and time.
  5. Regional Availability: In certain countries, automatic time setting might not be supported.

Final Thoughts

Having the correct date and time on your iPhone ensures your alarms, reminders, and calendar events work properly. Hopefully, this guide helped you fix any issues with incorrect time or time zone on your device.

If you’re still facing trouble, drop your question in the comments below. I’ll do my best to help you out.

Read more:

  • How to change the snooze time on your iPhone
  • How to keep your iPhone screen on for a longer time
  • How to set timer on iPhone camera to take hands-free photos

mainEntity.name: Why am I not getting my authentication code from Facebook?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sometimes, it takes a while to receive an SMS code. Therefore, always check back constantly. If you do not receive your verification code from Facebook, ensure that your phone number is set correctly in your profile settings. Go to the Use two-factor authentication section, select SMS or WhatsApp, and check the last two digits of your phone number. If you can't recognize it, select Change phone number, enter your number, and verify it. You can also try requesting a new code or using a backup method, such as an authentication app or recovery codes.

mainEntity.name: What should I do if two-factor authentication isn't working?

On the login page, select Other Options, then click Get more help.

mainEntity.name: Can I lock a folder in macOS without third-party software?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. macOS includes built-in tools like Disk Utility and Terminal that let you create encrypted disk images or compress folders without relying on third-party apps. Disk Utility is the most secure option for password protecting a folder.

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to decrypt a locked folder if I forget the password?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. If you lose or forget the password for an encrypted disk image, there’s no built-in way to recover it. Apple doesn’t provide a password reset option for encrypted folders, so it’s important to store your password securely (e.g., in the Password app).

mainEntity.name: How to increase the size of an encrypted disk image container?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can create a new larger disk image and transfer the contents of the old one to it. Currently, macOS doesn’t allow direct resizing of encrypted disk images. When creating the new image, select a larger size to give yourself room for future files.

mainEntity.name: Which encryption option (128 vs 256 AES) is best on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both are secure. 128-bit AES encryption is faster and sufficient for most users. 256-bit AES encryption provides a higher security level but may slightly reduce performance. If you’re protecting highly sensitive data, 256-bit is the better choice.

mainEntity.name: Can someone else open my encrypted folder on another Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, as long as they have the .dmg file and know the correct password, they can open the encrypted folder on any Mac. macOS handles the decryption process natively, so no additional software is required.

@graph.name: How to change the time on your iPhone or iPad manually
@graph.description: Learn how to manually set the date and time on your iPhone or iPad when automatic time settings aren't suitable.

step.name: Open Date & Time settings
step.text: Launch the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad, then go to General and tap on Date & Time.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone or iPad.
Navigate to General, then tap on Date & Time.

step.name: Manually set time and date
step.text: Toggle off 'Set Automatically' and manually select the time zone, date, and time as needed.

itemListElement.text: Turn off the 'Set Automatically' option.
Tap on Time Zone and select your preferred city.
Set the correct date and time at the bottom of the screen.

@graph.name: How to change the Time Zone on your iPhone automatically
@graph.description: Easily adjust your iPhone's time zone settings to update automatically using location services. This ensures your device always shows the correct local time.

step.name: Enable Location Services
step.text: Open the Settings app, go to Privacy & Security, then tap Location Services and turn it on.

itemListElement.text: Open the Settings app on your iPhone.
Tap Privacy & Security.
Select Location Services and toggle it on.

step.name: Allow system time zone updates
step.text: Scroll down to System Services and make sure Setting Time Zone is turned on.

itemListElement.text: Scroll down and tap System Services.
Toggle on Setting Time Zone.

step.name: Set the time zone to update automatically
step.text: Go back to Settings, tap General → Date & Time, and turn on Set Automatically. Make sure your iPhone is connected to the internet.

itemListElement.text: Return to the main Settings screen.
Tap General, then Date & Time.
Toggle on Set Automatically.
Ensure your iPhone is connected to the internet.

step.name: Restart if prompted
step.text: If your iPhone shows a message about updated time zone information, restart your device to apply the changes.

itemListElement.text: Restart your device if you see a pop-up saying updated time zone information is available.

keyPoints.title: Importance of Accurate iPhone Time
keyPoints.explanation: Having the correct time on your iPhone is crucial for smooth operation and syncing with time-sensitive apps, as it automatically adjusts based on location and daylight saving changes.

keyPoints.title: Manually Changing Time Settings
keyPoints.explanation: You can manually set the date and time by disabling 'Set Automatically' in the Settings app under General > Date & Time, then adjusting the date, time, and time zone.

keyPoints.title: Automatic Time Zone Adjustment
keyPoints.explanation: Enable 'Location Services' and 'Set Time Zone Automatically' in Settings to let your iPhone detect your current location and update the time zone automatically, which is helpful when traveling.

keyPoints.title: Common Reasons for Time Setting Issues
keyPoints.explanation: Problems with changing time settings can arise from Screen Time restrictions, carrier support issues, disabled Location Services, device management policies, or regional unavailability.

keyPoints.title: Ensuring Correct Time for Your iPhone
keyPoints.explanation: Having the accurate time on your device is essential for receiving alerts, reminders, and alarms, and understanding how to troubleshoot common time-setting issues helps maintain this accuracy.
